pages.title: Principles of building the Goblin documentation
pages.summary_html:
The Goblin documentation describes the target architecture of the system and sets a common guideline for its development.

This memorandum is the preamble to the future documentation. It records the main goals of Goblin and defines the purpose of the documentation, its structure, its language and the principles of linking materials together.
pages.body_html: The memorandum records the requirements for the documentation. The detailed content of the other sections will be defined later.

pages.title: 1. Main goals and tasks of the Goblin system
pages.summary_html:
The main task of Goblin is to have agents carry out a project by a flowchart prepared by a person. The scheme sets the stages of work and the links between them, and the specs explain what must be done at each stage. Such execution is called a run.

The second task is the visual presentation of a project. Goblin can be used as a standalone editor of interactive diagrams without starting any agents. Additional functions of the system will be described later.
pages.body_html:
Runs: agents carrying out a project

The main goal of Goblin is to organize the execution of a project by a flowchart drawn by a person. The person describes the stages of work, links them together and sets a spec for each block. Then they start one or several agents, who carry out the tasks according to the scheme.

Such execution is called a run. This is the central idea of Goblin: to turn a visual project plan into a sequence of real agent actions.

Visual editor: presenting a project as schemes

The second main task of Goblin is to help a person see the stages of a project and the links between them. For this, the system provides a visual editor of flowcharts and interactive diagrams.

This is a standalone way to use Goblin: a person can create and study visual schemes without starting a run and without agents carrying out tasks.

Additional functions

Goblin also has additional, secondary tasks. Their purpose and place in the system will be described as the requirements are refined further.

Related topics: [[memorandum-structure|4. Five main sections]].

pages.title: 2. Purpose of the documentation
pages.summary_html:
The documentation sets the target architecture of Goblin: how the system should be built and how its parts should interact. It serves as a common plan by which people and agents develop the project.

This plan also includes features that are yet to be implemented. So the text must make clear where the desired structure of the system is described and where its current state is described.
pages.body_html:
The documentation must become the main architecture document of the Goblin project: it explains how the system should be built, how its parts should interact and by what rules its functionality should be developed.

Its basis is the target model of Goblin. It covers both the existing features and the solutions provided by the architecture that are yet to be implemented. The current state of the project may differ from this model.

The documentation must express precisely the structure of the system that we aim for. Describing a target behavior does not in itself mean that it is already implemented. Where the current state is meant, this must be clear from the text.

Main principle: the documentation sets the general plan of Goblin, against which people and agents check their decisions when developing the system.

Related topics: [[memorandum-agents|8. Guide for agents]]; [[memorandum-structure|4. Five main sections]].

pages.title: 3. Language and order of presentation
pages.summary_html:
The memorandum and the documentation follow one principle: title, summary, detailed content. The short part consists of two or three connected paragraphs and gives a clear idea of the main point; the detailed part covers the topic fully.

The text must lead the reader step by step from the general meaning to the details. For this, it uses simple language, uniform terms and explicit explanations of the links between concepts.
pages.body_html:
The documentation is written by a person for a person. The text must be clear, logical and simple, and technical accuracy must help understanding.

Every heading of the memorandum and of the documentation begins with a title. Then comes a "Summary" block of two or three paragraphs: a coherent digest that conveys the main idea and is clear on its own. After it comes a "Detailed content" block with a full explanation of the topic, the necessary details and examples.

The structure must lead the reader step by step from the general design of the system to separate objects and the details of how they work. Every section, subsection and block of text must have a clear place and purpose.

Materials of the same kind are built on one principle. Names and terms are used consistently, and the links between concepts are explained explicitly. The reader must not have to restore missing explanations on their own or guess how one object is linked to another.

Related topics: [[memorandum-object|6. One order for describing objects]].

pages.title: 4. Five main sections
pages.summary_html:
The documentation covers five directions: backend, frontend, run, admin panel and personal account, and future plans. Together they explain the internal structure of Goblin, how a person works with the system, how agents carry out tasks and the further development of the project.

Each section will have its own headings and subsections. Materials are built on a common principle and linked to each other, so that the reader can follow the work of one function through different parts of the system.
pages.body_html:
The documentation consists of five main sections. Each includes its own headings and subsections needed for a detailed description of the structure and development of Goblin.

Backend

Describes the internal architecture of the project: the organization of scripts and program modules, functions and their purpose, the order of calls, the database structure and the control of how the system works. The section explains where and how the logic of Goblin is implemented.

[[frontend|Frontend]]

Describes the interface through which a person works with Goblin: the layout of panels, headings, tabs, tools and the canvas for managing a project. The section explains what the user sees, what each element is for and how to work with it.

Run

Describes starting a prepared flowchart and its execution by agents. A run is treated as a standalone part of the system with its own concepts, rules and links to the interface and the internal architecture.

Admin panel and personal account

Describes the administrative part of the system and the user's personal account. Inside the section, the capabilities of the administrator and the capabilities of the user are covered separately.

Future plans

Describes the planned development of Goblin: new features, improvements and changes that are yet to be implemented. Plans are linked to the target architecture and to the matching materials of the other sections.

Related topics: [[memorandum-interface|5. Documentation interface]]; [[memorandum-references|7. Cross-links]].

pages.title: 5. Documentation interface
pages.summary_html:
In the documentation interface, the table of contents is on the left and the selected material is on the right. The reader goes from a section to a heading and to an object, keeping a sense of their place in the overall structure.

From the description of an object, you can go to related materials of other sections. This way the interface helps to study both a single function and its link to the rest of the system.
pages.body_html:
The interface is built around two areas: the table of contents on the left and the selected material on the right. The table of contents reflects the hierarchy of sections, headings and objects.

For example, the reader opens the "Frontend" section, then the "Tools" heading and picks the "Flowchart" object. Its description appears on the right. By the same principle, materials about tables, arrows, gateways, links and other tools are available.

From the opened material, the reader must be able to go to related descriptions in other sections. The interface must help to understand which object is being studied now and what place it takes in the overall architecture.

Related topics: [[memorandum-object|6. One order for describing objects]]; [[memorandum-references|7. Cross-links]].

pages.title: 6. One order for describing objects
pages.summary_html:
Every object is described in the same way: first the name, then a summary of two or three paragraphs, then the detailed content. The short part explains the purpose of the object and its role in Goblin.

The detailed part covers how the object works, its properties and its makeup. After it comes a separate block of technical links to descriptions of scripts, database tables and related sections. Links can also appear in the short and detailed descriptions.
pages.body_html:
A parent heading contains only a general description and general rules of work. Descriptions of separate objects and subsections are placed in their own articles. The right block does not repeat lists and overviews of subheadings: navigation through them is already in the left table of contents. Meaningful links inside the text and a separate block of technical links are kept.

The description of each object is built in one sequence:

  1. Name. A title that names the object unambiguously.
  2. Summary. Two or three connected paragraphs about what the object is, what it is for and what role it plays in the system.
  3. Detailed description. A full description of how the object works and is used, its properties, elements and technical design.
  4. Technical links. A separate block after the description: PHP scripts, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, database tables and structures, and related sections. Links to program resources and tables lead to their descriptions in the "Backend" section.

So, the material about a flowchart in the frontend must explain the object itself and its makeup, and then lead to descriptions of the scripts that process it and of the database tables where it is stored. Its link with running the flowchart is covered through jumps to the "Run" section.

Related topics: [[memorandum-references|7. Cross-links]].

pages.title: 7. Cross-links
pages.summary_html:
All five sections are united by a common system of cross-references, keywords and mentions. It lets you trace the link between what a person sees in the interface, the internal processing of data and the execution of the scheme.

Each link has its own ID and is stored in a separate links table. When opening a material, the reader sees its outgoing links and all documents that refer to it. The common map and search let you study the connections of the whole documentation.
pages.body_html:
The documentation must form one system of linked materials. This needs a common mechanism of cross-references, keywords and mentions that covers all five sections.

Articles are stored in the documentation_pages table, and links in a separate documentation_links table. Each link has its own ID, the ID of the source document and the ID of the target document. One record gives both an outgoing link for the source and an incoming link for the target.

In the text, the author marks the words that should become a link and gives the link ID: [[frontend-left-panel|flowchart description]]. Here 42 is a sample number of an existing link, and "flowchart description" is the text of the jump. PHP finds the link by its number and builds a link to the target document. The text of one link can differ in different places of the source document.

Links can appear in the short and detailed descriptions. In addition, after the text a block of technical links is shown, grouped by purpose. A link can be present only in this block, with no mention inside the text. In the links table, the resource_type field sets the group: php, html, css, javascript, database or related. Both ends of a link remain documentation articles; links to scripts and tables lead to articles about them in the backend.

On the page of a material, two lists are visible: "Outgoing links" and "Incoming links". Incoming links are computed from the same table and lead to the source documents. They do not need to be added by hand. The tree of headings stores nesting separately from the links between articles.

The link map shows documents and the directed jumps between them. Search by titles, texts and keywords helps to find a material and see its links. For agents, a machine-readable view of articles and links is available.

A link must explain the meaning of the jump. For example, from the description of the control panel the reader goes to the scripts that handle actions in this panel; from the description of an object, to how it is stored in the database or to the rules of its execution.

Keywords and mentions must help to find materials that relate to one concept, no matter which section they are in. Jumps between the frontend, the backend, the run, the accounts and future plans must reveal the links between parts of the system and their development.

Related topics: [[memorandum-format|9. Format and storage]].

pages.title: 8. Guide for agents
pages.summary_html:
For agents that develop Goblin, the documentation serves as a guide to the structure of the system. When creating or changing functionality, an agent must check its decisions against the common target architecture.

The descriptions must give enough information to understand the task, its limits and its links to other parts of the project. The single structure and the links help to find this information and use it in work.
pages.body_html:
The documentation is intended also for agents that will program Goblin: create and change scripts, modules and functionality of the system.

Any agent working on the project must check its decisions against the target architecture described in the documentation. The general idea, the rules for how objects are built and the links between parts of the system serve as a guide for implementation.

So the descriptions must be complete and unambiguous enough for an agent to understand the purpose of its task, find related materials and implement the change in line with the general plan of the project.

Related topics: [[memorandum-language|3. Language and order of presentation]]; [[memorandum-object|6. One order for describing objects]].

pages.title: 9. Format and storage
pages.summary_html:
The documentation is placed in the md_backend/документация/ folder and is presented to the reader in HTML format. Its content must be conveniently organized and linked.

The source materials are stored in a database, and PHP builds an HTML page from them. The title, the summary and the detailed content of each heading are stored separately; the common structure and the links tie the materials together.
pages.body_html:
The documentation files are placed in the md_backend/документация/ folder. The format of the final view for reading is HTML.

Each heading is stored as a separate record in the database: name, summary, detailed content, parent section and order of placement. PHP reads these records and builds a page with the table of contents on the left and the selected material on the right.

Headings have permanent addresses and keywords. A separate links table stores link identifiers, their sources and targets. PHP uses it for links inside the text, lists of incoming and outgoing links and the common map. The content of the page is taken from the database each time it is opened.

Related topics: [[memorandum-structure|4. Five main sections]].

pages.title: Frontend
pages.summary_html:
The frontend is the working interface of Goblin. Its basis is the left, top and right panels and the central canvas. Through them the user chooses a project and a folder, builds a scheme, edits objects and watches how tasks are carried out.

Skins change the look and the layout of elements while keeping the basic features of the system. This section explains the general rules of the interface. Each panel and its tools are described in its own article.
pages.body_html:
Work begins with a project and a folder. A project unites folders, agents and assets; the open folder sets the scheme the user works with. The choice of an object determines the content of the properties panel.

Changing the skin changes the presentation. Changing the mode "Canvas", "List" or "Hierarchy" changes the way of working with the same data. Details are given in the articles [[frontend-skins|"Skins"]] and [[frontend-views|"View modes"]].

The basic structure of the section was set by the owner of the project. The descriptions of actions below are supplemented from the current code; differences from the declared model are marked in the matching articles. Features that are required but not yet implemented must be marked separately.

pages.title: Top panel
pages.summary_html:
The top panel holds the general commands of Goblin. It gives access to navigation, search, the link for the agent and the indicators of current work.

The view modes, skins, color scheme and orthogonal projection are placed in separate groups. The availability of individual buttons depends on the working mode and on editing rights.
pages.body_html:
Icons come with hover hints. Active switches are highlighted. Unavailable actions are shown as inactive buttons; their availability depends on the state of the editor and the user's rights.

In the current code, the tabs of the right panel are moved to the top area if there is room for them there. The name "right panel" means the content area that they switch.

Search

The magnifier opens the search box; ⌘K (Ctrl+K) leads there too. The box closes with the magnifier, with the Esc key or with a click anywhere else; when it closes, the field is cleared. The search goes over the elements of the current folder: an element fits if its number starts with the digits typed or its title contains the text typed (case does not matter). The list has at most 12 rows, each with a number, a type icon and a title (if there is no title, the type name is shown).

A click on a row does three things in order. The found element becomes the only selected one, and the right panel switches to its properties. The search box closes. The canvas flies smoothly to the element: over 650 milliseconds the zoom and the camera position change together, slowing down toward the end, and the element ends up in the middle of the screen. The zoom is chosen so that the whole element is visible with margins: small ones are not blown up (at most 1.4), huge ones are shrunk (at least 0.2).

If another flight starts during the flight (for example, you pick another result or follow a remark in "Info"), the new flight cancels the old one. When the flight ends, the camera does not jump, it simply stays where it is, and half a second later its position is remembered for this folder. Arrows are not flown to: the canvas does not fly to an arrow, it is only selected.

The same smooth flight is used when following a link and when clicking a remark in the "Worth a look" block ([[frontend-right-properties|Properties]]).

pages.title: Skins
pages.summary_html:
A skin defines the look of the cards and the layout of the Goblin panels. It lets you adjust the presentation to the kind of work while keeping the common scheme and its data.

The choice of skin is remembered in the browser. The target principle is that the basic functions are available with any look; the current options differ in information density and layout.
pages.body_html:
SkinFeatures
WorkingName, description and service icons; the left panel in sections.
ClassicLarge titles, covers, number and MD; tabs on the left, folders as tiles.
DesignerLarge images and minimum text; tools and colors collapsed at first.
DeveloperNumbers, IDs, properties, links and spec.
leaderWorker, presence of a spec and run state.
ShowcaseLarge name and image, a reduced set of service marks.
StudioOne studio look, compact cards, tabs and tiles.

A skin changes how data looks but does not create a copy of the project. Details hidden by a skin remain available through the matching parts of the interface.

In the current code, most skin switches are dimmed outside canvas mode. For "Studio" there is an exception. This limit of the switch should be taken into account when describing availability, without confusing it with the purpose of the skin itself.

Features of working on a phone are described separately: [[frontend-skin-mobile|Mobile skin]].

pages.title: Left panel
pages.summary_html:
The left panel is for navigation and choosing the means of work. It holds the settings, projects, folders and tools with the color palette.

The presentation depends on the skin: sections can be shown at once or opened as tabs. Their purpose stays the same when the look changes.
pages.body_html:
Switching and collapsing

In "Classic" and "Studio", a section is opened by the matching tab in the top panel. Clicking the open tab again collapses the left panel. The chosen tab is remembered in the browser.

In skins that show all sections at once, each section can be collapsed by its heading. The switch to projects is above the list of folders. In "Designer", tools and colors are collapsed by default until the user chooses another state.

Link with current work

When you enter a project, the panel switches to its folders. Changing the view mode does not by itself change the chosen skin. In the current implementation of skins with sections, opening the "Run" tab on the right replaces the content of the left panel with the archive of runs.

Where a run is going, the icon of the folder and of the project in the lists turns green and "breathes" (in rows and tiles, in all skins). The lists of folders and projects with a running run come from pulse (runFolders and runProjects) once every three seconds while the browser tab is visible; a paused run also counts as running. The list of projects marks the person's projects — their own and those where they have been; a guest sees only the open project.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/engine/pulse.php, public/src/shell/topbar.js, public/src/left/projects.js, public/src/left/folders.js, public/css/chrome.css, md_backend/ru/frontend.md on 29.09.2026

pages.title: Right panel
pages.summary_html:
The right panel combines the properties of the selected object, the project agents, assets, the run and the AI assistant. The user opens the needed tab by its icon.

The content depends on the chosen section, project, folder and the selection on the scheme. The panel lets you work with details while keeping the link with the whole scheme.
pages.body_html:
The open tab is remembered in the browser. When the project changes, its content is updated. Going to another folder updates the assets and the history of the assistant's conversations.

The header with the number and type of the object belongs to the properties tab. When other tabs are opened, it is hidden. A request to show properties from the canvas switches the panel to the matching tab.

pages.title: Central canvas
pages.summary_html:
The canvas shows the scheme of the open folder. The user places elements, connects them with arrows, joins them into groups and edits them through the properties panel.

The scale and the camera position help to work both with a single object and with the whole scheme. The look of the cards depends on the skin, and the ways of navigation depend on the canvas settings.
pages.body_html:
Main actions

ActionResult
Choose a tool and point to a placeAn element of the chosen type is created on the canvas. The tool icon can also be dragged from the panel.
Click an objectThe object is selected; its data is available in the properties.
Drag the selected objectIts position changes. With snapping on, the final position is aligned to the grid.
Drag a resize handleThe size of the object changes within the limits of its type.
Drag an arrow from a portA directed link is created between valid flow elements.
Select several objectsCommon operations on the set are available, including grouping.

Navigation

With the trackpad panning setting on, a two-finger move shifts the canvas. A pinch changes the scale if it is allowed in the settings. With trackpad panning off, scrolling is used for the scale.

Space turns on moving the canvas with the mouse, if the matching setting is active. The "Show on canvas" command in the properties points the camera at the object. The grid and gesture settings are in the [[frontend-settings|settings]].

Editing

Esc clears the tool choice and the selection. Delete or Backspace removes the selected elements. Undo uses ⌘/Ctrl+Z, redo uses ⇧⌘/Ctrl+Z. Copy, paste and duplicate are available through ⌘/Ctrl+C, V and D. While typing text, these commands must not get in the way of editing the field.

In view mode, changing the scheme is limited. Run statuses are shown over the scheme and describe the execution; the scheme itself and the history of its runs remain different entities.

pages.title: Settings
pages.summary_html:
The "Settings" menu in the left panel combines the interface language, commands for working with files and the scheme catalog, the way to the account, the canvas settings window and a link to the documentation.

The commands call separate windows or the matching sections of Goblin. The display and gesture parameters, like the interface language, are saved in this browser.
pages.body_html:
ItemAction
LanguageThe "Русский" / "English" switch at the top of the menu. The choice works in this browser; the page reloads in the new language. Details are in the article [[frontend-languages|"Languages: interface and agents"]].
Scheme catalogOpens the [[frontend-new-scheme|"New scheme"]] window on the catalog tab.
Scheme builderOpens the same window on the builder tab: a survey and assembly of a scheme.
Open…Offers to import .gbl into the current project or .canvas into the current folder.
Save…Offers .gbl for the whole project; .canvas, HTML, PDF and Mermaid for the current folder.
AccountGoes to the personal account.
Canvas settingsOpens the window with the canvas parameters and three buttons: "Guide", "Leader instructions" and "Lists".
Goblin documentationOpens this documentation in a new tab.

The "Canvas settings" window

At the top of the window there are three buttons. "Guide" opens the help on working with the canvas. "Leader instructions" opens in a new tab the server instructions for the leader for the open folder, built for the team and the environment; if no folder is open, Goblin asks you to open one first. "Lists" shows the reference lists of the configuration.

Below are the canvas parameters. The grid can be shown or hidden, its step and visibility changed, and snapping of objects turned on. Two-finger moving, pinch zoom and control through the space key are set separately, as are the zoom speed, the view of assets and agents, the arrow ports and the run display delay. The reset button brings back the default values.

The run display delay keeps the visual status on screen so that the transition is noticeable. It relates to display and does not set the speed at which agents carry out work.

Folder info

The "Info" section is no longer in the "Settings" menu: it is shown in the properties of the open folder when nothing is selected on the canvas. See [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

Exporting a file through "Save…" is a separate action. Ordinary changes of elements are passed through the editor's sync mechanism.

pages.title: Projects
pages.summary_html:
The section shows the projects available to the user. A project unites folders with schemes and the resources linked to them.

One click selects a project and shows its properties. A double click opens the project and takes the user to its folders.
pages.body_html:
Selecting and opening

Selecting a project and entering it are different actions. First you can view the project properties in the right panel; a double click opens its folders. Going back to the list of projects is available from the left panel navigation.

In the row view, the number of folders is shown next to the name. In the tile view, sorting by name or date is available. The exact view is set by the skin.

Creating a project

The "New project" or "+ project" button asks for a name. After confirmation, the project is created. Canceling the input stops the action.

If the list is empty, the interface offers to go to the account. The availability of projects is set by the current user and the access rights.

pages.title: Folders
pages.summary_html:
A folder sets a separate scheme inside a project. When it is opened, the elements and links of this scheme are loaded.

Folders can be nested in each other. Depending on the skin, they are shown as a tree of rows or as tiles; the selected folder is highlighted.
pages.body_html:
Navigation

A click on a folder loads its scheme. In the row view, indents show nesting, and next to the folder the number of objects without arrows is shown. In the tile view, sorting by name and date and the switch to projects are available.

The current folder sets the context of the assets, the assistant's conversation history and the run. So going to another folder changes more than the central area.

Creating and parameters

The "New" or "+ folder" command asks for a name, creates the folder and opens it. The "▦ new scheme" button opens the [[frontend-new-scheme|"New scheme"]] window: a catalog of ready-made schemes and the builder.

When no object is selected on the canvas, the properties tab lets you work with the folder: change the name, set the run work folder and adjust the common arrow parameters. The work folder on disk and the scheme folder are related but different concepts.

pages.title: Tools
pages.summary_html:
Tools create the objects of a scheme and the links between them. The set includes block, decision, gateway, group, area, note, table, arrow and link.

The icon of an ordinary element can be chosen and then a place on the canvas pointed to, or the icon can be dragged onto the canvas. Arrows and links are created between objects. Grouping and the palette are also here.
pages.body_html:
Choosing a tool

Clicking the chosen tool again clears the choice. An arrow is created by dragging from an object's port; there is no separate button for placing an arrow in the set of ordinary elements. A link also requires pointing to two objects.

Grouping and colors

"Group" joins the selected objects into a group; "Ungroup" removes the grouping. These actions are also available through ⌘/Ctrl+G and ⇧⌘/Ctrl+G. Availability depends on the selection and on the editing mode.

A click on a color sets the color of new objects and applies it to the current selection. The palette shows the chosen color; changing the look does not change the purpose of the object.

pages.title: Functional elements
pages.summary_html:
The general commands of the top panel let you undo and redo changes, find objects and copy the link for the leader agent.

Four indicators show the activity of the participants in the work. The state of the buttons and the hints help to understand which action is available now.
pages.body_html:
Undo and redo

Undo cancels a registered editor action; Redo repeats the canceled one. A new edit clears the redo chain. The current mechanism keeps up to a hundred actions in the page memory. The editor history is not the same as the run history.

Search in the scheme

The magnifier or ⌘/Ctrl+K opens a search over the loaded elements of the current folder. The number is matched against the start of the entered string, the name by inclusion, ignoring case. The first twelve matches are shown.

Choosing a result selects the object. Esc or a click outside the window closes the search. This is a search in the scheme; search in the documentation works separately.

Link for the agent

An ordinary click copies a task link for the leader with the project and the current folder. The server builds the instructions for work from it. A click with Shift copies an ordinary canvas link for a person.

Indication

A lit dot marks activity; the hint reveals the participant and the current work. The data is updated about once every three seconds while the browser tab is visible.

In the current code, the indicators are labeled "worker", "leader", "Jev" and "assistant". In the original description, the fourth indicator was called "DeepSeek". This difference in names is kept explicitly: the assistant indicator reflects the state of its tasks.

pages.title: Color scheme and orthogonal projection
pages.summary_html:
The color scheme defines the light or dark look of the interface. The projection defines the way the scheme is shown visually on the canvas.

These settings are separate from the choice of skin. Changing the theme or the projection must not change the meaning of objects or the order of their links.
pages.body_html:
Color scheme

In the current interface, one button switches between the light and the dark theme. The choice is saved in the browser and restored the next time it is opened.

Projection

The projection button switches between the ordinary flat view and a tilted volumetric view. The button highlight shows whether the volumetric view is on. The coordinates of the scheme remain the basis for placing objects; it is their display that is transformed.

The projection is applied consistently to cards, arrows and gesture coordinates. The visual height and thickness affect the volumetric view. This mode does not determine the order in which blocks are executed.

The original description uses the name "orthogonal projection". In the code, the switch is called iso, and the calculation is done by the orthographic projection module.

pages.title: View modes
pages.summary_html:
Canvas, list and hierarchy show one scheme in different ways. The mode is chosen with a separate icon in the top panel.

The canvas is for spatial work, the list is for viewing rows and quick edits, and the hierarchy is for studying nesting. The changes apply to the shared data of the folder.
pages.body_html:
ModeUser work
[[frontend-canvas|Canvas]]Placing objects, arrows, groups and areas.
ListNumber, type, name, links, worker, spec and step state. The name can be edited in the row; the spec button opens the task.
HierarchyNesting columns; compact expansion of the selected branch or showing all levels. Selecting a row shows the properties.

The list has a filter by number, name or type. Links are shown as their own rows, including those coming from other folders.

In the hierarchy, objects can be moved between containers. For links, there are modes with no lines, only for the selected one and all lines. Thematic links are marked separately.

The full run log is an additional mode that opens from the run panel. It is not among the three main icons of the top panel.

pages.title: Properties
pages.summary_html:
Properties reveal the data of the current selection. For one object, the fields of its type are shown; for several, the available group actions.

If no object is selected, the panel can show the folder, the selected project or a greeting. So the title and the set of fields always depend on the context.
pages.body_html:
Makeup of the properties

AreaContent
Main fieldsName, description, position in containers and links.
MD / specOpening or creating the task. For a decision, it sets the criterion for choosing a branch.
Run stepState, worker, time and result or error, if the step exists.
AssetsAttachments of the supported object types.
WorkerChoosing the worker agent for a block.
Extra properties and lookObject parameters, styling and data that depend on the type.

Context and commands

For a gateway, choosing the target folder is available, for an arrow, the link parameters, for a table, its structure. Not every section is shown for every type: the makeup is set by the object registry.

The focus command shows the selected object on the canvas. For a group and an area, switching the frame view is provided. Deleting applies to the selection.

For a folder, the name, the run work folder and the arrow settings are available. When the object changes, the panel starts showing from the top; updating the same object tries to keep the input and the scroll position.

Folder properties

When nothing is selected on the canvas, the panel shows the properties of the current folder (if there is no folder, the selected project). The panel header is hidden then. The "Folder" section comes first and is open: the folder name, the run work folder (typed by hand or picked with "Browse…"), the checkbox "Give the worker the whole picture of the scheme", "Folder arrows", the buttons "‹› Folder code" and "Get the script", and "Delete the folder" with a confirmation.

Below it is the "Info" section. It used to open from the "Settings" menu ([[frontend-settings|Settings]]); it is no longer there: it lives only here and belongs to the folder itself. The section is collapsed by default, and its title carries the number of remarks from the "Worth a look" block (no number if there are none). Whether it is open or closed, the browser remembers while you work in the editor.

BlockWhat is in it
In this folderHow many elements of each type (only the types present in the folder), then "total", "with a spec" (how many have a spec) and "assets" (the sum of attachments of all elements).
In the project"project" (title and key), "revision", "next number", "folders", "agents" (in brackets, how many of them are leaders) and "runs of this folder".
Open runShown only if a run is open in the editor: its label (rN) and state, and below, how many steps are in each state.
Worth a lookShown only if there are remarks. Each remark is a button row like "⟨number⟩ title — what is wrong".

All the numbers are counted in the browser from what the editor has already loaded (the elements and steps of the open folder, the project, folders, agents, runs). The section makes no separate requests to the server and changes nothing.

"Worth a look"

There are three kinds of remarks. A block without a spec: "no spec". A block with a spec but without an agent: "no worker assigned". A block, decision or gateway that no arrow touches (neither incoming nor outgoing): "no arrows". An element without a title is shown as "untitled". The first 40 remarks are shown; the rest are folded into the line "…and N more".

A click on a row leads to the element on the canvas: it becomes the only selected one, the panel switches to its properties, and the canvas flies smoothly to it at a zoom where the whole element is visible (the same flight as in the [[frontend-top-panel|search of the top panel]]). To return to the folder properties, clear the selection.

pages.title: Agents
pages.summary_html:
This section shows the project's agents and lets you set up their cards. Agent roles are leader and worker; the assigned worker performs the block's task where cards are in effect.

The same tab is where you choose the team setup for the open folder, and, within a team, the run environment. The agent card and these settings define different things: who works and how they interact.
pages.body_html:
List and cards

Agents are shown as rows or tiles. You can sort by name, tool, date, and use in blocks. A single click selects an agent; a double click opens the card.

The card contains the name, role, CLI, model, and work parameters. The sets of values are loaded from the configuration; the list of models depends on the selected CLI.

An agent can be dragged onto a block by a special handle to assign it. Selecting several cards allows group actions, including deletion.

Team setup and run environment

Above the agent list is the "Team setup" choice for the open folder: "Leader does everything" (default), "Leader — worker", as well as "Leader — consultant — worker" and "Leader — consultant — auditor — worker" marked "later". In the "Leader does everything" setup, the leader is both the leader and the executor: the environment choice is hidden, and agent assignments to blocks have no effect. More about setups — [[run-role-models|"Roles"]].

In the other setups, "Folder run environment" appears below: "Subagents — inside the leader" (default), "Orca — separate terminals", and "SendMessage — Claude sessions". There is no "not selected" option. Both choices belong to the folder, not to the whole project: when you switch folders, the tab is redrawn.

The "Leader instruction" button in the left panel and the spec link from the top bar give an instruction built for the setup and environment of the open folder. Cards on blocks work only in Orca and SendMessage: there the worker on the card gets the step, and a block with a leader or an empty card is done by the leader itself. In subagents and in the "Leader does everything" setup a card starts nothing: the leader chooses the executor. Assignments on cards are kept when the setup or environment changes. The environment set in the folder must match the actual way agents are launched; a card by itself does not start an executor. More — [[run-environment|"Execution environment"]].

pages.title: Assets
pages.summary_html:
Assets give access to the files of the work folder and to the attachments of objects. In this tab you can view the assets of the current folder or of all folders in the project.

A file in the library and its attachment to an object are different parts of the work. The spec has its own properties section and is not mixed with ordinary attachments.
pages.body_html:
Folder and project assets

The "Folder / Project" switch sets the scope. In folder mode, the files of its work directory in/ are shown. In project mode, files are grouped by the folders that have a work directory set.

Files can be uploaded through the upload area. If no work directory is set, the interface offers to specify it in the properties or to upload a file to create it automatically. An empty list and a missing work folder are shown with different messages.

Object attachments

In the properties of a supported object, "file", "link", and "from storage" are available. The last option attaches an asset that already exists. The attachments view switches between a list and a preview.

An asset can be dragged onto a block of the matching folder. The list of work directory files and the list of attachments of the selected object show different relations; an asset can exist in the library without being attached to the current block.

pages.title: Run
pages.summary_html:
The "Run" tab shows how the scheme is executed: the overall state, steps, executors, results, and the event log.

In the current implementation, the browser observes the execution. The run is started and driven by the leader or the Goblin CLI; the interface also provides stopping and preparing the scheme for a new start.
pages.body_html:
Display

The run shows a state: running, paused, stopped, reached the end, or failed. If the system is waiting for an action, the reason for waiting is shown.

Steps are shown as separate items with a number, a state, and an executor. A click selects the matching scheme object. The counter shows the number of accepted steps. The full log opens from the event feed. The feed also shows the conversation between the leader and the server (the "conversation" filter): in an expanded reply to done you can see the "⚠" lines of the soft reply check.

Commands of the current interface

CommandBehavior
Start runOpens an explanation about launching the leader or CLI. The button does not start agents in the browser.
Stop runFor an active run, it needs a second press. It sends the immediate stop command and updates the state.
Reset scheme for runNeeds confirmation by a second press. It prepares the folder (run.prepare with files): removes the previous statuses from the canvas, removes covers and step results from the cards, clears the service files of the steps. The out/rN/ folders with the results of past runs stay; input assets are kept. If a run is active, it must be stopped first. The leader does the same reset itself on begin.

The delay of status display is set separately and affects the visualization. The full rules of execution, roles, and lifecycle will be covered in the main section [[run|"Run"]].

pages.title: AI assistant
pages.summary_html:
The AI assistant lets you discuss the scheme, ask for an explanation, find problems, and prepare changes. Conversations are tied to the folder where they were started.

Suggested changes are shown as a plan and applied by the user's button. The tab holds the conversation history; the conversation itself opens on the assistant screen.
pages.body_html:
Conversation and context

Enter sends the message, Shift+Enter adds a line. The "Folder | Project" switch above the field sets the scope of the question: the assistant sees either the open folder or the whole project. When you move to another folder, its history is loaded separately.

Available are a new conversation, history, a link to the conversation, and quick requests: explain the scheme, run a review, prepare a spec, or suggest a better layout. Under the field and next to replies, token usage is shown when the data is available.

Voice

The microphone sits next to "Ask" and works as live dictation. While it connects, the button is dimmed; when it turns red, you can speak. Words appear in the field as you talk, at the caret. A second press stops the dictation and the text stays in the field: only "Ask" or Enter sends the question. The microphone only dictates. Editing the field by hand during dictation takes priority: new words go at the caret, and erased text does not come back.

The speaker is a separate option, independent of the microphone. When it is on, the assistant reads aloud every new reply, however the question was asked (by voice or typed by hand). The speaker is off by default; the browser remembers the choice, and turning it off silences a reply that is playing. Past replies are not read when the history is opened. If the browser did not give access to the microphone, a hint shows where to allow it.

Keys never reach the browser: the server hands out a temporary token for recognition and the ready sound of the answer (voice.session, voice.speak), see [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]]; the dictation itself is [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-voice-js|panel/voice.js]]. You can set your own access to the voice models in your account, the "AI" section ([[accounts-user-ai|AI conversations and usage]]).

Link to the conversation

The chain-link button copies the link and opens it at once in a new window. This is a separate conversation page — [[backend-resource-public-chat-php|chat.php]]: all questions and answers, the assistant's train of thought and the usage. The page is drawn by [[backend-resource-public-src-shell-chatpage-js|shell/chatpage.js]]. Until the conversation has a question, there is no link — ask something first. The same page opens from the "Log" link of a conversation in your account.

Applying suggestions

While waiting, the state of the job is shown. If the result contains edits, an "Edit plan" appears with the commands "Apply" and "No, thanks". Applying updates the scheme; declining cancels the suggested job.

"Stop" ends the assistant's current job. This is a separate command from stopping a real run. An error is shown in the conversation and must not be taken as a successful change of the scheme.

Builder

The builder opens in a separate window [[frontend-new-scheme|"New scheme"]] — from the assistant's quick menu: a card survey, a draft with a minimap, and folder creation.

The assistant helps design a scheme and analyze results. Execution of specs by agents belongs to the [[run|run]].

pages.title: Backend
pages.summary_html:
The backend stores projects and executes the rules of Goblin. It accepts commands from the interface and from agents, checks permissions, changes data, and returns the result.

The same object must keep its meaning no matter who works with it: a person on the canvas, an agent through the API, or an account user.
pages.body_html:
Architectural principle

The page and the terminal utility call server operations. The rules for creating objects, moving the run, and accessing assets are concentrated in PHP modules. MariaDB stores the data, constraints, and history.

The current implementation is described from the sources and the database structure as of September 23, 2026. Requirements for a future change are marked separately; the existence of an article does not mean the feature is already implemented.

Boundary of responsibility

A change of appearance must not change the spec, the execution links, or the acceptance result. A data change goes through the operations of the matching domain. A direct write to a table bypasses part of the PHP rules and is not an equal way of working with the system.

pages.title: Run
pages.summary_html:
A run is the execution by agents of a project described by a block scheme. The person sets the stages, specs, and links, and the system hands out the allowed work, saves results, and manages transitions.

This is the central function of Goblin. Displaying the scheme remains a capability on its own: a drawn diagram does not yet mean that its specs were carried out.
pages.body_html:
Basic model

The scheme describes what must be done. A run stores a separate pass through this scheme. An attempt of a step ties a specific spec to an executor, a result, and an acceptance decision.

A transition is allowed by the rules of the graph after the intended decision. An agent's message about readiness does not replace the saved state of the step.

Architectural rule

All participants check against the current state of the server. The address of the spec, the attempt number, and the result are passed on without substitution; a repeated reply must not be taken as a new pass of the cycle. The target documentation sets this rule for further implementation.

pages.title: Admin panel and account
pages.summary_html:
This section describes working with an account and managing a Goblin installation. The capabilities of a user and of an administrator depend on their access context.

The account gathers the projects available to the person and information about the work. The admin panel is for managing data and maintaining the installation.
pages.body_html:
General rule

A page must clearly show the object of an action and its result. Going to the account does not change the rules of the subject area: scheme edits go through the intended server operations.

Sign-in to account.php and sign-in to admin.php are implemented separately. Having a user session must not be read as administrative permission.

pages.title: Future plans
pages.summary_html:
This section keeps ideas for the further development of Goblin and target requirements that are still to be implemented or clarified. It helps tie current work to the overall architecture.

A description of a future capability does not mean it is already available. For each idea, the status, the expected behavior, and the signs of readiness must be stated.
pages.body_html:
How to keep plans

An idea is worded through the task of a person or an agent. Then the desired behavior, the affected entities, and the criterion by which the work can be considered finished are described. Deadlines and commitments are added only after a separate decision.

Statuses

"Requirement" marks an agreed principle of the target system. "Proposal" is a possible development that needs a separate assessment. "Implemented" is allowed after the work is done, and confirming the result should be told apart from the fact of a code change.

Below, in separate articles, proposals are worded on the basis of the current design. Including them in the documentation does not mean the implementation is already done or assigned to a certain date.

Run optimization

[[future-run-optimization|Two HTML assets: a comparison of schemes with adjustments, and the auditor's proposals]].

pages.title: Block
pages.summary_html:
A block represents a stage of work. It contains a name, a description, a spec, and the assigned worker.

During a run, the block's spec is passed to the executor. In the frontend, a block is shown as a card whose content depends on the skin.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

After creating it, select the block and fill in the name and description in the properties. In the "MD / spec" section, write the requirements for the work and the result; in the executor field, choose a worker agent. Assets and topic links can be attached to the block.

Links and limits

A block can be marked as the starter of a run. A folder has one starter; it is drawn as a circle, is not handed to a worker, and its spec describes the run for the leader.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Decision
pages.summary_html:
A decision marks a fork in the scheme. Its spec contains the criterion for choosing the next path.

In the properties of a decision, the name, description, spec, extra parameters, and run step information are available. The worker assignment typical for a block is absent here.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Create a decision and describe the choice condition. Connect it to the following elements with arrows; the arrows have branch labels available. The text of the condition must allow the transition to be determined without guessing.

Links and limits

Changing the color or size of a decision affects the presentation. The rules for making the decision during execution belong to the "Run" section.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

Choosing a branch by a worded condition using a meaning-based assessment is described in the article [[run-jev|Jev]]. If confidence is insufficient, the decision needs a person.

pages.title: Gateway
pages.summary_html:
A gateway marks a transition to another folder of the scheme. Its main special property is the destination folder.

On the canvas, a gateway takes part in directed links alongside a block and a decision. The destination is set in the properties.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

After placing a gateway, enter a name and choose the "Target folder" in the "The door leads to" section. Connect the gateway to the related stages with arrows.

Links and limits

A gateway connects parts of the scheme placed in different folders. The detailed rules for executing a transition will be described in the run section.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Group
pages.summary_html:
A group joins elements inside a frame with a title. It helps organize the scheme and work with a set of objects.

A group can be created with the tool or assembled from a selection. Its content, assets, and styling are available through the properties.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Select the elements and press "Assemble" or ⌘/Ctrl+G. The "Disassemble" command or ⇧⌘/Ctrl+G removes the grouping. Collapsing a group hides the content inside a compact view; repeating the action expands it.

Links and limits

A group can be an end of a topic link. Run arrows are not attached to the group's frame. In the properties, the frame can be turned into an area.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Area
pages.summary_html:
An area marks a zone or a strip of the scheme and contains elements. It helps show a meaningful or spatial division of the work.

An area is a container, like a group. Its content and styling are changed through the properties.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Create an area with the tool and place the elements that belong to it inside. In the properties, the name, description, content, spec, topic links, and view settings are available. For the area's label, a choice of position is provided.

In the properties, in the "Look" block, an area has an "Area caption" row with two pairs of icons. The first pair puts the caption on the left or on the right; the second sets the height: at the top or in the middle. By default the caption is on the left and in the middle. The choice is stored in the area's style — the fields align (left / right) and valign (top / middle) — and shows on the canvas at once. The icons have no hint text; the names "Caption at the top" and "Caption in the middle" work as their labels

Links and limits

An area can take part in topic links, but it is not an end of a run arrow. Switching the frame between "group / area" is available in the properties.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Note
pages.summary_html:
A note adds an explanatory label or line to the scheme. It is used for information the reader of the scheme needs.

A note has a name, a description, and appearance parameters. In the registry of its properties, the executor and run step sections are absent.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Select the note tool, point to a place on the canvas, and fill in the text. Its size and styling let you place the explanation next to the needed part of the scheme.

Links and limits

A note is not connected by run arrows and is not used as an end of a topic link. Its role is a visual explanation.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Table
pages.summary_html:
A table shows data in rows and columns right on the canvas. It suits matrices, lists, and comparisons.

The structure of a table is edited in the properties panel, and the cell text directly on the canvas. A table also supports assets and styling.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Place a table with the tool. In its properties, add or remove rows and columns and adjust the view. To change the text of a cell, double-click it on the canvas.

Links and limits

A table is an object of the scheme. It is not a database table and does not become an execution step just because it is placed on the canvas.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Arrow
pages.summary_html:
An arrow sets a directed transition between elements of the flow: blocks, decisions, and gateways. It stores a source and a destination.

An arrow is created by dragging from an object's port to another allowed object. Its properties define the branch and the way the line is drawn.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Drag the connection from the port of the source element to the target. In the properties, the name, branch label, line style, reverse flow direction, and port parameters are available. Ports can be chosen automatically or keep a manual attachment — depending on the settings.

Links and limits

Groups, areas, notes, and tables are not ends of a run arrow. For topic relations between supported objects, a link is used.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Link
pages.summary_html:
A link is a topic reference between objects. It can lead to another folder and helps show relations between parts of the project.

The ends of a link can be a block, a group, or an area. A link does not take part in the order of execution of a run.
pages.body_html:
Working with the object

Select the link tool and specify the source and target objects. It is created between objects, not as a separate card in an arbitrary place. An object's links are available in its properties.

Links and limits

In the list and the hierarchy, links are shown separately from flow arrows. Both the object's outgoing links and incoming ones from other folders are counted.

General placement and selection operations are described in the article [[frontend-canvas|"Central canvas"]], and the available fields in the article [[frontend-right-properties|"Properties"]].

pages.title: Files and data
pages.summary_html:
Every technical entity has its own article with a permanent address. Links from the interface lead to these articles and let you go from a user's action to its implementation.

A resource can be a table, a PHP script, or an interface file. The name and path tie the description to the source project.
pages.body_html:
Rules of description

An article explains the purpose of a resource, its inputs, result, and limits. The fields of a table or the functions of a file are described in the article of the resource itself.

Links are stored in documentation_links. That is why the reader sees both the outgoing technical links and the articles that link to the current one. Moving an article in the tree does not require changing its identifier.

pages.title: PHP scripts
pages.summary_html:
PHP ties requests to the rules of the subject area. Modules are split by purpose, and the public entry points include the needed parts of the application.

The file reference lists the declared functions, their signatures, and the explanations from the source. Technical links lead to other documentation resources.
pages.body_html:
Working with the code

The public handler checks the request and the call context. A domain function works with project objects. Helper functions convert data, read the configuration, or run database queries.

The function catalog reflects the source file as of the date of preparation. Static links show the direct calls and SQL queries found in the code; dynamic dispatch is described additionally in the API article.

pages.title: HTML markup
pages.summary_html:
HTML markup groups the interface-related resources of this type.

Each resource has a separate article, so it can be linked from the description of a panel or a tool.
pages.body_html: The contents are expanded in the left table of contents. The incoming links of a specific resource show which documentation materials link to it.

pages.title: CSS styling
pages.summary_html:
CSS styling groups the interface-related resources of this type.

Each resource has a separate article, so it can be linked from the description of a panel or a tool.
pages.body_html: The contents are expanded in the left table of contents. The incoming links of a specific resource show which documentation materials link to it.

pages.title: JavaScript modules
pages.summary_html:
JavaScript modules group the interface-related resources of this type.

Each resource has a separate article, so it can be linked from the description of a panel or a tool.
pages.body_html: The contents are expanded in the left table of contents. The incoming links of a specific resource show which documentation materials link to it.

pages.title: Database tables
pages.summary_html:
Goblin's data is stored in MariaDB. The SQL structure defines field types, uniqueness of records, foreign keys, and actions on deletion.

Each table is described separately by the actual schema. The structure snapshot contains no user rows, passwords, or token values.
pages.body_html:
How to read the structure

NULL means the absence of a value; an empty string and zero have their own meaning. DEFAULT shows the server value on insert without an explicit field. AUTO_INCREMENT issues the record identifier.

Foreign keys ensure referential integrity. CASCADE deletes the related rows, SET NULL removes the reference, RESTRICT forbids the action while a dependency exists. Application constraints are additionally enforced by PHP.

Source

The full structure was taken from the working database goblin_v2 and saved in md_backend/документация/architecture-schema.json. The articles give fields, indexes, relations, CHECK, triggers, and CREATE TABLE. The current value of the AUTO_INCREMENT counter is removed from the DDL: it belongs to the contents, not to the data model.

pages.title: Folder data — lib/folders/folders.php
pages.summary_html:
Folders: create, rename, move, delete.

The article links this file with the PHP modules and tables it calls. Its functions must be used in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Folders: create, rename, move, delete. Provides: folderRow(), folderCreate(), folderUpdate(), folderDelete(), folderRunEnv(), folderRoleScheme(), folderUsesAgentCards(), workDirFor(), workDirIn(), workDirDropIfEmpty(). Does not: does not assemble the scheme for the canvas — that is folders/scheme.php. A folder is a canvas. Folders nest inside each other; deleting takes the whole branch with it.

Beyond the list in the header the file contains folderActiveRunEnv(), folderWorkDir() (the work folder — empty or a path inside the allowed roots file_roots), folderBranch() (a folder and all its descendants), folderNoCycle() (refusal to put a folder inside itself) and two constants. RUN_ENVS — run environments (subagents, orca, sendmessage: how the leader is connected to the workers). ROLE_SCHEMES — the role hierarchy (solo, leader-worker, and also consult-worker and consult-audit-worker, marked "later": there are no instructions for them yet). The choice is stored in the folder's run_env and role_scheme columns and is set by the folder.create and folder.update operations (parameters runEnv and roleScheme). In solo there is no active environment; in a team with no choice, subagents work; agent cards on blocks work only in Orca and SendMessage.

When a folder is created, its work folder public/workfiles/<name> with an in/ subfolder is created at once (a trial batch does not touch the disk). When a branch is deleted, links across the branch boundary are deleted with tombstones (linksCutAcross), and the targets of gateways across the boundary are reset to null with a revision bump (gatesCutAcross); empty work folders are removed only after the transaction commits (dbAfterCommit), so a batch rollback does not lose them.

pages.summary_html:

The article links this file with the PHP modules and tables it calls. Its functions must be used in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Scheme elements: create, change, delete, read. Provides: elementCreate(), elementUpdate(), elementDelete(), elementRestore(), elementRow(), linkEnds(), linksCutAcross(), gatesCutAcross(), endFolders(). Does not: does not decide what goes into what (kinds.php), does not compute the membership (members.php), does not touch assets (assets/links.php). The primary data lies in columns, all the styling in a single style field. A link is stored as an arrow — from_id and to_id — but lives by its own rules: the ends are a block, group or area; the ends' folders may differ; the link's folder is always the owner's folder (from).

Beyond the list in the header — the helpers resolveAgentRef(), arrowBranch(), gatewayTarget(), colorAllowed(), styleJson(). elementRestore() is the element.restore operation: undoing a deletion under the former number. Before moving and deleting folders, they call linksCutAcross() (deletes links that have one end beyond the branch boundary, with tombstones) and gatesCutAcross() (resets the gateway target across the boundary and bumps the revision: otherwise the foreign key would do it silently and open editors would not know); endFolders() returns the folders of the given elements — for protecting a live run. There is no separate elementGet() function in the file: the element.get operation is served from elements/find.php.

pages.title: Agent storage — lib/agents/agents.php
pages.summary_html:
Project agents: who can lead a run and who can carry out steps.

The article links this file with the PHP modules and tables it calls. Its functions must be used in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Project agents: who can lead a run and who can carry out steps. Provides: agentRow(), agentList(), agentSave(), agentDelete(), agentDetach(), agentUnassign(), agentToken(), agentShape(). Does not: does not launch agents — the leader does that in its own terminal. There are exactly two roles: lead (the leader-orchestrator) and worker (the executor). The values cli, model, effort, permission, sandbox are checked against config.txt.

The article ties this file to the PHP modules and tables it calls. Its functions should be used in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Table content: one clear form and one check for it. Provides: TABLE_PROP, tableNormalize(), tableEmpty(), tableFromV1(). Does not: draw — the canvas draws (public/src/canvas/table.js). The form is deliberately simple, so that a person can read it, not only code: { "head": ["Responsible for", "Does not do"], // header: highlighted "rows": [ { "name": "Goblin", "cells": ["scheme", "does not start the CLI"] }, { "name": "Agent", "cells": ["work", "does not accept on its own"] } ] } `head` — the column labels without the first one: the first column is taken by row names. `name` — the row name, `cells` — its cells in column order. There are no merges and no nesting: a table here is a way to show rows, not a laid-out document.

Location

lib/elements/table.php. The description was prepared from the source file as of September 23, 2026.

File functions

Signatures are taken from the source. The explanations reproduce the comments next to the declaration; a missing comment is marked explicitly. The line number is a landmark in this version of the file.

A project unites folders, schemes, agents, assets and the work history.

The url_key key is used in addresses, id — in internal links. The next_no and next_run_no counters allocate numbers within a project; rev is used to synchronize changes. The lang field sets the language of the project’s agents and built-in AI.

Triggers

The snapshot has no triggers for this table.

Application rules

The url_key key is used in addresses, id — in internal links. The next_no and next_run_no counters allocate numbers within a project; rev is used to synchronize changes. The lang field sets the language of the project’s agents and built-in AI.

The project language is one for all its runs. The leader and worker read instructions in it, run tasks and the feed are written in it, and the built-in AI answers in it. Each person picks their own interface language (the goblin_lang cookie), so in one project people can have different interface languages while the agents use one. A new project gets the interface language of the person who created it; to change it, use the project.update operation with the lang field (in the editor — “Agents language” in the project settings). Only ru and en are allowed: PHP checks this (the LANGS constant), while SQL only limits the length to two characters. While a run in the project is running or paused, the language cannot be changed — the guard “change the agents’ language of a live run” stops it. More in the article [[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]]. The same language picks the version of the scheme catalog: see templates.i18n.

SQL describes the allowed storage form. Permissions, project membership, the current stage of work and the preparation of related data are checked in PHP. The sources of these rules are given in the technical links.

  `rev` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `next_no` int(10) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 10,
  `next_run_no` int(10) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `guest_write` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `ai_confirm` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `strict_checks` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(3),

  KEY `ix_projects_owner` (`owner_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_projects_owner` FOREIGN KEY (`owner_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE SET NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT=7248 DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci

pages.title: Table elements
pages.summary_html:
The elements table stores Goblin scheme objects: blocks, decisions, gateways, arrows, groups, areas, notes, tables and links. One row describes one object and ties it to a project and a folder.

This is where the main object fields, connection ends and styling live. The composition of containers, extra properties, assets and run state are stored separately. Below is the full structure of the current table: fields, indexes, foreign keys and constraints, as well as the application's handling rules.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

The id identifier is used for connections in the database. The no field is the object's number within the project: it stays clear to the user regardless of the folder. When a deleted object is restored, the application can bring back the old number by creating a row with a new ID.

This article records the existing structure, read from SHOW CREATE TABLE and the system metadata of the goblin_v2 database. Snapshot date: 2026-09-23. Changes to the target architecture should be described separately from this snapshot.

Storage parameters

ParameterValue
Tableelements
EngineInnoDB
Character setutf8mb4
String collationutf8mb4_unicode_ci
Number of columns17

Full field structure

FieldMariaDB typeNULLDefaultAutomaticPurpose
idbigint(20) unsignedNonot setauto_incrementInternal row identifier. Foreign keys refer to it. Issued by AUTO_INCREMENT.
project_idbigint(20) unsignedNonot set—The element's project. Linked to projects.id; the number no is unique within this project.
folder_idbigint(20) unsignedNonot set—The scheme folder the element belongs to. Linked to folders.id.
noint(10) unsignedNonot set—The element number the user sees. Unique within the project, across different folders; issued by the server counter projects.next_no.
typeenum('block','decision','gateway','arrow','group','area','note','table','link')Nonot set—Element type. The full list of nine values is given below.
titlevarchar(512)No''—Element name. An empty string is allowed; the field does not store NULL.
descriptiontextYesNULL—Text description. A missing value can be represented as NULL. This is not a separate MD file of the spec.
agent_idbigint(20) unsignedYesNULL—Reference to the agent card agents.id. Allowed on a block; NULL means no agent is assigned.
from_idbigint(20) unsignedYesNULL—Source of an arrow or owner of a link. Reference to elements.id.
to_idbigint(20) unsignedYesNULL—Destination of an arrow or target of a link. Reference to elements.id.
branchenum('flow','yes','no')YesNULL—Arrow branch: flow — normal transition, yes — "yes", no — "no". Must be NULL for the other types.
backtinyint(1)No0—Flag of a return arrow. The application writes 0 or 1; a value of 1 does not swap from_id and to_id.
target_folder_idbigint(20) unsignedYesNULL—Destination folder of a gateway, reference to folders.id. NULL means no target is set.
stylelongtextNo'{}'—JSON with styling and coordinates. The physical type is LONGTEXT; the database checks that the JSON is syntactically valid.
revbigint(20) unsignedNo0—Element change revision. The application writes the revision of the project operation; this is not a run step number.
created_atdatetime(3)Nocurrent_timestamp(3)—Row creation time, to millisecond precision. Set by the database by default.
updated_atdatetime(3)Nocurrent_timestamp(3)on update current_timestamp(3)Time of the last row change, to millisecond precision. Updated by the database when the record changes.

In the notations bigint(20), int(10) and tinyint(1), the number in parentheses does not set the number of allowed digits or values. TINYINT(1) by itself does not limit the field to the values 0 and 1. For VARCHAR(512) the number is the maximum length in characters, for DATETIME(3) it is the fractional-second precision.

Values of type

ValueObjectSpecial data
blockBlockMay have agent_id. A starter is also a block; the starter flag is stored in props.
decisionDecisionThe fork criterion and the outgoing branch arrows.
gatewayGatewayMay have target_folder_id.
arrowArrowfrom_id and to_id are required; branch and back are used.
groupGroupMembership is stored in members.
areaAreaMembership is stored in members.
noteNoteText fields and styling.
tableTable on the canvasThe structure of its contents is stored in extra properties.
linkLinkfrom_id and to_id are required; branch = NULL, back = 0.

Indexes

IndexColumns in orderUniqueMethodPurpose
PRIMARYidYesBTREEUnambiguous row lookup and the target of foreign keys.
uq_elements_noproject_id, noYesBTREEForbids repeating one number within one project.

ix_elements_fromfrom_idNoBTREELooking up outgoing connections and serving the source foreign key.
ix_elements_toto_idNoBTREELooking up incoming connections and serving the destination foreign key.
ix_elements_targettarget_folder_idNoBTREEFinding gateways, leader into the folder.
ix_elements_agentagent_idNoBTREEFinding the elements of an assigned agent.
