The number no is unique in a pair with the project, not with the folder. There is no unique index for the pair from_id, to_id: the ban on a repeated identical connection is implemented in PHP.

Foreign keys of elements

ConstraintFromToOn target deleteOn key change
fk_elements_agentelements.agent_idagents.idSET NULLRESTRICT
fk_elements_folderelements.folder_idfolders.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_elements_fromelements.from_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_elements_projectelements.project_idprojects.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_elements_targetelements.target_folder_idfolders.idSET NULLRESTRICT
fk_elements_toelements.to_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT

CASCADE deletes dependent rows when the parent record is deleted. So deleting a project or a folder deletes its elements, and deleting a connection end deletes the related arrows and links. SET NULL keeps the element, clearing the reference to the deleted agent or to the gateway's destination folder. RESTRICT forbids changing a key that the target uses.

Incoming foreign keys from other tables

ConstraintFromToOn target deleteOn key change
fk_links_elementasset_links.element_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_members_containermembers.container_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_members_elementmembers.element_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_props_elementprops.element_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_marks_edgerun_marks.edge_idelements.idCASCADERESTRICT
fk_steps_chosenrun_steps.chosen_edge_idelements.idSET NULLRESTRICT
fk_steps_elementrun_steps.element_idelements.idSET NULLRESTRICT
fk_steps_viarun_steps.via_edge_idelements.idSET NULLRESTRICT

When an element is deleted, the database deletes its extra properties, its membership in containers, its asset bindings and the related run_marks.edge_id records. In run_steps, references to deleted elements and arrows are set to null: the step history rows are kept. Deleting an asset binding is not in itself deleting the asset record.

The self-references elements.from_id and elements.to_id are already listed in the previous table.

CHECK constraints

CheckWhat the database guarantees
JSON_VALID(style)The style field contains syntactically valid JSON. The check does not define its set of keys and does not by itself require a JSON object.
ck_elements_arrowFor arrow and link both ends must be filled. For the other types, filling both ends at once is forbidden.
ck_elements_branchFor all types except arrow, branch must be NULL and back must be 0.
ck_elements_gatetarget_folder_id is allowed only for gateway; for the gateway itself the target may be NULL.
ck_elements_agentagent_id is allowed only for block; for the block itself the assignment may be NULL.

ck_elements_arrow has an exact boundary: for an ordinary object the check forbids two filled ends, but does not forbid one filled end. The application contract is stricter: the end fields belong only to an arrow or a link. Likewise, SQL does not check that the source and destination belong to one project or have allowed types.

Application rules

RuleWhere and how it is applied
Project membershipPHP checks the project of the folder, the agent, the connection ends and the gateway's destination folder. Foreign keys alone do not ensure that the projects match.
NumberingnextNo() increments projects.next_no and issues the number. Ordinary creation does not reuse a freed number. Restoring is a separate operation with a conflict check.
Arrow endsBlock, decision and gateway are allowed. The yes and no branches are allowed only on the output of a decision; the ordinary branch is flow.
Link endsBlock, group and area of one project are allowed, including from different folders. A link belongs to the folder of the from_id owner and cannot point to itself.
Duplicate connectionsFor the same pair of ends the application looks for an already existing arrow or link of the same type and rejects the repeat. There is no SQL UNIQUE for this pair.
Type changeAn ordinary update allows only converting group to area and back.
Active runSemantic changes of an element go through the protection of the active scheme. The set of checks is defined by the engine code; it is not a restriction of the SQL table.

Structure of style

The common styling keys include x, y, z, width, height, thick, color, locked and order. The special keys depend on the type: for example, the ports and route of an arrow, the collapsed state of a group or the kind of an area.

styleJson() overlays the sent keys on the previous ones; the value null removes the key. The color is validated by the application. For a block, decision and gateway, if z is missing, the server adds z = 1. So the SQL default {} and the result of ordinary creation through the API may differ.

The fields props, in, assets and hasSpec that appear in the JSON response are not elements columns. They are assembled from related data. Run states and results belong to run steps.

Mapping to API names

ColumnAPI field
folder_idfolder
agent_idagent
from_idfrom
to_idto
target_folder_idtarget

The response representation is assembled by lib/elements/shape.php. The full response includes styling and revision; the working view shortens the visual data. The internal SQL row and the public JSON do not match one to one.

Triggers

In the current database, no triggers are registered for elements. The automatic update time is set by the property of the updated_at column.

Full SQL definition

Below is the definition of the current table. The current AUTO_INCREMENT counter in the table options is omitted: it changes as rows are created and is not a permanent part of the structure.

CREATE TABLE `elements` (
  `id` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `project_id` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL,
  `folder_id` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL,
  `no` int(10) unsigned NOT NULL,
  `type` enum('block','decision','gateway','arrow','group','area','note','table','link') NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(512) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `description` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `agent_id` bigint(20) unsigned DEFAULT NULL,
  `from_id` bigint(20) unsigned DEFAULT NULL,
  `to_id` bigint(20) unsigned DEFAULT NULL,
  `branch` enum('flow','yes','no') DEFAULT NULL,
  `back` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `target_folder_id` bigint(20) unsigned DEFAULT NULL,
  `style` longtext NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}' CHECK (json_valid(`style`)),
  `rev` bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `created_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(3),
  `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(3) ON UPDATE current_timestamp(3),
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `uq_elements_no` (`project_id`,`no`),
  KEY `ix_elements_rev` (`project_id`,`rev`),
  KEY `ix_elements_folder` (`folder_id`),
  KEY `ix_elements_from` (`from_id`),
  KEY `ix_elements_to` (`to_id`),
  KEY `ix_elements_target` (`target_folder_id`),
  KEY `ix_elements_agent` (`agent_id`),
  KEY `ix_elements_folder_type` (`folder_id`,`type`),
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_agent` FOREIGN KEY (`agent_id`) REFERENCES `agents` (`id`) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_folder` FOREIGN KEY (`folder_id`) REFERENCES `folders` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_from` FOREIGN KEY (`from_id`) REFERENCES `elements` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_project` FOREIGN KEY (`project_id`) REFERENCES `projects` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_target` FOREIGN KEY (`target_folder_id`) REFERENCES `folders` (`id`) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  CONSTRAINT `fk_elements_to` FOREIGN KEY (`to_id`) REFERENCES `elements` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `ck_elements_branch` CHECK (`type` = 'arrow' or `branch` is null and `back` = 0),
  CONSTRAINT `ck_elements_gate` CHECK (`type` = 'gateway' or `target_folder_id` is null),
  CONSTRAINT `ck_elements_agent` CHECK (`type` = 'block' or `agent_id` is null),
  CONSTRAINT `ck_elements_arrow` CHECK (`type` in ('arrow','link') = (`from_id` is not null and `to_id` is not null))
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci;

Structure sources

The initial schema is in sql/schema.sql. Migration 007-engine.sql adds the folder-and-type index; 008-link.sql adds the link type and updates the check of connection ends. For this article, priority is given to the current database, since the original schema and later migrations may differ.

The application rules are described from lib/elements/elements.php, lib/elements/kinds.php, lib/elements/shape.php and lib/core/ids.php.

pages.title: bin/goblin.php
pages.summary_html:
Goblin is the agent's command line.

The article links this file with the PHP modules and tables it calls. Its functions should be used in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

Goblin is the agent's command line. It provides one program for two roles. Who you are is decided by the token in the environment: GOBLIN_RUN — leader: drives the run, issues tasks, accepts the work; GOBLIN_STEP — worker: does one step and submits the result; GOBLIN_AGENT — worker with a long-lived token: takes its own steps itself. GOBLIN_WORKER_SESSION — permanent worker instance id for engine 2. Always required: GOBLIN_URL API address, for example http://localhost/goblin/api.php GOBLIN_PROJECT project key from the #p= link Optional: GOBLIN_LEAD leader session name — goes to the worker in the note for the step. The program keeps no state of its own: everything lives on the server. The commands work the same on localhost and on a hosting. Where things are: lib/cli/net.php — HTTP, tokens, line parsing; lib/cli/lead.php — leader commands; lib/cli/engine.php — the engine: state, go, drive, pace, history, work; lib/cli/worker.php — worker commands; lib/cli/launch.php — task package and worker launch; lib/cli/watch.php — run watchdog; lib/cli/help.php — short hints.

pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

Server command line: migrations, backup, code map, cleanup, AI jobs. Runs only from the terminal. Usage: php bin/server.php migrate [--apply]; php bin/server.php backup [label]; php bin/server.php files-gc [--apply]; php bin/server.php map; php bin/server.php ai-job ID. The one-time transfer from Goblin v1 (v1-* commands) is done and removed: its code is in archive/lib-transfer/.

Commands. migrate — list the migrations from sql/migrations that are not in schema_migrations (with --apply — apply them and record the time). backup — a snapshot in backup/<date>_<label>: code via rsync (without backup/, workspace/, data/files/, secrets.php and archive/), a database dump via mariadb-dump and ОПИСЬ.txt. files-gc — find .bin files in files_dir that no asset refers to (with --apply — delete them). map — print to stdout the code map from the headers of the files in lib, public/src and bin; creates no files. ai-job ID — run a background job of the built-in AI (aiJobRun).

collects exactly what goes out (spec, input, work, criteria), checks the length limits, computes the request fingerprint. pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Submission signaller: TypeSafe Jev. Provides: jevReady(), jevAsk(), jevSignal(), jevBranch(), stepJev(). Does not: accept or return anything — it only raises a flag. Role. Everything that can be checked exactly, Goblin checks itself: the sample of the answer, the decision's condition, the presence of files, the step time. Jev takes on what an algorithm cannot see — whether the submission matches the assignment and what has already been accepted in meaning. The line `a=7` after `a=1` fits the sample but not the assignment. The rule for disagreement: if the algorithm said "no" — it is no, opinions are not asked. If the algorithm said "yes" and Jev raised a flag — the step is not accepted by itself, but goes to the leader. Measurements on live runs: it recognizes a contradiction confidently (89% on a planted defect), while the verdict "accept/return" swings (47…95% confidence), so it never has the deciding vote.

Simple path for the leader agent: plain GET addresses and a text reply.

The article links this file to the PHP modules and tables it calls. Use its functions in the intended request or command context, respecting the caller's access checks and transactions.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Simple path for the leader agent: plain GET addresses and a text reply. Provides: goScheme(), goBegin(), goTask(), goWork(), goDone(), goFail(), goAgain(), goWhere(), goWait(), goStop(), goInvite(). Does not: introduce its own run rules — it calls the same engine (lib/engine/) as the full API. It does not check the submission: the leader answers for the worker's work, the server only softly checks the form of the answer and the arithmetic ("⚠", goAnswerWarnings). Why separate from the full API: an agent in a terminal needs one curl and a reply that reads by eye. JSON, tokens and batches are not its concern. The leader sees only the skeleton: block number and name, task address, command (goNextLines). Only the worker sees the spec and input: op=task writes the task to a file and returns the line "task in file …" (goTaskFile); text — &text=1. The task address "137.3" (block.round) stands on the first line of the task and at the start of the worker's answer; done refuses by it an answer to another round (goAnswerAddress). The contract: the reply to any command immediately contains the next step. No separate "what next" request is needed — otherwise the leader would guess when to ask.

The service folder lies IN the work folder on purpose (runServiceDir): the worker starts in the work folder and may be unable to read beyond it or may stall on a permission question. The tasks are separated from the worker's own files by the service folder, and from the browser by its .htaccess (serviceDirMake). The name is set by the server: the leader has nothing to count. A repeated task writes the same file.
goTasksDir:1058function goTasksDir(array $run): stringThe run's tasks folder: <work folder>/service/tasks/r<N>.
goSchemeFile:1075function goSchemeFile(array $run): ?stringThe overall picture of the scheme for the worker — the file "схема.txt" next to the tasks, one per run. Only if "Give the worker the overall picture of the scheme" (share_scheme) is enabled in the folder properties. The task holds one line with the path: the worker reads the file once, and the tasks do not bloat. The live scheme cannot be edited during a run, so the file is written at the first task and does not change afterwards.
goSchemeMap:1099function goSchemeMap(int $folderId): arrayScheme skeleton as chains — without spec: ◯190 Start → ▣75 Start counting → ▣76 Next file → ◆77 File exists? ◆77 yes → ▣78 Look for a face → ◆79 Face found? Decision branches — on their own lines; a node already shown — briefly, by number (▣76).
goStepRunning:1158function goStepRunning(int $projectId, int $runId, array $step): voidMove the issued step to "working": the block on the canvas lights up.
goWork:1178function goWork(): voidGET op=work&block=N — the task is handed to the worker, who has taken it up. The status is needed only for the picture: the block lights up "in progress", and a person at the screen sees where the run is now. Skipping it is harmless.
goFail:1208function goFail(): voidGET op=fail&block=N&why=… — the task failed.
goInvite:1251function goInvite(): voidGET op=invite&run=rN[&reply=ADDRESS] — the worker's intro, as a ready line. The leader composes nothing for the worker: it forwards this line as is. It contains the path to the worker instruction, which the server built for the folder's environment at begin (goWorkerFile), and how to answer — for this environment only. reply — the leader's address: in Orca a terminal (then the line has a ready reply command), in SendMessage — its session name. The line has no double quotes: it is forwarded by the command --text "$(curl …invite…)".
goWorkerFile:1298function goWorkerFile(array $run, array $folder, bool $fresh = false): ?stringThe run's worker instruction — the worker.md file next to the tasks, one per run. Built at begin for the folder's environment (workerDoc); the worker does not go to the server, but will always read a file in the work folder. $fresh — rewrite (begin); without it the file is written only if it is missing (the run started before this edit, or the setup was changed to a team after begin). In solo there is no worker — and no file either.
goSelf:1312function goSelf(array $run, array $step): boolWhether the leader does the step itself: in solo — always; in Orca and SendMessage — when the step got no worker (the card has leader or nothing). In subagents the leader decides itself.
goWhere:1321function goWhere(): voidGET op=where[&run=r12] — where the run is and what to do now.
goBrief:1342function goBrief(array $run): stringTail of the short summary: which blocks are in progress now and how many times they went around the loop.
goWait:1370function goWait(): voidGET op=wait[&run=r12][&sec=25] — wait for changes. The connection is held until the run version grows. Needed only when several workers are working and the leader has nothing to do right now.
goStop:1392function goStop(): voidGET op=stop[&run=r12] — close the run.
goAgain:1419function goAgain(): voidGET op=again&block=N — redo a block: the last attempt is erased, the block is issued again. Needed when the worker botched it and the leader has already marked "done". The engine rule is the same: it can be erased only if nothing has been built on this result yet — otherwise the server will name what to reset first.

Acceptance specifics

goDone saves the answer and calls stepAcceptDo on behalf of the leader. This confirms the leader's decision, not an automatic run of all step.submit checks. The command matches the block and attempt address, recognizes a repeat of an already accepted answer and picks up the files named in the report (goCatchFiles). Instead of an answer a decision needs a branch (stepDecideDo), a gateway — a pass mark (stepPassDo). The form of the answer is checked softly (goAnswerWarnings): a mismatch with the answer sample, "calls=K" beyond paid_calls or the expr arithmetic yields a "⚠" line in the reply and in the feed, but the answer is still accepted.

The article links this file to the PHP modules and tables it calls. Use its functions in the intended request or command context, respecting the caller's access checks and transactions.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Assets: project assets. They live on their own and attach to anything. Provides: assetRow(), assetShape(), assetGet(), assetCreate(), assetUpdate(), assetDelete(). Does not: attach (assets/links.php) and does not serve bytes (assets/files.php). The type (kind) is a plain string from config.txt [asset_kinds]: a new type needs no migration. There is exactly one source: an address (uri), uploaded bytes (file_key) or text (body).

Beyond the list in the header there are the helpers assetUri(), assetKind(), assetFolders(). asset.get returns one asset with text, a folder gallery or the whole project's gallery (scope=library), the assets of one owner (element, folder, run or step, with an optional role) or the project's last 500 assets. assetShape marks an asset missing if the file at the disk path has vanished. assetCreate does not spawn records: a path that already has a record returns the earlier asset. An asset with links is deleted only with force; uploaded bytes (file_key) are erased after the transaction commits (dbAfterCommit) — if the batch is rolled back, the asset stays with its file.

pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Utility of the new engine (stage E3): view a run, make a manual step in one call, lead it to a human, take worker's job. Provides: cmdState(), cmdHistory(), cmdPace(), cmdGo(), cmdDriveRoute(), cmdDrive2(), cmdWorkRoute(), cmdWork2(), workTake(), runState(), runPhase(), reviewOf(), didLine(), serverHas(). Does not do: it knows nothing about run rules — neither decision conditions, nor acceptance, nor marks. The server makes the move (run.advance); the utility prints what it did and notices when a human is needed or a worker is silent. Exit codes (md_backend/ru/progon.md): 0 run passed or step made · 2 server unavailable 3 human needed · 4 worker silent · 5 stopped, failed or paused · 6 dead end. drive and work are the main commands: cmdDriveRoute() and cmdWorkRoute() pick the path by the run's engine. drive2 and work2 are alias names of the new path, drive1 and work1 are the old move (engine = 1). The command table is COMMANDS in bin/goblin.php.

pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

The run watchdog: silent while everything is moving, and it finishes when the leader is needed. Provides: cmdWatch(). Does not do: changes nothing — only reads run.get and writes the journal. pages.title: lib/core/db.php
pages.summary_html:
A database connection and four ways to query it.

This article links the file to the PHP modules that call it and to the tables. Use its functions only in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

A database connection and four ways to query it. Provides: db(), dbAll(), dbRow(), dbValue(), dbRun(), dbId(), dbTransaction(), dbOnRollback(), dbAfterCommit(), dbUndoDisk(), dbNow(), dbStamp(). Does not: know any table — SQL lives only in the domains.

There is one PDO connection per process: errors are exceptions, rows are associative arrays, prepared statements are used without emulation, and numbers from the database are not turned into strings. dbTransaction() does not nest: inside an open transaction the closure simply runs. What a rollback does not remove from disk is registered via dbOnRollback() and removed by dbUndoDisk() (which also forgets the deferred work). What cannot be rolled back — for example deleting a file — is deferred via dbAfterCommit() until the transaction is committed: outside a transaction the work runs immediately, and a failure of such work does not spoil the response, because the database has already decided. dbStamp() converts a moment from a database field to epoch seconds using the database's own calculation, so that the PHP and database time zones do not diverge.

pages.title: lib/engine/advance.php
pages.summary_html:
The engine's advance: do everything that can be done without a human.

This article links the file to the PHP modules that call it and to the tables. Use its functions only in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

The engine's advance: do everything that can be done without a human. Provides: engineAdvance(), advanceAfter(), advanceOn(), advanceLoad(), advanceLive(). `advanceRun()` does not sleep and does not go to the network: it is one transaction under the project lock. `engineAdvance()` orchestrates Jev in two short lock sections and calls the network between them. In one advance, in order, while there is something to do (no more than 50 actions, Jev — no more than ADVANCE_JEV_LIMIT per request): 1. the run is not going — nothing; a human asked to stop — cancel the open steps; 2. the display pause has not expired — nothing, wakeIn = how much is left; 3. acceptance of what was submitted — decided by the run's judge (runs.judge); 4. decisions with a condition — by the input variables; 5. issuing the ready blocks; 6. the end of the run — if it is passed. What the run is waiting for — a string in runs.wait_for. The version grows only on a real change. The advance runs for all runs with engine = 2 under any driver (manual and utility): the driver only asks for an advance, the rules are here. Runs with engine = 1 are not touched by the engine. The browser does not make an advance. After a command (advanceAfter) the advance is only deterministic, without the network; Jev is called by run.advance.

pages.summary_html:
An expression parser: one grammar for block arithmetic (expr) and a decision's condition (cond).

This article links the file to the PHP modules that call it and to the tables. Use its functions only in the intended request or command context, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

An expression parser: one grammar for block arithmetic (expr) and a decision's condition (cond). Provides: exprParse(), exprCompute(), exprNames(), the classes ExprVerbal, ExprMissing, ExprFail. Does not: know about steps and the database, does not call eval — only text and variables. The grammar (recursive descent): program := statement (';' statement)* [';'] statement := name '=' expression — an assignment, only in arithmetic | expression expression := and ('||' and)* and := comparison ('&&' comparison)* comparison := sum [('>' | '>=' | '<' | '<=' | '==' | '!=') sum] sum := product (('+' | '-') product)* product := sign (('*' | '/') sign)* sign := '-' sign | '(' expression ')' | number | name Names are letters of any language, digits and "_": conditions on schemes are written in Russian. In a condition a single "=" means "equals" — that is how people write. The signs ≤ ≥ ≠ are understood.

pages.title: lib/engine/judges/formal.php
pages.summary_html:
The formal judge: decides by code, without people and without the network.

This article links the file to the PHP modules and tables it calls. Use its functions in the intended request or command context, keeping the caller's access checks and transactions.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and boundaries

The formal judge: decides by code, without people and without the network. Provides: judgeFormal(). Does not: change the step — only issues a decision; does not ask Jev. Checks run in order, and the first one that fails is a return with a reason: there is a result → pattern (kind, then values {a}) → arithmetic → files and requests. It can accept only if a SUBSTANTIVE check passed — arithmetic with assignments or a pattern with variables. Files and a pattern without variables are technical validity: a non-empty picture of the wrong object passes them all. No substantive check — "unsure", the step waits for a person. The exception is the block property trust_form = true. The return reason for the worker has no expected numbers ("arithmetic does not match the input"): otherwise it would submit the hint without calculating. The full comparison is in detail, the leader sees it.

pages.title: lib/folders/transfer.php
pages.summary_html:
Moving a folder to another project — with its content and history.

This article links the file to the PHP modules and tables it calls. Use its functions in the intended request or command context, respecting the caller's access checks and transactions.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Moving a folder to another project — with its content and history. Provides: folderTransfer(), transferRows(), transferAddresses(), transferAssets(). Does not: copy, but moves: the old project no longer has the folder. Everything tied to the folder moves with it: elements, composition, properties, assets, runs with steps, tasks, labels and events. Block and run numbers are issued anew — they are unique within a project, and in the new home the old ones may be taken; steps and events follow the new block numbers. Agents live in the project, not in the folder — assignments are removed from the blocks and steps. Tombstones remain in the old project; the moved rows carry the new project's revision.

The transfer is split into parts. folderTransfer(), under the lock of both projects, checks the protection of a live scheme, cuts the links and gateway targets across the moving boundary (linksCutAcross, gatesCutAcross) and makes the top folder a root in the new project. transferRows() moves the branch rows, blocks, runs and the tables tied to them; transferAddresses() renumbers steps and events by the new block numbers; transferAssets() moves asset bindings (an asset that is also held by something that stays is copied, not moved).

Purpose and limits

Utility: project tree and the card of the selected object. Provides: structureAct(). Does not: write to the database directly — only through API operations, so every change has a journal entry and a revision. Before an edit, structureOwn() checks the project owner; moving a folder to another project goes through folderTransferFromCabinet() from public/account.php, and everything else is one batch of a single operation with a revision and a journal entry (structureOp).

pages.title: Request handling
pages.summary_html:
A request passes through the public entry point, operation and access checks, and then reaches a domain handler. The response is returned after the intended operation is done.

Separating the entry from the domain logic lets the interface and agents share the same rules. A command name does not give the right to run it without a suitable context.
pages.body_html:
Sequence

For the API, the entry is public/api.php. lib/boot.php loads the library; dispatch reads the operation, finds its description in OPS, checks the HTTP method and role, and then calls the handler.

The handler reads the parameters, gets the project and checks that the objects belong to it. The response and errors are built with lib/api/http.php. The editor HTML is assembled separately: the client gets data through the API.

Different kinds of commands

read marks a read route in the catalog, batch — an operation allowed in a batch, single — a separate command. The simple agent path has GET commands that change state. So whether it is safe to open an address again cannot be decided by the HTTP method alone.

pages.title: Transactions, revisions and retries
pages.summary_html:
Related scheme changes are atomic: either the whole batch is saved or none of its operations. A revision lets clients get a consistent delta of the project.

Run commands use a lock on the same project. The retry request identifier helps tell a repeated delivery from a new command.
pages.body_html:
Batch of changes

runBatch runs the operations in a transaction and raises the project revision once per batch. Temporary refs let later operations refer to objects created in the same batch.

A retry with the same key and a matching body gets the earlier response. The same key with a different body is treated as a conflict. The journal stores the arguments, the previous values and the result of the operation.

Client changes

changes returns rows with rev greater than the revision known to the client, plus data about deletions. Deletions are applied before updates. The project revision describes data changes, while runs.version describes changes of the state of a specific run.

Run lock

engineLocked runs a command under a lock on the project row. The lock serializes changes of steps and marks with scheme edits. Network waiting happens outside the transaction; after returning, the state is checked for freshness.

pages.title: Rights and access context
pages.summary_html:
The server identifies the participant by the token presented or by the user session. The role is not accepted as a trusted field in the command body.

Permission for an operation and access to a specific project are checked separately. Knowing the project key gives the read access the system intends, but not a universal right to write.
pages.body_html:
Determining the role

A run token sets the leader role; step or agent — worker; project is used as human access to the project. A user login is tied to a session, and a guest request stays a guest request.

requireRole checks that the role is allowed for the operation. requireProject and requireWrite check the project and writing: the linked token, the owner and the guest_write setting are taken into account. sameProject does not allow substituting an object from another project.

Worker limits

A worker gets the context of its step, the inputs and the allowed actions. The decision on acceptance and on choosing a branch belongs to the leader or to the intended checker. Passing on a secret token changes the access context, while changing the role field in a request does not.

Admin login

The admin panel uses its own login check and cookie. A user account and an admin session should not be considered one mechanism.

pages.title: Storage of assets and files
pages.summary_html:
An asset is a separate object of the project. Its content and way of storage are independent of where it is used in a scheme or a run.

A link tells why the asset is needed: as a task, a source, a sample, a cover or a result. Thanks to this, one resource can take part in different contexts.
pages.body_html:
Creating and linking

assets stores the text, the address or the key of an uploaded file and its metadata. asset_links names the owner and the role. Removing a link does not automatically mean deleting the standalone asset.

PHP ensures one spec per owner. A result and a preview belong to a run or a step; for a decision, a spec is allowed as the selection criterion. A cover made by a run is marked made_by_run and is kept apart from the design set by a person.

Access to files

File operations check the project and the token scope. Local paths are limited by file_roots and are checked using the real path. A worker gets the files of its step.

In the work folder, source files and results are told apart. A new run uses the results directory out/rN; preparation can archive the previous out, keeping the inputs.

pages.title: Handling built-in AI requests
pages.summary_html:
The assistant turns the user's request into a proposal of operations on the scheme. The call to the model is made by a background job, so the web request does not wait for the network response.

The model response goes through compilation into allowed operations. Data is saved through the ordinary server change mechanism.
pages.body_html:
Request path

aiContext collects the context of the project and folder, the tasks, the source files, the pre-check and the run data. ai.jobs queues the request and starts the handler. The model client gets this context and returns a response with the cost accounted for.

aiCompile picks the allowed operations and reports the parts that were dropped. The chat shows the plan first; applying it is a separate action. The builder has its own flow: a card survey, assembly as a difference from a catalog scheme, a trial rollout and repair, then the folder (lib/ai/build.php). Its rules are a separate file конструктор.md and the "Catalog experience" from the passports.

What playback means

aiPlay evaluates how the scheme would go on assumed outcomes. First an exact pre-check is done, then a semantic evaluation. This mode does not create real attempts and does not prove that an agent did the tasks.

Accounting

The conversation, messages and jobs are stored separately. A model error and an unknown cost differ from a successful response with zero cost. Jev for run evaluation has a separate call path and its own decision rules.

pages.title: How the documentation works
pages.summary_html:
The documentation is stored as a tree of articles and a separate graph of directed links. PHP outputs the selected article and the navigation by sections.

Every item is built the same way: a title, two or three paragraphs of summary, the detailed content and collapsed technical links.
pages.body_html:
Article and link

documentation_pages contains parent_id, slug, title, summary_html, body_html and keywords. The historical name keywords is used for the array of tags.

documentation_links stores its own id, the source, the target and the resource type. In the text, the marker [[ID|visible text]] is used. In the source content files, a slug is allowed instead of an ID, and the publisher replaces it with the identifier of the saved link.

Display

The right block shows only the selected article. Navigation by subsections stays on the left. A general article explains the purpose and common rules of the section; the details of child articles are not copied into it.

Inline links are placed in the summary or the detailed text. Additional technical links are grouped after the description and are collapsed at first. Incoming mentions are computed by target_page_id of the same links table.

Search and map

Text search matches the query against the title, the tags and the content of an article. The search is literal; several words are treated as a phrase. A tag opens a separate selection by tag.

The map is built from the saved links. It shows the structure of mentions, not the execution route of a Goblin scheme. The map scale can be changed with a trackpad gesture.

Updating

All the main articles are stored in a single content.json. Publishing keeps the identifiers of existing articles and links. When the implementation changes, the matching article and the related requirements must be updated.

Callouts

Any article can hold separate callouts in documentation_callouts. The type future_plan marks a plan for the future, agent_correction — an addition or correction made by an AI agent. A callout has its own identifier, the source article, the content, the author and the order. The type is also reflected in the HTML attribute data-callout-kind.

Plans are collected automatically in the [[future-list|List]]. Agent corrections are shown in a separate color in the source article and do not automatically become an approved requirement. Empty callouts are not shown.

The workflow is described in [[backend-documentation-publishing|publishing]], the meaning of the marks — in [[backend-documentation-status|item statuses]].

The map supports a section filter and the nearest incoming/outgoing links of the selected article. The filter does not remove links from the database. The search also covers the text of callouts.

pages.title: API operations catalog
pages.summary_html:
The catalog links an operation name to the HTTP method, the roles and the PHP handler. It mirrors the OPS table in the current router.

Role admission in the catalog is the first stage of checking. The parameters, access to the project and whether the action is allowed in the current state are checked by the handler itself.
pages.body_html:
Reading the catalog

batch allows the operation to run in a transactional batch. single runs as a separate command. read marks the route mode; for the simple agent path, the actual action of the handler must be taken into account.

The short commands begin, task, work, done, again and others use GET, although some of them change state. To read instructions, docs.run is used; getting an instruction does not by itself prove that a run was started or finished.

The simple leader path (scheme, begin, task, work, done, fail, again, where, wait, stop, invite) consists of the names from SIMPLE_OPS in [[backend-resource-lib-api-simple-php|lib/api/simple.php]]; in the OPS registry each of them has its own row, and the response comes as text. docs.run returns a Markdown task for a folder (folder=ID): by default — for the leader, to do a run (the optional worker=… is the address of the performer), and with role=draw — a task to draw or fix the scheme of the folder. The docs.run&role=draw row in the table shows this variant; it has no separate entry in OPS, and the handler is the same — docsRun.

folder.embed returns a signed link to an embeddable illustration of one folder (without a project key). asset.workfile.rename and asset.workfile.delete rename and delete a file of the work folder and fix the assets that refer to it; run.event puts an event into the run feed.

project.update accepts title, guestWrite, aiConfirm, strictChecks and lang. lang is the agents language of the project (the instructions for the leader and worker, the run tasks, the built-in AI): only ru and en are allowed, otherwise the request is refused with "Agent language must be one of: ru, en". It can be changed by someone who is allowed to write to the project (the human role: a person or a project token). While a run is going in the project (running or paused), a change of language is rejected as a conflict with the active run. A new project gets the interface language of the person who created it; from the project language the server chooses the language of its replies to agents (see [[frontend-languages|"Languages: interface and agents"]]).

voice.session and voice.speak are the voice operations of the built-in AI (handlers voiceSession and voiceSpeak in lib/ai/voice.php). Both are POST, role human only, mode read: they are not written to the change journal. The caller must be a member of the project, and the key and address of the voice service come from the personal or shared access ([[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]]); with no key the reply is a refusal, "no key for voice". voice.session takes no parameters and returns JSON {value, expires, url}: a temporary OpenAI token for one recognition session (valid for 10 minutes; the installation key never reaches the browser), its expiry time, and the address of the service the browser connects to by itself. voice.speak takes text (not empty, at most 4000 characters are spoken; empty text is the error "Nothing to speak") and replies not with JSON but with mp3 sound right in the response body.

pages.title: Settings and installation maintenance
pages.summary_html:
Installation settings, lists of allowed values and migrations define the environment of the server code. Changing them affects the whole installation, not only the open project.

The service CLI program runs migrations, backups, cleanup and background jobs. A user's scheme is changed through domain operations.
pages.body_html:
Settings

lib/core/config.php reads the installation configuration and secrets, and takes into account the matching environment variables and the hosting configuration. config.txt holds lists, including the CLI and model options. Changing the shared lists is allowed to the administrator.

The documentation lists the mechanisms and parameter names, but does not copy secret values. The allowed file roots are set by file_roots.

Service launch

bin/server.php accepts the commands migrate, backup, files-gc, map and ai-job. Migrations and cleanup have a separate apply mode --apply; reading the state and applying changes are different actions.

schema_migrations records the structure changes that were applied. Background AI jobs use ai-job with a job identifier. A service launch is not the execution of a scheme by an agent.

pages.title: leader — worker
pages.summary_html:
The leader coordinates the execution: it gets a task from the server, passes it to the worker, and gives the worker's answer back to the server; it also safeguards the course of the run. The worker does the task it was given and returns the result.

This is the "Leader — worker" team (leader-worker). One agent can do both roles in turn if this is agreed explicitly: in the "Leader does everything alone" team this is exactly what happens. Even then, issuing the task, doing it and acceptance stay separate actions.
pages.body_html:
leader

In the simple path, the main one for a run, the leader is a postman and a safeguard of the course. It takes a task from the server, forwards the line "task in file …" to the worker, and passes the whole worker answer to the server with the command done word for word: the server itself separates explanations and remarks placed before the address into the journal. It sees only the frame — the number and name of the block, the task address, the command; the spec, the input and the answers of earlier blocks are seen by the worker. If the course goes wrong, the leader sorts it out itself: chooses the branch of a decision that Jev did not settle, asks a worker that went silent, reissues a failed block once (again), handles the ERROR message from the worker. It calls the human when the trouble is in the scheme or the spec, when the failure repeated, and to close the run. The leader does not edit the spec and does not check the work.

A block marked "performer — leader: do it yourself" is done by the leader itself and handed in through done: this is how every block works in the "Leader does everything alone" team, in Orca and SendMessage — on a block with no worker on its card; in subagents the leader decides itself whether to give the block to a subagent or to do it.

In the full API and CLI, the leader uses the allowed commands for opening, acceptance, return and choosing a branch. It passes the worker the exact task address and keeps the addressed answer. Changing the text of a result to match the expected answer is not allowed.

worker

In the simple path, the worker does not go to the server: it reads the whole task file and answers the leader in one line following the sample, starting it with the task address. A remark about the work goes in the same line before the address. Nobody checks the worker's work, so the worker writes "done" only when the work is really done.

In the full API, the worker gets the package of its step: the spec, the inputs, the previous results and the rules of handing in. Through the API it reports progress, registers external requests and hands in the result. The server ties access to the token of the step or of the agent.

The way of launching and communication is described separately: [[run-environment|Runtime environment]]. The team compositions and their differences are in [[run-role-models|Roles]].

pages.title: Preparation and launch
pages.summary_html:
Before launch, the scheme must have a clear entry, tasks and allowed transitions. The server pre-check finds the obstacles that can be found without doing the work, and separately the remarks that do not hold the run.

Preparation clears the display of the previous run and the service files of steps; the results of past runs stay in their out/rN folders. Creating a new run is a separate operation.
pages.body_html:
Order of actions

First the scheme and the instructions for its folder are fetched (docs.run), then run.check is done. If there are several entries, the starting element is given. Before launch, the work folder, the available tools and the assignment of performers are checked.

The pre-check response has two parts. problems are obstacles: the scheme is not ready, and begin answers "SCHEME NOT READY" with a list and does not start the run. warnings are remarks about the scheme: they do not hold the run, but run.check shows them, as do the lines "⚠ block N …" in the begin response and the "Pre-flight check" section in docs.run. Right now there are two kinds of remarks: a block in a round without max_attempts (the server limits it to 20 issues itself) and join=any on parallel branches (the block will be issued once per branch with part of the input; assembling needs join=all). The leader does not edit the scheme, and in the end reports the remarks to the human.

run.prepare requires that the folder has no active run. It hides the statuses of previous runs and removes from the cards everything a run hung on them: covers and step results. With files, the service files of steps (service/steps) are also cleared, and files handed in outside out/ move to out/rN/ of the run that made them. The out/rN/ folders themselves are not archived and not erased: the results of runs pile up side by side. The human's assets — in/, pic/, the spec, its attachments and covers — are never touched. The old backups service/archive/out_oldN stay as they were, and new ones are not created.

Creation

Under a lock, run.start checks that there is no other active run, creates runs with engine=2 and issues the leader token. Results are placed in out/rN: the server creates the folder at start. For the JSON path, driver is chosen from manual/utility, judge — from human/formal; Jev is set by a separate setting.

The simple begin includes its own preparation and the leader launch: the pre-check, the reset as in run.prepare with files, under a lock, creating the run (driver=lead, judge=human, jev=judge), the out/rN folder and the worker instruction service/tasks/rN/worker.md (in the "Leader does everything alone" team it does not exist), then the first task. Once, the response brings the "⚠" remarks, the run description from the starter if there is one, and "SCHEME IN BRIEF". The begin sequence must not be mechanically replaced by a set of commands from another protocol: the received instructions must be followed.

A run of a folder that a gateway leads into is started by a human; the entry into it is passed with the starter response, see [[run-graph|"Transitions, forks and loops"]].

pages.title: States and attempts
pages.summary_html:
A run holds the overall state of the pass, and a step holds the state of a specific attempt of an element. Several attempts of one block are told apart by the attempt number and the row identifier.

A handed-in result may still wait for a decision. Successful completion is defined by the state of the graph, not only by the absence of a working worker.
pages.body_html:
Run

StateMeaning
runningExecution is active.
pausedProgress is suspended.
stoppedThe run is stopped.
doneThe pass finished successfully.
failedAn unsuccessful outcome is recorded.

A pause and a stop request have different consequences. stop_at marks the stop request, finished_at — the completion. The order of commands is checked by the server.

Step

On issue, issued is created, while working running is used, on handing in — submitted. Acceptance moves the attempt to accepted. Returns, cancellations and errors are recorded in the history; the exact allowed values are listed in the structure of run_steps.

A result belongs to the pair "element — attempt" inside a run. A loop and rework can increase attempt, so the attempt number should not be taken as only the round number.

Completion

The engine checks that there are no open steps and no free marks, that an accepted terminal result exists and the state of the last attempts. A dead end, waiting for a human and successful completion are different outcomes.

pages.title: Transitions, forks and loops
pages.summary_html:
The executable graph consists of blocks, decisions, gateways and the arrows that connect them. Its state is defined by the accepted steps and the available inputs.

A mark on an arrow means permission to move on. It is issued and consumed by the server, which makes it possible to tell an available transition from one already used.
pages.body_html:
Issuing work

engineGraph builds the graph of the folder. ready determines the available elements by their inputs; marks stores which step issued a mark and which step took it. A repeated request must not create a second step from the same input.

Fork

A decision chooses an allowed exit. A numeric condition is parsed by code without eval; a missing required variable is not treated as a negative answer. A verbal condition may require Jev or a human decision.

Merge and loop

On a merge, the required inputs and the origin of marks are taken into account. The values of variables come from the steps that really opened this transition; a conflict of values of one variable requires a decision.

Back arrows mean a return. Attempts are stored separately, and marks note the passing of an arrow. The displayed round of execution and the number of attempts can differ. On a repeat, the block also gets the input of the previous round: [[run-task|Task, inputs and result]].

The server names the dangerous places before launch. A collector that waits for all inputs but will get only one branch of a decision (join=any is needed), and a loop without a back arrow (the pre-check names the arrow that must be marked back) are obstacles. Remarks do not hold the run: a block of a round without max_attempts (the server limits it to 20 issues itself) and join=any on parallel branches, not on branches of one decision — the block will be issued once per branch with part of the input, and assembling needs join=all. The remarks are shown by run.check, begin and docs.run, see [[run-start|"Preparation and launch"]].

Edge of the graph

A group, a table, a note and a navigation link each have their own purpose in the editor. The mere fact of their presence on the canvas does not make them an executable block. A gateway has special rules, including the link to the target folder.

In the simple path, passing through a gateway is marked by done&block=N. The server response names the target folder and reminds that its run does not start by itself: a human starts it. When the target run is started, the starter gets the gateway response ("gateway from "A" · rN: block … → …", no longer than 500 characters), and the first block sees it in the "Input" as the answer of its predecessor.

pages.title: Task, inputs and result
pages.summary_html:
The step package joins the spec and the data needed to run exactly this attempt. The worker must work with the package it was given, keeping the task address.

The result holds the finished work and the intended assets. A progress report, an external request and the final handing in are counted separately.
pages.body_html:
Package

stepPackage builds the task and the inputs. It includes assets and results by actual dependencies; judgePackage prepares data for reviewing a result. spec_hash helps tie an issue to the content of the task.

In the simple path, a line "Run files (already made): out/rN/…" is added to the task: the names of files that the run already put in out/rN/ (only the top level of the folder, at most 30). The "Input" carries only the answers of direct predecessors, while a block after a fork also needs the files made higher up in the scheme. The line is for understanding; numbers and answers the worker takes from the "Input".

Repeat in a loop. A back arrow brings the block a mark only from a decision, so the server adds the "Input" of the previous attempt of the same block (goInputs): the fresh line of the block replaces the old one, and the others are marked "(previous input)". Under the task header there is a line "Round 2 — decision 44 returned "…": branch no" (goRoundLine). The previous version of a file that the repeat will rewrite is copied to out/rN/.попытки/, and the record of the past attempt points at the copy (goKeepTries).

Run spending. The line "Paid calls in the run so far: N" (goSpent) is the sum of calls=K from the accepted answers of blocks with the paid_calls limit: the final block does not need to look for it in other people's tasks.

Handing over work

In the simple path, task writes the package to a file and reports its path. The variant text=1 is meant for text transfer. An answer like "137.3: …" points to block 137, attempt 3; this address must be kept when passing to the leader.

The file named in the worker's answer is searched for by the server itself (a path "out/…" — first of all in out/rN/ of its own run, a bare name — in the work folder and in out/rN/) and is attached to the step as the result; the first picture becomes the cover of the block. Only what was created or changed after the step was issued counts as a result: a mentioned source does not become a result. One file — one author: a file in the same form (path and sha256) that another block of this run already handed in is not attached again, even if the next block is issued in the same second.

In the full API, the worker uses step.get, step.note and step.submit. The allowed inputs, assets and answer forms are checked by the server in the context of its token.

Variables

vars parses the numeric values of the result and merges them with the input variables. A decision and a gateway pass on the input values. Parsing a number does not yet confirm that the calculation is right: that is a job for the expression and form checks.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/api/simple.php (goTaskText, goRunFiles, goCatchFiles), md_backend/ru/progon.md (section 2) 29.09.2026

pages.title: Review and acceptance
pages.summary_html:
Acceptance decides whether a result can be used to move forward. The system separates checking that a result is valid from judging whether the task was actually done.

The base mode is stored in runs.judge, and Jev's participation in runs.jev. A decision applies to one specific submission; a new submission needs a fresh decision.
pages.body_html:
Formal checker

Code checks that a result exists, its form, variable values, arithmetic, files and registered job requests. A failure gives grounds for a return with a reason.

A non-empty file and a match with a simple answer form confirm technical validity. Accepting on its own needs a check of substance — for example calculations or a form with variables. Without one, the formal checker returns unsure, unless trust_form=true is set explicitly.

Human and Jev

human leaves the final decision to a person and prepares a hint from the formal checks. Jev judges the meaning-based criteria and verbal forks using a prepared package.

The network request runs outside the project lock. Before saving the decision, the engine checks that the original state is still current. Uncertainty and an unavailable judgment must not turn into automatic approval.

The leader's simple path

In the short protocol, done means the leader decided to accept the work: goDone saves the result and calls stepAcceptDo. Such an answer must not be taken as proof that all conditions of a full step.submit submission were checked automatically.

A soft check of the answer does not replace acceptance. If the answer does not fit the answer pattern (the same pattern parsing as the formal form check), or its calls=K is greater than paid_calls, or the numbers do not match the arithmetic of the block's expr (exprCheck, same as the formal judge; the server does not name the expected numbers), the server still accepts the block, but adds a "⚠ …" line to the done answer. The leader decides: if it is a mistake, the block is redone with the again command — the server itself clears the untaken issues and the answers of decisions after it, and if the block further on is in progress or already accepted, it names the whole list; in a loop where a new round has only just been issued, the last submitted round is redone (the max_attempts limit counts rounds, not numbers: an erased round does not count); if it is as intended, they go on.

Modes and a short instruction: [[run-jev|Jev]].

pages.title: Tracking calls and results
pages.summary_html:
If a task needs an external service, the worker makes the actual call. Goblin records the job request and links the received asset to the attempt.

For a paid action, the intent is registered first, then the external job id and its outcome are saved. This makes it possible to trace where a result came from.
pages.body_html:
Recording a job request

step.job saves provider, tool, model, request and a local ref. After the external service answers, job_id, state, error or response_asset_id are added. A repeated registration must refer to the same job request if delivery of its result is repeated.

Submitting an asset

The executor saves the output file and links it to the step result. Checks take into account that the file exists and is not empty, its origin, and the recording of the job request, according to the project settings.

Registering a job does not start an external service. A row, or an issued job_id, also does not prove that the result has already been received: the state and the asset must match the actual answer.

pages.title: Waiting, stopping and recovery
pages.summary_html:
After a delivery error, first read the server state: the command may have run even if the client got no answer. The next action is chosen from the saved state.

Continuing, reissuing and resetting mean different things. Keep the attempt history when you need to understand how the run went.
pages.body_html:
Waiting

run.state supports since and wait: the request waits for the version to change, but no longer than the set limit of 25 seconds, and it takes the display pause into account. wait_for explains why the engine is not moving forward.

The display pause show_pause controls the visibility of the sequence on the canvas. It does not replace the run's business pause and does not mean the worker has stopped working.

Return and repeat

A return asks for the result to be reworked. A reissue controls the execution of an attempt in a state the server allows. In the simple protocol, again checks dependencies before it allows a repeat.

An answer with an old attempt address must not close a new attempt. A repeat of an already accepted addressed result is recognized; an answer that contradicts the current attempt is rejected.

Reset and prepare

run.reset deletes the step history within its own reset operation. run.prepare keeps the history and prepares for a new start the display (statuses, covers and step results on the cards) and the service files of the steps; the out/rN folders of past runs stay. These operations cannot be used interchangeably.

During an active engine2 run, the meaningful data of the folders involved is protected. Changing layout and styling is allowed within the handler's rules; changing the spec or the route requires stopping the run.

pages.title: Observation and history
pages.summary_html:
The canvas, the timeline and the log show different sides of one run. The server is the source of state, and the visual effects show its answer.

To explain a specific transition you need attempts and marks; for the sequence of actions, events. The activity indicator shows that a participant is working, but does not confirm a successful outcome.
pages.body_html:
Canvas

run.paint computes the highlight from steps and marks. lit means an available mark, done — a transition already used. For repeated passes, the arrow shows the pass number; for a block, the state of the last attempt and the round.

Timeline and log

run.timeline builds intervals for the steps that have start and end times. run.log reads events, run.report builds a report. Events keep the author, title, text and extra data.

Activity

pulse returns information about working participants for interface indicators. It also tells the left panel where a run is going: runFolders — the project's folders with a run in the running or paused state, runProjects — the keys of the person's projects with such a run; they light up the folder and project icons ([[frontend-left-panel|Left panel]]). The leads key gives the folders where the leader has taken the instruction but the run has not started yet: the canvas blinks their starter. This information does not replace the state of a step and the checker's decision. The watch utility observes a run; autonomous advancing is done by another mode.

pages.title: api, simple path and cli
pages.summary_html:
Goblin offers several ways to work with one server-side run. The full API returns structured data, the simple path returns readable text answers, and the CLI wraps server operations.

The choice of protocol determines how the task is received and how the result is handed over. When switching between them, keep the run and attempt identifiers and remember that acceptance differs.
pages.body_html:
Simple path

scheme shows the scheme, begin starts the pass, task issues the task file, work marks the work, done hands over the leader's decision. fail, again and stop control the error, the repeat and the stop.

begin shows remarks about the scheme ("⚠ block N …"), and once — the run description from the starter and "SCHEME IN BRIEF". The done answer, besides the confirmation and the next task, may carry the "⚠" of the soft answer check; for a gateway it names the target folder. invite gives the worker's intro as a ready line (in the "Leader does everything alone" team it is a refusal). The server builds the role instructions for the team composition and the folder environment (lib/api/instructions.php): the leader gets their own in full in docs.run, the worker — as the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md, which begin writes.

where and wait are used to continue the dialog with the server and can trigger advancing. They should not be described as a purely passive snapshot. The server's answer contains the next commands and the task address.

CLI and environment

GOBLIN_URL and GOBLIN_PROJECT set the server and the project. GOBLIN_RUN holds the leader's token, GOBLIN_STEP — the step's, GOBLIN_AGENT — the permanent worker's. GOBLIN_WORKER_SESSION tells executor instances apart.

The CLI does not keep its own copy of the execution state. The server checks permissions. The help goblin <command> --help describes the arguments; running help must not perform the action.
