pages.title: Personal account
pages.summary_html:
The personal account opens through account.php and requires a user login. It brings together the information about a person's work with projects.

The page is built on the server. Forms send an action, after which the user gets an updated screen or an error message.
pages.body_html:
Login and session

A new user gives an email, a password and a name. On login the password is checked against the saved hash, and the session is represented by a token with scope=session. Logging out ends the user session.

Access to actions

Handling POST, except login and registration, requires currentUser. Managing the shared configuration lists also requires an admin login. Showing an available object does not cancel the permission check when it is changed.

pages.title: User projects
pages.summary_html:
The project list gives a quick way into the editor and into the view-only mode. Next to each project are the number of folders, elements and the time of change.

A project owned by the user is marked separately. Being in the list and being editable depend on different conditions.
pages.body_html:
Working with the list

The name leads to the editor with the project key. "View" opens the view=1 mode. "New project" leads to the editor, where the project is created by the intended opening scenario.

Data

The list is fetched by userProjects. When an edit is made, the server takes the owner, the token and guest_write into account again. The list is not an independent source of permissions.

pages.title: Tree and object card
pages.summary_html:
The structure section lets you work with a project as a tree of objects. On the left you pick a project, folder or element; on the right its card opens.

The card is for viewing and for the intended edit forms. Saving goes through Goblin operations with a log and a revision.
pages.body_html:
Navigation

Folders are shown nested. Arrows do not take separate rows of the tree: the links are shown in the card. The chosen object determines the content of the right area.

Saving

structureAct handles the forms and calls the domain operations. structureView is responsible for display. This split keeps the shared access rules and the scheme protection during an active run.

pages.title: Agent list
pages.summary_html:
The account shows a combined list of agents from the projects the user owns. You can see the name, role, CLI, model and project.

Cards are changed in the editor. Viewing the list does not start an agent and does not give it new work.
pages.body_html:
Use

Through the project link the user goes to its settings in the editor. The role lead means leader, worker — the executor. The CLI and model parameters come from the saved card.

List size

The account's current query is limited to 300 cards and selects them by the project owner. This is a summary of the available cards, not a list of all running processes.

pages.title: Scheme templates
pages.summary_html:
The account shows the available scheme templates with a name, category, number of elements and origin. A template lets you reuse the structure of a scheme.

Creating a template from a folder and unpacking it are done in the editor. The account lets you view and delete the user templates that are allowed.
pages.body_html:
Content

The template body uses temporary refs, so the original identifiers are not carried into the new folder. When unpacked, new elements are created through server operations.

Deletion

Built-in templates are marked separately. The delete form is shown for a non-built-in template that has no owner or belongs to the current user; the handler additionally checks that the action is allowed. Deleting a template is not the same as deleting a folder already unpacked from it.

pages.title: User tokens
pages.summary_html:
The tokens screen shows their kind, project, label, issue date and state. It helps tell a valid access from a revoked or expired one.

The original secret is shown when it is issued, and only its hash is stored in the database. The account does not restore the secret from that hash.
pages.body_html:
Selection

The current screen selects up to 100 latest tokens with scope=project, run or step, if the user owns the project or is named as the token's creator. It is not a full list of all technical installation sessions.

State

revoked_at means revocation. expires_at sets the end of the term. The screen is a list: a separate issue or revoke button is not implemented in this table. Such operations are done by the matching server routes and admin tools.

pages.title: AI conversations and usage
pages.summary_html:
The AI screen collects your personal access to the models, the conversations of the projects the user owns and the recorded usage. It helps you go back to a project and see the history of requests.

The usage refers to the built-in AI. It cannot be automatically taken as the full usage of all external agents and services that took part in a run.
pages.body_html:
Personal model access

At the top of the screen is the "Personal model access" form: your own API address, model and key, for you only. There are two blocks: "Assistant and builder — DeepSeek" and "Voice — recognition and read-aloud (OpenAI Live)"; voice also has speech languages, a read-aloud model and a voice. An empty field means the shared access of the installation — it is shown in the field in grey, and the shared key is not shown. Your own key is typed in plain text. Under each block it says whose key is in use now. The "Save access" button writes the values to the access field of your user record ([[backend-resource-table-users|users]]).

The access in force is chosen by [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]]: in an ordinary request it is the access of the signed-in person, in a background AI job — of the person who asked the question.

Conversations

The list shows the time of change, the project and the conversation title. Each conversation has two links: "Log" opens the conversation page in a new window (the whole course: questions, answers, usage) — the same page as the conversation link in the assistant panel ([[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]]); "open the scheme" leads to the project's scheme. The current query is limited to 200 conversations.

Accounting

For each project aiUsage is called for 14 days. The table has the day, the number of requests and the number of tokens. The limits in force are set by the AI handling and its settings, and the static caption of the screen does not replace this check.

pages.title: Profile and password
pages.summary_html:
The profile shows the name and email of the current user. The password change form asks for the old and the new password.

Changing the password concerns the user's account. Admin access and agent tokens have their own life cycle.
pages.body_html:
Changing the password

The form sends the password action. The server calls userPassword for currentUser and reports the result. The pass_hash field stores the hash; the original password is not a property the profile shows.

Limits of the screen

The current profile screen has no form for editing the name and email on your own. The admin has separate actions for managing user data.

pages.title: Shared configuration lists
pages.summary_html:
The lists set the allowed options for the installation settings, including agent parameters. This is shared data that affects the projects of different users.

An ordinary login to the account does not allow changing these values. Saving and deleting rows requires an admin context.
pages.body_html:
Storage and change

Values are read from config.txt through lists. The list-save and list-drop actions call listWrite after the adminIn check. The server uses the values when it checks agent cards.

Scope

A CLI line may define the command that starts the executor. So changing a list is a setting of the whole installation and must not be presented as a local styling of one scheme.

pages.title: Admin panel
pages.summary_html:
The admin panel opens through admin.php and requires a separate login. It lets you see the installation data and perform the intended management operations.

The screen gets JSON with the section data and sends changing actions as separate POST requests. Reading and changing are separated in the server code.
pages.body_html:
Login and request

adminApi checks adminIn before it returns data. Reading uses ?api=name, an action uses POST ?api=action with the do field. lib/admin/data.php prepares the data, lib/admin/actions.php makes the change.

Applying changes

Edits of the project name and settings, and of schemes, call the intended domain operations. Managing users, tokens and service cleanup has special handlers. So not all admin actions are an ordinary batch of scheme edits.

pages.title: Overview and installation state
pages.summary_html:
The overview shows summary figures and recent activity. It helps you notice unfinished work and go to a specific object.

The service signals reflect certain server checks. No signal is not a full check that the whole system is healthy.
pages.body_html:
Figures

adminOverview collects the number of objects, activity, live and recent runs. The overview takes into account AI requests and changes from the log.

Service flags

It checks pending migrations, long-running AI jobs, recent errors and the availability of the intended settings. To find the cause, open the data of the matching object.

pages.title: Managing projects and schemes
pages.summary_html:
The admin can view projects and folders, change the intended parameters and delete objects. These operations affect the shared data of the installation.

A live run limits meaningful changes to the scheme that depends on it. Before deleting a project, its active runs may need to be stopped.
pages.body_html:
Project

project.update changes the name and the guestWrite, aiConfirm, strictChecks settings. Assigning ownerId is handled separately, with a check that the user exists.

Scheme

scheme.rename and scheme.delete are applied through ordinary folder operations in a batch. The log, the revision and the protection of an active run are kept.

Deletion

project.delete accepts the stopRuns parameter to stop the active runs first. After the protection check, the project is deleted with its SQL dependencies; the work folders are handled by the intended function that deletes empty folders.

pages.title: Run control
pages.summary_html:
The admin sees the list of runs and the details of the chosen pass. This is a tool for observation and service management of the installation.

The intended action run.stop stops the chosen run. Viewing the card is not acceptance of the results of its steps.
pages.body_html:
Viewing

The routes runs and run get data through adminRuns and adminRun. To analyze the execution, the saved states, attempts and events are used.

Stopping

adminRunStop performs the stop with a server mechanism. Later work with the scheme takes the final state of the run into account. An automatic successful finish must not be replaced by an admin stop.

pages.title: Users and tokens
pages.summary_html:
The admin manages user records and can cut off access through sessions and tokens. These actions differ from changing a project's agent card.

The user, the agent and the token are separate entities. Their identifiers cannot be used interchangeably.
pages.body_html:
Accounts

You can create a user, change data, set a password, end sessions and delete a user. The handlers user.create, user.update, user.password, user.logout and user.delete perform these operations.

Tokens

token.revoke revokes a specific token. tokens.cleanup performs the intended cleanup of records. The token hash is used for checking, and the label and the tail — for a person to recognize it.

pages.title: Log and maintenance
pages.summary_html:
Service actions help maintain the database, files and background jobs. Each action has its own scope and result.

Viewing the state does not apply migrations and does not delete data. Changing actions are performed by separate commands.
pages.body_html:
History

journal and entry show the records and operations of the log. journal.prune takes a term in days and clears the intended history. Clearing the log is different from deleting a project or resetting a run.

Files and database structure

files.gc starts a file cleanup by the server's rules. workdir.delete works with the orphaned folder you name. migrations.apply applies pending migrations. The exact limits are set by the handlers and the configuration of the file roots.

AI and templates

ai.sweep handles stuck background jobs. Templates and the catalog are handled by a separate section, [[accounts-admin-catalog|"Scheme catalog"]]. These actions do not run the jobs of a block scheme.

pages.title: Keeping the architecture documentation current
pages.summary_html:
The documentation should remain the main guide for people and agents who change Goblin. It separates the target design from the current implementation.

Asset statuses and the check date are already in place. The next idea is to tie articles to source versions and automatically mark descriptions that may have become outdated after a code change.
pages.body_html:
Recording the status, the check date and the basis of an article has been added to the [[backend-documentation-status|status mechanism]]. Old assets without an individual check keep an undefined status.

Further development: tie the check date to a specific source version and mark the articles affected by a code change. There is no automatic control yet that the text matches the implementation.

pages.title: Link types and knowledge navigation
pages.summary_html:
The agreed principle: an article should show its outgoing links and incoming mentions. A link is stored as a separate record with an identifier.

The proposed development is to add to the technical classification the meaning of the relation: what implements a requirement, what an object depends on and what uses its data.
pages.body_html:
Proposal

Keep the existing identifiers and add a separate description of the meaning of the relation. The file type PHP or database answers the question about the resource; the relation "implements" or "uses" answers the question about the link.

Signs of readiness

The map and the list let you select the needed kind of relations. Incoming mentions are built from the same record, and a repeated mention does not create contradicting links. A person can go from an interface element to the data and the handler.

Limit of the current model

Now resource_type groups technical resources, and the unique source/target pair allows one link record between two articles. Before introducing several meaning-based relations, the uniqueness model must be defined separately.

A section filter and a mode of the nearest links of an article have already been added. The next possible step is semantic relation types: "handles", "stores", "depends on". They need a separate model, because the current resource_type classifies the target resource.

pages.title: Explicit agreement on the agent environment
pages.summary_html:
The target requirement: an executor must understand where it really works and what tools it has. A scheme setting must not replace this information.

The proposed development is to show, before the start, the expected environment and the actual environment reported by the executor, and to explain a mismatch before work is issued.
pages.body_html:
Proposal

Compare the folder's run_env, the parameters of the agent card and the data of the current executor. If a scenario requires Orca and the agent is in an ordinary terminal, the system should offer an agreed way of executing or clearly name the missing capability.

Signs of readiness

The leader sees which roles are performed and where the worker starts. When one agent combines roles, the separate stages of issuing, executing and acceptance are kept. An unsupported environment is not marked as successfully started.

Current basis

A folder has run_env, an agent has a CLI and parameters, an attempt has ran_on and session. The presence of these fields alone does not mean a finished procedure of agreeing on capabilities.
tags: explicit agreement on the agent environment

pages.title: Traceability of execution
pages.summary_html:
The target principle: from a result it should be clear which task and which attempt created it. Delivery of a message, submission and acceptance must be told apart.

The proposed development is a single view of execution evidence for different launch protocols. It should show the actual actions and the basis for accepting a result.
pages.body_html:
Proposal

Combine on the result card the attempt address, inputs, assets, external job requests and the checker's decision. State clearly whether the result was accepted by the leader through the simple path or reviewed by the automatic checker.

Signs of readiness

A repeated delivery is recognized without new paid work. An old answer does not close a new attempt. For each acceptance you can see who made the decision and which checks were actually done.

Current basis

Attempts, events, job requests and decisions are already stored separately. The simple done and the full step.submit have different acceptance semantics; the evidence interface must keep this difference.

pages.title: Same functions across different skins
pages.summary_html:
The agreed principle: a skin changes the look and the layout of panels while keeping the basic capabilities of Goblin. A user should find the same actions in different styling variants.

The proposed development is an explicit description of the availability and placement of a command in each skin, tied to a single functional description.
pages.body_html:
Proposal

Describe an action once, and keep the differences of presentation as properties of the skin. Moving a button must not create a new domain command or diverging rules of how it works.

Signs of readiness

When the skin changes, the chosen project, the meaning of actions and access to the main capabilities are kept. The documentation shows the differences of placement without copying the full description of a function into each interface variant.

Current basis

The interface already has styling variants. The proposal concerns a single accounting and description of how functions correspond, not a claim that all variants match fully in behavior.

pages.title: Roles
pages.summary_html:
A role scheme defines who coordinates the work, who performs the tasks and who takes part in making decisions. In different scenarios the set of roles and the split of responsibility may differ.

The team composition is chosen for each folder on the "Agents" tab (folders.role_scheme). Two compositions work: "Leader does everything alone" (default) and "Leader — worker"; compositions with a consultant and an auditor can be chosen, but they are marked "later".
pages.body_html:
General principle

The description of a role scheme must define the responsibility of participants and the handover of the task, the result and the decision. One agent combining roles does not cancel the difference between these actions.

Where the participants start and how they exchange messages: [[run-environment|Execution environment]].

Team compositions

Compositionrole_schemeWhat it means
Leader does everything alonesolo (default)The leader is alone — both the leader and the executor. It does not call subagents or other agents, the worker intro (op=invite) is refused, the worker.md file is not written, worker steps are not assigned. The run environment is hidden, a saved one has no effect.
Leader — workerleader-workerThere is a worker; the chosen environment applies. In detail — [[run-roles|"leader — worker"]].
Leader — consultant — worker; Leader — consultant — auditor — workerconsult-worker, consult-audit-workerMarked "later": you can choose them, but the consultant and auditor roles do not work yet — the run goes as "Leader — worker".

The server builds the instructions for the chosen composition and environment: an agent gets only its own scenario and learns nothing about the others.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/folders/folders.php (ROLE_SCHEMES), lib/api/instructions.php (instrScenario, instrLeadHead), lib/api/simple.php (goInvite, goWorkerFile), md_backend/ru/progon.md (section 2) 29.09.2026

pages.title: Execution environment
pages.summary_html:
The execution environment defines where agents work and how the leader hands over a task and gets an answer. It describes how the launch is organized and the links between participants.

Goblin offers the variants Orca, SendMessage and subagents. The environment applies only in a team: in the "Leader does everything alone" composition it is hidden and not used. The folder setting must match the real capabilities of the executors; an environment named in a scheme does not start itself.
pages.body_html:
General principle

The environment defines how executors are started and how messages are passed. The split of responsibility is described separately in [[run-role-models|Roles]]. One role scheme can use different environments.

Choosing the environment

The choice is stored in folders.run_env and is made after the team composition (folders.role_scheme) is chosen, on the "Agents" tab. There is no "not chosen" option: an empty value means subagents. In the "Leader does everything alone" composition, which applies by default, the environment choice is hidden and the saved value has no effect.

From the composition and the environment, Goblin builds the agent instructions (lib/api/instructions.php): the leader gets their own in full in the docs.run link, the worker — as the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md, which begin writes. Each agent sees only its own scenario and learns nothing about other environments.

Who does a block also depends on the environment. In Orca and SendMessage the agent cards apply: a block with a worker on the card is done by the worker, and a block with the leader or an empty card — by the leader itself (the "NEXT" line carries the note "executor — leader: do it yourself"). In subagents the cards do not apply: the leader decides itself whether to give the block to a subagent or to do it.

The environment name in a folder does not confirm that it is available in the current session. If the environment does not match the real capabilities, agree on the way of execution before handing over dependent tasks. The task address and the attempt number are kept with any way of exchange.
pages.source_note: checked against md_backend/ru/progon.md (section 2), lib/api/instructions.php, lib/folders/folders.php (ROLE_SCHEMES, RUN_ENVS, folderActiveRunEnv), lib/api/simple.php (goSelf) 29.09.2026

pages.title: List
pages.summary_html:
Here the "Plan for the future" callouts from the documentation articles are collected automatically. Each idea shows its source section, which you can go to.

The text is stored once: changing a callout updates it both in the source article and in this list. Separate articles with ideas stay in their own sections of the plans area.
pages.body_html:
Ideas from sections

The selection is built from callouts of the type future_plan. "Agent fixes" have a separate type and are not included here.

pages.title: Scenarios
pages.summary_html:
A scenario describes a typical block scheme: which task it solves, what data it gets and how it goes from the start to the result. Such an example helps you build your own process from clear stages.

This is where descriptions of repeatable solutions and ideas for using Goblin are kept. A scheme example is a model of how to build; its presence in the documentation does not mean that a matching run has already been done.
pages.body_html:
Principle of description

Each scenario states the goal, the input data, the sequence of blocks, the conditions of transitions and the expected output. A fork needs clear selection criteria, a repeat needs an exit condition and an attempt limit.

Specific tools are chosen in the block tasks. The roles of participants are described in [[run-role-models|Roles]], and the available external capabilities in [[run-services|Third-party services]].

pages.title: Loop with an exit condition
pages.summary_html:
A loop repeats the work until the exit condition is met. It suits step-by-step improvement of a result or processing data in batches.

Each repetition must have a defined input, a verifiable result and a limit on continuing. Unlimited repetition is not a finished scenario.
pages.body_html:
Purpose of the example

This is a template for writing a task and drawing a scheme in Goblin. It does not create a scheme and does not launch agents. Paths are given relative to the work folder; when run, results are placed in the current run's folder out/rN.

Source data

The file in/brief.txt contains facts about a product. You need to prepare a text of 120–180 words using only these facts. Criteria: a clear purpose, three benefits from the source, no unconfirmed promises. Three versions of the text are allowed, including the first one.

Flowchart

Spec by node

NodeSpec / conditionOutput and acceptance
B1 · PreparationRead brief.txt. Write out the confirmed facts and criteria. Fix the limit: 3 versions.criteria.md contains the source facts, the word range and the verifiable requirements.
B2 · WorkFor the first attempt, write the text. For the following ones, fix the comments from B3 while keeping the requirements already met. Save each version separately.draft-vK.md; K is the scenario's version counter. The text does not replace the previous file.
B3 · CheckCompare the current version with each criterion, count the words and mark unconfirmed statements.review-vK.md: criterion, check result, comment. The counter K is taken from the text version.
D1 · QualityChoose "yes" only if all criteria are met. If the quality needs a human judgment, ask the reviewer for a decision."Yes" → B4; "no" → D2. Uncertainty is not treated as success.
D2 · LimitCompare the number of prepared versions K with 3.K < 3 → B2 with comments; otherwise → B5.
B4 · ResultCopy the accepted version to final.md and attach its check.final.md and the final check; this is the successful result of the task.
B5 · ReviewSave the last version, the remaining comments and the reason the limit was used up. Pass the decision to a person.handoff.md. The requirements for the text are still not met; handing over to a person is not passed off as successful acceptance.

Execution rules

The back arrow D2 → B2 must be marked as a return. The scenario's version counter should not be replaced with attempt: re-issuing a step can increase attempt without producing a new version of the text.

Accepting B3 means that the check report was written correctly; it does not mean a positive assessment of the text itself. The transition is chosen by the contents of the report.

For B2, the issue limit supported by the engine is set in addition. It is useful to distinguish the business limit on versions from the technical limit on repeated issues.

pages.title: Conditional branching
pages.summary_html:
Branching chooses the further work by a condition. Unlike issuing several tasks in parallel, a fork decides which route suits the current input.

The condition must rely on available data. If the data is not enough, that is a reason to get a clarification, not to automatically pick the negative branch.
pages.body_html:
Purpose of the example

This is a template for writing a task and drawing a scheme in Goblin. It does not create a scheme and does not launch agents. Paths are given relative to the work folder; when run, results are placed in the current run's folder out/rN.

Source data

Input: in/photo.png. The task is to prepare a square image of 1024 × 1024 pixels without cropping the content. If the source already matches the size, it must be saved without reprocessing.

Flowchart

Spec by node

NodeSpec / conditionOutput and acceptance
B1 · AnalysisOpen the file and determine the width, height and format. If the file is damaged or missing, report an error; do not invent the dimensions.metadata.json with width, height and format.
D1 · ChoiceCheck that width=1024 and height=1024 hold at the same time."Yes" → B2; "no" → B3. If the dimensions are missing, wait for B1 to be fixed.
B2 · SourceCopy the suitable PNG to the results folder without changing the pixels.original.png, identical to the input file.
B3 · ProcessingFit the image into a 1024 × 1024 square, keeping the proportions. Add white margins; do not crop or paint in any content.processed.png of 1024 × 1024. The content of the source is fully preserved.
B4 · Source outputAttach original.png to the result and report: no processing was required.The file is available as an asset of the result of the active branch.
B5 · Processing outputCheck the size of processed.png and that nothing was cropped, and attach it to the result.An asset and a short report on the conversion.

Execution rules

In the example the branches have separate end blocks. This way there is no need to wait for the result of the branch that was not chosen. If a common continuation point is added, its entry rule must explicitly match the alternative routes.

This example requires resizing, not generative processing. An external service is chosen only when the task really needs it.

pages.title: Image processing
pages.summary_html:
The scenario turns a source image into an asset with the given properties: for example, the needed size, improved detail or changed content.

The processing is done by an agent with a suitable tool. Krea is one of the possible services; the specific tool is chosen by the task and the available capabilities.
pages.body_html:
Purpose of the example

This is a template for writing a task and drawing a scheme in Goblin. It does not create a scheme and does not launch agents. Paths are given relative to the work folder; when run, results are placed in the current run's folder out/rN.

Source data

Input: a product photo in/product.png of 1024 × 1024. You need to prepare a 2048 × 2048 PNG and keep the shape, colors, logo and lettering. The external service for this example is [[run-service-krea|Krea]].

Flowchart

Spec by node

NodeSpec / conditionOutput and acceptance
B1 · PreparationCheck that the source is readable. Fix the size, the important lettering and the details that must not change. Prepare a request for upscaling.request.md and the source file as the input of the next block.
B2 · KreaChoose an available upscaling tool. Before the paid call, register a request, then make the call and save the external identifier. Wait for the result under the same request.candidate.png and details of provider, tool, model and job_id. Do not replace the real call with a local imitation.
B3 · CheckDetermine the size and format. Compare the shape, color, logo and lettering with the source; mark artifacts.review.md: technical parameters and a conclusion on each requirement.
D1 · AcceptanceChoose "yes" when all requirements are confirmed as met. Pass an uncertain judgment of meaning to a person."Yes" → B4; "no" → B5.
B4 · ResultSave the accepted file as product-final.png and attach it to the step together with the report.A 2048 × 2048 PNG and a confirmed link to the external request.
B5 · CommentsSave the rejected candidate and the reasons. Prepare a proposal for the next action without a new paid call.issues.md; rework needs a separate decision.

Execution rules

The tool parameters are taken from the current schema of the available Krea connection. If the needed mode or size is not available, the worker says so instead of promising a capability that does not exist.

After a network failure you need to find out the state of the saved job_id. Sending a new paid job again is not a way to poll the old one.

This example does not set any automatic paid retries. If needed, it can be extended with a [[run-scenario-cycle|loop]] with an explicitly limited number of processings.

pages.title: Image retouching
pages.summary_html:
Retouching is image processing with explicitly given local or overall changes. The scenario must explain what to fix and which features of the source to keep.

A retouching task is worded more precisely than "make it better": it names the area to process, the desired effect and the signs of an acceptable result.
pages.body_html:
Purpose of the example

This is a template for writing a task and drawing a scheme in Goblin. It does not create a scheme and does not launch agents. Paths are given relative to the work folder; when run, results are placed in the current run's folder out/rN.

Source data

Input: in/portrait.png and in/retouch-brief.txt with the temporary skin blemishes marked. You need to remove only the listed blemishes and slightly reduce the highlights, keeping moles, skin texture, face proportions, expression and background.

Flowchart

Spec by node

NodeSpec / conditionOutput and acceptance
B1 · Edit mapRead the list of blemishes. Describe the allowed changes and the details to keep. If the area is ambiguous, ask for a clarification before retouching.retouch-plan.md with a list of specific edits.
B2 · RetouchingApply only the agreed edits with a suitable tool. Do not change the face geometry, age, expression, background and permanent features. For an external call, keep a record of the request.retouched-candidate.png of the original size and changelog.md. The source is saved separately.
B3 · ComparisonCompare the original and the candidate as a whole and by the changed areas. Mark whether the edits were made, whether the details were kept and any possible artifacts.comparison.md with the status of each requirement; a comparison image if needed.
D1 · DecisionAccept only the confirmed edits. If the preservation of appearance and details cannot be judged with confidence, ask for a decision from a person."Yes" → B4; "no" → B5. Uncertainty means waiting for a decision.
B4 · ResultSave portrait-final.png and attach the list of edits made.The final PNG of the original size, the report and a link to the source asset.
B5 · ReworkList the violations and the proposed fixes. Save the current version; do not start new processing without the leader's decision.retouch-issues.md; the result is not yet accepted.

Execution rules

For external processing, [[run-service-krea|Krea]] is acceptable if the connected tool supports the needed editing. Simple upscaling does not replace retouching.

The technical check of the size and the presence of the file is done separately from the visual acceptance. A positive technical result does not confirm that the face and texture were preserved.

When a rework loop is added, the limit on versions and external calls must be defined. The result of each version is saved separately.

pages.title: Third-party services
pages.summary_html:
Third-party services provide capabilities that an agent can call while doing a task: processing assets, generation and other operations outside Goblin.

This section contains short references for the worker. Access to a specific service depends on the connected tools and the agent's account; having a reference does not mean the integration is already available to every worker.
pages.body_html:
Place in the run

The block's spec states the task, the required inputs and the expected result. The agent chooses an allowed tool, makes the external call and returns the result to the step's context.

Goblin saves details of the request and the asset. The tracking mechanism itself does not send a request to the provider on the agent's behalf.

How a reference works

A service card explains the purpose, the input data, and the order of calling and getting the result. Specific models, parameters and limits should be taken from the current documentation of the available connection.

The distribution of roles and the [[run-environment|execution environment]] are described separately: a service is a callable capability, not a participant's role.

pages.title: Krea
pages.summary_html:
Krea provides tools for generating and processing images, upscaling and working with video. An agent can use a suitable capability of the service inside a Goblin task.

An example of use is processing a source image and then saving the result to the step's assets. For retouching, you need to choose a model that supports the required editing, and not treat any image enhancement as retouching.
pages.body_html:
Input data

Depending on the operation, you need a text task, a source image or other assets, and the parameters of the result. The agent finds out the available models and the parameter schema through the documentation or the tools of the connected tool.

Workflow

Prepare the inputs → register an external request → send the request through an available API or tool → save the job identifier → wait for completion → get the file → attach it to the step's result.

The Krea API supports job tracking; the available way to wait depends on the connection used. An accepted request does not yet mean a finished asset.

Sources

Service capabilities: the official Krea API page. Parameters of specific operations: Krea documentation. Prices and numeric limits are not fixed in this short reference.

pages.title: Kling
pages.summary_html:
Kling is a service for working with generative visual assets, including creating video from an image or a text task. In a run, it can perform a separate stage of preparing an asset.

The agent uses it through an available connection: an API, a CLI or another provided tool. The supported modes depend on this connection and the chosen model.
pages.body_html:
Input and result

To animate an image you need a source frame and a description of the motion; to generate from text, a description of the scene. The duration, format and extra parameters are chosen by the actual schema of the tool. The output is the asset received, not just a request number.

Workflow

Check that the needed operation is available → prepare the assets → register a request → call the service → save the external identifier → get the final file → hand in the step's result.

If a Kling model is called through another provider, the record must distinguish the actual provider from the model name. This matters for getting the result again and for recording the call.

Sources

Platform overview and integration routes: the official Kling documentation. The ability to create video from an image is also described in Kuaishou's material about Kling.

pages.title: Other services
pages.summary_html:
The catalog can be extended with other services that agents will need to do tasks. A new card describes a specific external capability and the way to use it in a run.

Before a service is chosen, no existing integration is assumed here. The name of a future tool and a promise of its result do not replace an available way to call it.
pages.body_html:
What to put in the card

The purpose of the service, the supported tasks, inputs, outputs, the way to connect and the official source of documentation. The external job identifier and getting the result after waiting are described separately.

Link with Goblin

A request is linked to a specific attempt. Files are saved as assets of the result. If the task requires a particular service, replacing it with another tool must be agreed within the task.

pages.title: Orca
pages.summary_html:
The leader and the worker work in separate Orca terminals. Tasks and replies are passed with the command orca terminal send; a block with a worker on the card is done by the worker, a block with the leader or an empty card is done by the leader itself.

Communication needs exact terminal addresses. The worker's address is passed in the task link; if it is missing, the leader creates a worker itself from the card. The Goblin instruction requires sending the message as one line and keeping the task address in the reply.
pages.body_html:
Short instruction for the leader

  1. Take your own address from ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE. The worker's address comes from the task link (&worker=term_…), exactly as given; do not guess addresses from names.
  2. If there is no worker address, the leader creates the worker itself in Orca: it takes the project's worker card (cli, model, effort; with no card, the same CLI as the leader's), creates a terminal with the command orca terminal create in its own worktree and waits until it is ready (tui-idle) before sending the briefing. After the run the terminal stays open or is closed according to the card parameter closeAfter.
  3. After begin and starting the watchdog, pass the briefing received through op=invite with the reply address (reply), then the exact line "task in file …".
  4. Wait for the addressed reply WORKER ANSWER: 137.3: … and pass it to done word for word; the server strips the prefix itself. After sending, end the turn and wait for an incoming message, not with the sleep command.

Short instruction for the worker

Read the task file in full, do the work and send the leader one line following the sample from the task, using the command from the briefing. The reply prefix: WORKER ANSWER:. The worker does not go to the Goblin server. After sending, end the turn and wait for the next task.

Delivery

The Goblin instruction uses --enter --wait-submit 4 --json and asks to read the receipt as a summary through jq (stages, requestId, provider, observation, warnings), without cutting it with grep, head or tail: without requestId a retry of the receipt is impossible, and whoever has lost it does not resend the message blindly.

If the receipt reports that the input was accepted but the start of the turn was not observed, one retry with the same command and the same --retry-request is allowed. There is no need to send a new copy of the message. If the warning remains after the retry, the leader does not send the task again and waits for the reply: if there is silence, the watchdog will wake it. In such a situation the worker sends the same reply once more with a new command without --retry-request (a duplicate is safe, the server recognizes it by the address), but no more than once. With agent_prompt_blocked the recipient has a window of the CLI itself open: human help is needed, after which the sending is repeated with --retry-request.

Source of the instruction

The instruction is not stored in an md file: the server builds it for the team's makeup and the folder's environment (lib/api/instructions.php: instrOrcaCommon() and instrOrcaLead() for the leader, instrWorkEnv() for the worker). The leader gets it in docs.run, the worker as the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md. The former связь-орка.md files are in instructions/old/simple/ and are not used. The availability of commands is determined by the installed environment.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/api/instructions.php (instrOrcaCommon, instrOrcaLead, instrWorkEnv), lib/api/simple.php (goInvite, goWorkerFile), md_backend/ru/progon.md 29.09.2026

pages.title: SendMessage
pages.summary_html:
In the accepted Goblin protocol the leader and the worker are separate Claude Code sessions on one machine. To discover participants and exchange messages, the tools ListAgents and SendMessage are used, if they are available in this environment; a message always consists of one line.

The agent card on a block only decides whether the block is done by a worker or by the leader itself; which session works as the worker is determined by its name, not by the card. The recipient's name must match exactly the name that the environment returned.
pages.body_html:
Short instruction for the leader

  1. Find the worker. The session name may be given in the task link (&worker=…); if it is missing, get the list of participants through ListAgents and take the session with the word "worker" in its name. If the needed session is not found or several fit, ask the person. Write the name exactly as ListAgents returned it.
  2. After begin and starting the watchdog, pass the op=invite reply word for word through SendMessage, then the line "task in file …". A block marked "do it yourself" is done by the leader itself.
  3. The reply arrives as an incoming message from the worker session; on notification, read it through ReadNotifications provided by the environment. Pass the last line of the result to done unchanged.
  4. Do not send the same message twice: SendMessage delivers by itself. No reply — wait for the watchdog, it will tell you when to ask the worker.

Short instruction for the worker

Read the task file in full and carry it out. Send one line following the sample through SendMessage to whoever sent the task; if the sender's name is not visible, find the leader session through ListAgents (its name contains "leader" or "lead"). Keep the block address and the attempt; one reply is sent once. The worker does not go to the Goblin server.

Source of the instruction

The instruction is not stored in an md file: the server builds it for the team's makeup and the folder's environment (lib/api/instructions.php: instrSendLead() for the leader, instrWorkEnv() for the worker). The leader gets it in docs.run, the worker as the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md. The former связь-sendmessage.md files are in instructions/old/simple/ and are not used. The tool names describe the protocol of this project and do not mean that every agent or every Claude Code installation has these tools.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/api/instructions.php (instrSendLead, instrWorkEnv), lib/api/simple.php (goInvite, goWorkerFile), md_backend/ru/progon.md 29.09.2026

pages.title: Subagents
pages.summary_html:
The leader launches workers with the means of its agent environment (in Claude Code, the Agent tool). Separate worker terminals are not required; the subagent's result returns to the leader through the delegation mechanism.

Agent cards on blocks do not apply here: who does the block — a subagent or the leader itself — is decided by the leader. It can create a worker for each task or continue one, if the tool supports it. A person choosing this environment serves as permission to launch subagents in the run.
pages.body_html:
Short instruction for the leader

  1. After begin and starting the watchdog, get the briefing through op=invite once for the current run.
  2. To a new subagent, pass two lines in the first message: the briefing word for word and "task in file …". When continuing the same worker (in Claude Code, SendMessage by its name or id), pass the next task as the line "task in file …".
  3. If the server has issued several independent blocks, a separate subagent can be assigned to each of them.
  4. Get the final message and pass its last addressed line to done word for word. A block that the leader decided to do itself, it does by the worker's rules and hands in its own reply through done.

Short instruction for the worker

Carry out the task you were given. As the last line of the final message, return the reply following the sample with the task address. Do not send it to anyone separately: the leader gets the result through the launch environment.

In this simple protocol the subagent does not run the run and does not contact the Goblin server on its own.

Source of the instruction

The instruction is not stored in an md file: the server builds it for the team's makeup and the folder's environment (lib/api/instructions.php: instrSubLead() for the leader, instrWorkEnv() for the worker). The leader gets it in docs.run, the worker as the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md, whose path is given in the briefing. The former связь-субагенты.md files are in instructions/old/simple/ and are not used. The specific launch tool is chosen by the capabilities of the leader's environment.
pages.source_note: checked against lib/api/instructions.php (instrSubLead, instrWorkEnv, instrSelfWork), lib/api/simple.php (goInvite, goSelf), md_backend/ru/progon.md 29.09.2026

pages.title: Jev
pages.summary_html:
Jev is used in Goblin for a semantic assessment of a result and for choosing a branch by a worded condition. It receives prepared data and returns an assessment, which the server handles by the run's rules.

Jev can work as an advisor or take part in an automatic decision. Exact checks are done by code, and insufficient confidence, incomplete data and a service error do not mean successful acceptance.
pages.body_html:
Purpose

Jev helps answer questions that are hard to reduce to a format check: whether a requirement of meaning is met, whether a forbidden statement is present, which branch matches the reply received. It does not do the worker's task and does not replace the leader.

Modes

runs.jevBehavior
offJev's semantic assessment is turned off; the other check rules apply.
advisorJev gives advice. With the basic reviewer human, the decision stays with the person; with formal, the result of the formal check is kept, and Jev's assessment adds to it.
judgeJev's assessment is used by the decision mechanism under the set rules. For a worded decision, this mode lets it choose a branch when the confidence is sufficient.

The Jev mode is stored separately from runs.judge, where human or formal is set. The explicit block property judge=human leaves the acceptance to a person.

What is passed for checking

The server collects the spec, the step's input, the text of the work or the contents of the submitted text file, the acceptance criteria accept and the rejection criteria reject. The criteria must be clear and verifiable from the data passed.

For example: accept the text if it describes the three benefits from the source task; reject it if it contains unconfirmed promises. For an image, a single text declaration "retouching done" is not enough: the current text check package does not prove the visual quality of the file.

Order of the decision

  1. The code performs the formal checks. Jev does not cancel an error found in the form, the calculations or the source data.
  2. If a semantic assessment is allowed, the server prepares an unchangeable package and calls Jev outside the project lock.
  3. The reply on the criteria is turned into a decision: accept, return or unsure. If the service is unavailable, unavailable is recorded.
  4. Before applying, the submission is checked to be up to date. A reply to data that has already changed is discarded; the state transition is done by the Goblin engine.

For an acceptance criterion, a high score supports acceptance, a low one — return. For a rejection criterion, a high score, on the contrary, points to a violation found. Intermediate and missing scores mean doubt. The thresholds are set by the implementation and the settings; a probability is not a guarantee of correctness.

Worded forks

For a decision, the condition and the input data are prepared. Jev chooses yes, no or unclear. The engine uses a definite branch only when the confidence is sufficient; otherwise it waits for a decision. Missing data does not turn into "no".

Short instruction for the leader

  1. Decide whether a recommendation or an automatic semantic assessment is needed, and choose the matching mode.
  2. Put the criteria in the block's task and make sure the input data and the result are available.
  3. Consider the reason for a return or a doubt. If data is lacking, clarify the task or pass the decision to a person.
  4. Keep the difference between Jev's advice, the formal check and the final acceptance.

Link with other mechanisms

The general rules are set out in [[run-review|Review and acceptance]]. The operation step.jev is a separate signal path: it gives an assessment and does not accept the result itself. The done command of the simple protocol confirms the leader's decision; it cannot be taken as evidence of a completed Jev check.

The description is based on the current Goblin modules. The existence of the article does not mean that access to the service is set up in a particular installation.

Creating a fork and its properties in the editor: [[frontend-tool-decision|Decision]].

pages.title: Editor state — public/src/core/state.js
pages.summary_html:
The module keeps the open project, folder, elements, selection and the selected run in page memory. It notifies the interface about changes through events.

This is the client-side view of the data. Confirmed records live in the database and arrive through the API; the module makes no network requests and draws no HTML.
pages.body_html:
public/src/core/state.js

Data and events

Objects and collections inside state are updated in place. elements holds the scheme objects, links holds the links, selection holds the selection; the steps of the selected run are kept separately in steps.

setScheme clears the collections and sorts the elements by type. putElement updates an object and sends element or links; dropElement clears the selection and reports the deletion. on returns an unsubscribe function, emit notifies subscribers synchronously.

rev belongs to the project; the run version belongs to the selected run. These counters must not be substituted for each other.
pages.source_note: public/src/core/state.js; checked against the code, without running a browser.

pages.title: API client — public/src/api/client.js
pages.summary_html:
The single point of network requests for the editor builds the addresses and command bodies for api.php. The project key is usually taken from the page address.

The client parses JSON, passes error messages to the interface and rejects an unsuccessful request. It does not decide anything about permissions or whether an edit is allowed.
pages.body_html:
public/src/api/client.js

Contract

get passes parameters through URLSearchParams; post and batch send JSON with the POST method. batch accepts an array of operations and extra fields, including opId. keepalive is supported when leaving the page.

talk requires a successful application-level ok response; network errors and JSON parsing errors also lead to a rejection. quietGet is used for background polling and returns null on failure.

hash, projectKey and folderId tie a request to navigation. talk does not automatically repeat an arbitrary write.
pages.source_note: public/src/api/client.js; checked against the code, without running a browser.

pages.title: Editor sync — public/src/api/sync.js
pages.summary_html:
The module loads the project, folder and run, then tracks server changes. The received data is passed to the editor state.

A late response from a previous folder or project must not replace the current screen. To ensure this, the loads use request counters and a context check.
pages.body_html:
public/src/api/sync.js

Loading

loadProject gets the project and its folders. loadFolder checks the load number and the project key; on a switch it resets the undo history, the selection and the run context. Then it updates the scheme and the list of launches.

loadRuns takes into account the preparedRun mark, the run pinned in the address and the activity of launches. loadRun does not accept a response from another run and does not roll a known version back to an older one.

Background reading updates the data through the API; reloading after a failure serves to reconcile with the server. It does not prove that a lost command was executed.
pages.source_note: public/src/api/sync.js; checked against the code, without running a browser.

pages.title: Edit queue — public/src/edit/scene.js
pages.summary_html:
The module creates and changes elements locally, records actions in the undo history and collects server operations into a queue.

Saving is done in batches. A visible result of a local edit does not yet mean that the server accepted it.
pages.body_html:
public/src/edit/scene.js

Saving

push sets dirty and schedules sending in 500 ms. flush sends only one batch at a time, and new edits accumulate separately. The batch is assigned an opId.

A new object first has a negative ID. After the server responds, the temporary ID is replaced with the real one; the selection, the arrow ends and the container contents are updated. The response is applied only to the project and folder the batch was sent from.

On an error the module calls resync. The current code does not store the sent batch in a durable queue and does not repeat it automatically with the same opId. This must not be described as a full offline mode.

The undo history is recorded in the edit commands. Property changes are merged with the previous values; removing a value is passed explicitly.
pages.source_note: public/src/edit/scene.js; checked against the code, without running a browser.

pages.title: Editor startup — public/src/main.js
pages.summary_html:
The entry module connects the panels, the canvas, the mobile interface and background updates. It sets the page startup order.

Domain rules stay in the specialized modules. main.js links their events to data loading and error display.
pages.body_html:
public/src/main.js

Sequence

First the error handlers are registered and the interface elements are initialized. Then the project and folder are loaded, after which the selected display mode is mounted.

The resync event rereads the current folder. beforeunload tries to send the queue with keepalive and warns about unsaved changes. hashchange handles a folder switch.
pages.source_note: public/src/main.js; checked against the code, without running a browser.

pages.title: How the editor works in the browser
pages.summary_html:
The editor consists of JavaScript modules: state, network client, edit commands and views. They work with shared project objects.

The interface first reflects an action locally, then receives confirmation from the server. So the state of the screen and the saved data must be told apart.
pages.body_html:
Path of a change

User action → edit command → queue → API → server transaction → response → update of client identifiers and revision. The server is responsible for rules and permissions; the skin is responsible for presentation.

When the folder changes, an old response must not change the new screen. On a failure the data is reread from the server. A local undo does not replace the server log.
tags: How the editor works in the browser
pages.source_note: public/src/main.js, core/state.js, api/client.js, api/sync.js, edit/scene.js.

pages.title: Save failures and conflicts
pages.summary_html:
When a batch fails, the editor rereads the server data. This brings back a consistent view, but does not guarantee that every local intention of the user is kept.

The server supports checking expected revisions and recognizing repeats. The presence of these mechanisms in the API does not mean that every client uses them fully.
pages.body_html:
Current contract

batchGuard checks ifRev and ifFolderRev when the client passed these conditions. The current flush in edit/scene.js passes opId, but does not set these revision conditions.

If the response is cut off, the client does not know the result of the write. Reread the folder and the log before repeating the action manually. The interface has no separate confirmed durable recovery queue.

If the server forbids a meaningful edit because of an active run, first stop that run or give up the change. Repeating the same forbidden command does not resolve the conflict.

pages.title: Mobile skin
pages.summary_html:
"Mobile" is the Goblin skin for phones and tablets. The canvas takes most of the screen, and the panels are gathered in a slide-out menu. Cards keep only the frame and the name; details open on request.

The skin works with the same projects and data. On first open on a device with a primary touch pointer, it is chosen automatically if the browser has no other skin saved yet.
pages.body_html:
Screen layout

The header has the ☰ menu, the name of the current folder, undo and redo. The menu has the tabs "Tools", "Folders", "Block", "Assets", "Run", "AI" and "More". The "More" tab has a way back to the desktop version.

Tapping an object selects it and shows a bottom action bar: properties, spec for the objects that support it, and delete. For an arrow from a decision, the buttons of the "YES" and "NO" branches are available. The properties panel does not open automatically on every selection.

Gestures

One finger moves the canvas, two move and scale it. To move a block, hold it and drag. A tool is placed by tapping an empty spot; an arrow connects two blocks selected one after another. Double-tapping an empty spot shows the whole scheme.

Features and limits

The mobile drawing set has block, decision, gateway, arrow and note. The working view is the canvas; the list, the hierarchy and the 3D projection are not enabled here. Details hidden on the card are kept in the object data.

The camera keeps the names readable, so a long scheme sometimes has to be scrolled. When Visual Viewport is supported, the windows take the height of the on-screen keyboard into account.

pages.title: Lost connection and unknown command result
pages.summary_html:
If no response came, the command cannot be considered either executed or canceled. First restore the connection and read the state of the same run.

A new launch or a reset is not a way to check the previous command. They may create different work or delete the history.
pages.body_html:
Order of actions

  1. Write down the project, the run identifier, the step and attempt, the command name and the repeat key, if there was one.
  2. After the connection is restored, read run.state with the exact run and full=1; refine the history through run.log. In the simple path, use where for the same run.
  3. Match the result with the step state. For an external service, additionally find out the state of the saved job ID before repeating a paid call.
  4. If the command supports repeating and its outcome is still needed, use the same key and the same body. Do not replace the key with a new one.
  5. If it is ambiguous, stop further issuing and hand the situation to a human.

run.state is a state read; run.advance can move execution forward. To find out the result first, use a read.

Do not call begin, run.reset or run.prepare as a means of diagnosing an existing run.
tags: Lost connection and unknown command result
pages.source_note: lib/engine/state.php; lib/api/simple.php; lib/engine/lock.php.

pages.title: Repeating a command without running it again
pages.summary_html:
A repeated delivery and a new command are different events. For operations through engineCommand, commandId is used; for edit batches, opId and the opScope scope.

The protection works only in the handlers that use the corresponding mechanism. It must not be carried over automatically to any API address.
pages.body_html:
Run commands

Save commandId before the first send. Repeat the same body with the same key and the same access context. Other arguments under the same key cause a conflict.

For a worker with an agent token, the exact step must be given. The repeat scope takes into account the participant and the target step/run.

If the response contains replay_secret_unavailable and committed=true, the command is already committed, but the secret is not issued again. Use the recovery from the response; do not treat this error as a cancellation of the command.

Batches and the simple path

For a batch, opId, opScope and the original list of ops are saved. New content needs a new key.

In the simple path, save the response address "block.attempt" and pass the worker response on without retelling it. Its protection against a stale result is not a universal commandId for all GET commands.
tags: Repeating a command without running it again
pages.source_note: lib/engine/lock.php; lib/api/batch.php; lib/api/simple.php.

pages.title: Lost or revoked token
pages.summary_html:
The token defines the participant's authority and context. An access error does not mean the run has to be started again.

Before recovery, find out whether the run is open and which attempt is currently active. Previous tokens must not be used after a reissue.
pages.body_html:
leader

  1. Get the run state through the allowed project access.
  2. For running or paused, a user with write permission calls run.attach. The operation is allowed for the human role; admin access is governed by the general rules.
  3. Save the new secret and the open steps from the response. The previous run token is revoked; the run state does not change.
  4. For a closed run, read the result; do not reissue the session.

worker

The leader or a human calls step.reissue only for issued/running. A new step token is issued, the old one is revoked and the previous session is dropped. This is the same attempt, not a new task issue.

Before continuing, stop the old process, so that two workers do not change one output file. Revoking the token does not end the external process by itself. Pass secrets through the chosen environment channel; do not publish them in the documentation.
pages.source_note: lib/engine/runs.php::runAttach; lib/engine/steps.php::stepReissue; lib/api/router.php.

pages.title: Jev is unavailable or unsure
pages.summary_html:
No response from Jev and insufficient confidence are not a positive check of the result. The cause must be read in the run state and history.

Continuing depends on the check mode and the actual step state. A human decision must be explicit and refer to the current attempt.
pages.body_html:
Order of actions

  1. Read run.state and the log: tell apart network, timeout, request limit, key error and insufficient confidence.
  2. If the key is the problem, fix the access settings; if it is a temporary failure, restore the service. Do not send quick endless repeats.
  3. Make sure the worker result and the attempt have not changed. When the service is restored, request the next move through run.advance, if the chosen way of leading allows it.
  4. If a human is needed, check the result itself and accept/return it; for a decision, choose the branch through the intended command step.decide.

step.jev gives a score, but is not an acceptance command. Turning Jev off does not confirm the quality of the work. A formal result error must not be considered fixed after the mode is changed.

If a visual assessment of an image is required, the agent's text report does not replace viewing the image.
pages.source_note: lib/engine/judges/jev.php; lib/engine/advance.php; lib/ai/jev.php.

pages.title: Publishing and updating links
pages.summary_html:
The only active source of the main articles is content.json. The publisher publish.php moves it into MariaDB, keeping the identifiers of existing articles and of the links in use.

Callouts are stored separately in the database and do not disappear when articles are published. The archive of the old files is kept for history, but does not take part in publishing.
pages.body_html:
How to update an article

  1. Change the record with the needed slug in content.json: the title, the short and the detailed description, references, tags and metadata.
  2. Write internal links as [[slug|label]]. references holds the extra technical links that are needed regardless of the text.
  3. Run php md_backend/документация/publish.php --page=slug. For related new articles, publish the whole file without arguments.
  4. The result checks are done separately, on the user's instruction.

Consistency

The publisher works in a transaction and locks the articles in a common order. Links from the text, references and callouts form the current graph. A link is removed only when it is no longer used anywhere; the remaining links keep their IDs.

The links from a plan to the list are computed from the existing future_plan. After a callout is deleted or its type changes, the service link disappears unless another plan or an explicit article link holds it.

The old addresses publish-*.php and import*.php are redirected to the single publisher. They no longer read the old JSON. The archive-before-unified-publisher files are an archive, not a second source.

Do not change the main texts directly in the database: the next publish will restore content.json. Deleting an article is not done by the publisher automatically.

pages.title: Statuses and approval of materials
pages.summary_html:
The status of an article shows how its content should be understood: as a proposal, an approved requirement or a description of implemented behavior.

The status of an agent callout reflects a separate decision on that callout. Color and author name alone do not mean that its content is approved.
pages.body_html:
Article

ValueMeaning
proposedProposed: the decision is still being discussed.
approvedApproved: the target requirement is agreed; implementation is not guaranteed.
implementedImplemented: the behavior is reflected in the code. This is not a mark that tests passed.
NULLStatus not defined: the old material is not yet classified.

reviewed_at is the date of checking against the sources, source_note is the basis and the limits of the check. Do not update this date for a change of formatting alone. If an article mixes requirements and implementation, split its text or move the future idea into a callout.

Callout

approval accepts pending, approved or rejected. A new callout waits for approval. Changing the text, type or author resets the previous decision; changing the display order keeps it.

The decision is recorded separately through review-callout.php with --id, --decision and --by. The agent does the approval only after an explicit decision by the user. The reviewed_by signature is not an authentication system.

Approving a correction does not rewrite the main text automatically. To include it in the article, a separate edit of content.json is needed; the callout stays visible with its own status.
