pages.title: Run architecture audit — 23.09.2026
pages.summary_html:
An analysis of the current implementation and documentation showed that the core of the run — steps, marks and server transitions — works on a proven scheme with a loop, a branch and a merge. The main difficulties come from differences between protocols and data contracts.

The test confirmed an extra starting block being issued when an entry is chosen explicitly, and different output folders in packages. Proposals for simplification are prepared separately. They do not change the current engine and await agreement.
pages.body_html:
Scope of the analysis

Checked: how a launch works, issuing and acceptance of steps, transition marks, decision conditions, loop, merge, worker context, command repeat, recovery, Jev and state display. The materials of the "Run" section were compared with the current handlers. Before this report was added, the section contained 30 articles, including nested ones.

The grounds for the conclusions are separated: test — an observation in an executed HTTP run; code — reading a specific implementation; hypothesis — an expected risk or gain that needs separate measurement. The results are in the [[run-audit-test-2026-09-23|test protocol]]. The browser and the mobile interface were not checked.

How a run works now

LayerResponsibilityMain sources
Input commandsThe full JSON API, the text simple protocol and the CLI use one storage, but choose different execution rules.api/router.php, api/simple.php, cli/engine.php
Life cycleCreating runs, pause, resume, stop, finish; changes under the project lock.engine/runs.php, engine/lock.php
PlanningLoading the graph, computing the available entries, issuing work, branches, finishing. A move is limited to 50 actions.engine/advance.php, ready.php, graph.php, finish.php
Transitionsrun_marks stores the arrow, the source attempt, the pass number and the consumer attempt. join=all waits for all direct inputs; the back input works separately.engine/marks.php
Executionrun_steps stores the attempt, the executor, the state, the result and the times; the package collects the spec, assets and predecessors.engine/steps.php, package.php, vars.php
CheckingFormal rules, a human decision and Jev. The network call to Jev is moved outside the lock, and the response is checked against the original state.engine/checks/*, engine/judges/*, advance.php
Artifacts and servicesassets/asset_links — assets; run_jobs — accounting of external requests. Registering a request does not call the external service by itself.assets/*, engine/jobs.php, checks/files.php
Observationrun.state — a snapshot; run_events — a sequence of events; run.paint — display. The browser waits for the state, then asks for the highlight.engine/state.php, events.php, paint.php; public/src/run/paint.js

What to keep

  • Separate entities for the scheme, the run and the attempt: changing the execution status must not rewrite the block's spec.
  • Marks with origin: they provide merges, loops and protection against reusing an input.
  • The shared project lock and atomic writing of commands. The lock can be narrowed to a run only after compatibility with scheme edits is proven.
  • Checking rights and step ownership on the server; pinning work to the worker session.
  • The difference between submitting and accepting. A formal check without a substantive basis returns unsure, except for an explicitly set trust_form.
  • The state version and a separate event cursor: these are different values.
  • Jev protection through fingerprint and nonce, checking that the response is current and no network inside a transaction.
  • Protection of dependencies on reset. stepNextAttempt takes reset events into account: a deleted attempt number is not issued again.

Confirmed discrepancies and points of complexity

Priority / basisObservationConsequence and recommended action
P1 · test r3 + coderun.start with from=27 returned start 27, but the engine issued 27.1 and 28.1 at the same time.The choice of entry does not limit the initial issue. Keep the chosen entry in the run and use it in readyList. Details and evidence are in the protocol.
P1 · test r1/r2 + codestepPackage.outDir in the full API is workDir/out; the simple task points to out/rN. runOutDir already computes the folder of a specific run.The contract of the result path differs. Use one path calculator; the migration must keep access to files that already exist. Overwriting files was not modeled in the test.
P1 · coderun.start does not call folderPrecheck. begin calls it, then does the preparation and creation in separate parts.A check in the interface may become stale by the time of the launch. Combine the graph check, fixing the entry and creating the run in one command handler; do the file actions in a controlled way. A race of concurrent begins was not reproduced.
P1 · code and confirmed protocol differencegoDone saves the response directly and calls stepAcceptDo; step.submit goes through checkSubmit and the further check mechanism.done is trusted acceptance by the leader, not a synonym of submit. Keep this ability as an explicit policy and show the basis of acceptance. New checks must not be enabled automatically for old schemes.
P2 · test r1/r2The numeric condition n < 2 in utility was computed by code, and with driver=lead it was passed to Jev.The way of communication changes the way of deciding. Separate the branching policy from the transport; keep the current mode for old schemes.
P2 · codemanual/utility/lead mix the way of leading and the semantics. JSON run.start/run.update offer manual/utility, while begin creates lead.Switching between protocols can change behavior. A visible execution profile and compatible command adapters are needed.
P2 · codestepResetDo deletes the attempt row after checking the descendants; again calls this reset. The reset event keeps the address.The log does not replace the fully deleted attempt data. Consider keeping the canceled version, without losing the existing ability to roll back dependencies.
P2 · codeAfter each action advanceRun rereads the graph, steps and marks; readyList reads the free marks again; checks may repeat while building the state.A candidate for query optimization. First measure the number of SQL queries and the lock time, then reuse the graph inside one transaction. The speedup is not measured yet.
P2 · coderun.stateWait polls the version in the DB about every 150 ms; the browser separately gets run.paint.With many clients, extra requests and busy PHP processes are possible. First measure the load and combine the consistent response data; introduce separate infrastructure only if needed.
P2 · codeSeparate task forms: stepPackage and goTaskText/goInputs. In simple the path restores the predecessors' text through decisions and gateways.A single package structure will reduce the risk of input mismatch; the text and JSON must become views of this structure. The verbatim text of the response and the choice of actual predecessors must not be lost.
P2 · codestep.pass saves the accepted gateway attempt and returns the target folder. The engine2 graph remains the graph of the current folder.The transition must not be described as an already implemented automatic execution of a child scheme. Describe the border of the current behavior; design the nested run separately.
P2 · codeThe text protocol performs changing operations through GET; commandId is not applied to all simple commands.Propose POST for changing commands and a stable delivery identifier. Support the old links with an adapter for the transition period. This is a contract improvement, not a proven incident.

Documentation audit

MaterialWhat needs clarifyingBasis
[[run-start|Preparing and starting]]Archiving the whole out is described as current. The current workDirClean keeps out/rN, cleans service/steps and moves individual results that lie outside out.Body of engine/prepare.php:workDirClean; the top comment of the file is also outdated.
[[run-start|Choosing the start]]The advice to give from when there are several entries does not warn about the reproduced issue of both entries.Test r3 and engine/runs.php, ready.php.
[[run-graph|Executable graph]] and [[run-jev|Jev]]driver=lead must be stated explicitly: in it even the decision formula goes through Jev. The general rule "a numeric condition is computed by code" is not precise enough.Two runs of the same scheme and advanceDecide.
[[run-task|Package and result]]Exact contracts of the output folders and of the package differences are needed; for now the description is mostly general.Packages r1/r2.
[[run-recovery|Recovery]]again must be told apart from returning for rework and from reissuing a token: it deletes the attempt through stepResetDo. The address is not reused after deletion.simple.php:goAgain; steps.php:stepResetDo/stepNextAttempt.
[[run-protocols|Protocols]]The CLI table is useful as a reference, but does not explain the differences in acceptance, branching, access and repeats. A compact table of contracts is needed.Comparison of simple/API/CLI.
[[run-scenarios|Scenarios]]The examples should add the execution profile, join, the back-arrow flag, the attempt limit, the exact form of input/output and the expected finish.A scenario by itself does not set a specific engine setting.
[[run-environment|Run environment]]For allowed execution of both roles in the current terminal there is no separate explicit option in run_env. In the test the environment was left unselected; Orca was not launched.folders.php:RUN_ENVS and the actual test environment.

The main articles were not rewritten within this audit: the clarifications found are collected for agreement. The existing description of the differences between done/submit, of Jev uncertainty and of the borders of run.prepare/run.reset is already useful and must be kept.

Conclusion

The working core is server execution of the graph with saved attempts and marks. The greatest benefit will come from agreeing the contracts of the input, the task package and the acceptance, then separating the execution policies from the transport. Rewriting the whole engine is not justified by the results of this audit.

The specific scheme and the sequence of changes are proposed separately: [[future-run-simplification|Simplifying the run architecture]]. There are no measurable promises of speedup: the current tests checked the correctness of small schemes, not performance.

pages.title: Test runs and evidence
pages.summary_html:
One test scheme was run through the full API with formal acceptance and through the simple protocol with Jev's decisions. Both runs ended with the result c=34. A short diagnostic of start-point selection was also run.

Positive transitions and several rejections were checked: wrong arithmetic, a retry key conflict, a different session worker and a stale reply address. This article gives the exact limits of the test, the run numbers and where the evidence is kept.
pages.body_html:
Conditions

Date: September 23, 2026. Server: local Goblin, real HTTP calls to api.php, live PHP and MariaDB. Both roles were played by the current agent from the terminal, one after the other. No other agents, Orca or browser were started. The test worker's card has CLI=other, run_env left empty.

A separate project audita061ebb4dcc5 (id 7036) was created. The original user schemes were not changed. The main folder is 10751, the diagnostic one is 10752. All three runs that were created finished. Issuing two parallel blocks in the test does not mean two processes worked at the same time: the blocks were done one after another by a single agent.

Test scheme

10 Start → 11 n=0 → 12 n=n+1 → 13 n<2?
                          ↑         │ yes, back arrow
                          └─────────┘
                                    │ no
                                    ↓
                              14 pass n
                              ↙           ↘
                       15 a=n+10       16 b=n+20
                              ↘           ↙
                              17 c=a+b (join=all)

Block 12 allows six attempts, to check separately the return of faulty work and two passes of the loop. Every work block contains a spec and expr; the decision contains cond. The pre-check of the main scheme returned ready=true with no remarks.

Results

RunModeActual outcome
r1 · id 1982utility / formal / Jev offdone; 11 attempts: 10 accepted, 1 returned. Result c=34; 10 marks, 0 free.
r2 · id 1983lead / human / Jev judge; begin → task → donedone; 10 accepted attempts. Result c=34; 10 marks, 0 free. Two actual Jev replies.
r3 · id 1984utility / formal / Jev off; diagnostic two startsfrom=27, but 27.1 and 28.1 were issued. The mismatch is confirmed; both test tasks were then completed, the run is done.

Checks in r1

SituationObservation
Repeated submission of n=0 with the same commandId and bodyThe earlier command result for the same step came back. No extra attempt appeared.
Changed body with the same commandIdHTTP 409: the key is taken by another command.
A different session tries to take a step that is already takenHTTP 409 with code2=step_claimed. This is a sequential conflict of two sessions, not a load test of a race.
Deliberately wrong submission n=99 instead of n=1Attempt 12.1 returned; 12.2 issued with the same input n=0.
Corrected submission n=112.2 accepted; decision 13.1 chose yes; the new attempt 12.3 got n=1.
Next submission n=2Decision 13.2 chose no; the loop ended.
BranchingAfter 14.1 was accepted, 15.1 and 16.1 were issued at the same time.
MergeAfter one branch, block 17 was not issued. After the second it was issued with a=12 and b=22.
Pause and resumerun.pause gave paused, run.resume gave running for the same run. The work went on. Submission right during the pause was not checked separately.
Finishc=34 accepted formally; finish wrote done. The result was read through run.state and compared with the tables.

Checks in r2

The simple begin created driver=lead. The spec and inputs were read through task&text=1. Replies came back with the address of the block and attempt; the leader passed them on without changes. The input of the final block held the verbatim results of both branches: a=12 and b=22.

A repeat of 12.1: n=1 after 12.2 was issued was recognized as already accepted and did not change the new attempt. The contradicting old reply 12.1: n=999 was rejected with HTTP 409. Then the correct reply 12.2 was accepted.

Jev was really called: event 24633 gave yes (score 0.98; took_ms=842), event 24645 — no (1.00; took_ms=621). These are the service's scores in specific replies, not a measured accuracy of the model. The total time reported for these two calls is 1463 ms; it cannot be read as a speedup that the refactoring guarantees.

Diagnostic of the chosen start in r3

In a separate folder, two unrelated starting blocks were created — 27 and 28, each with the spec "Return x=1". The run.start request passed from=27. The start field of the reply said 27, but advance.did contained open for 27.1 and 28.1; the following snapshot confirmed both as issued.

The cause, by the code: from is used when checking and building the start reply, but the chosen start is not saved as a readiness restriction of engine2. readyList allows all starting nodes when there is no special starter. The diagnostic tasks were completed so as not to leave an active run. This is not a fix of the defect.

Limits of the check

Not checked: engine1, concurrent load, a network break during commit, a PHP/DB restart, expiry and reissue of tokens, stopping an external process, a gateway with a separate child run, file uploads, paid Krea/Kling generations, an undefined/failed Jev reply, the interface and rendering delays. The tests do not prove that all variants of Goblin are fully correct.

Evidence

The folder md_backend/документация/audits/2026-09-23-run/ holds the HTTP log without tokens, the final snapshots, a sample of steps/marks/events and the structures of the five tables, the original version of the articles and the checksums of the files. The file manifest fixes the version of the corpus; it does not mean that every line of every file was checked.

Main scheme: scheme text. Result of r1: API state; result of r2: API state. These addresses read data; they do not start a new run.

pages.title: Simplifying the run architecture
pages.summary_html:
The proposal is to keep the server engine with marks, but to unify the start, the task package and the change commands. The rules of acceptance and branch choice should be set explicitly and keep their meaning when the text protocol, JSON or CLI changes.

First the confirmed mismatches of the chosen start and of the output paths are fixed, then the duties of the modules are separated and the load is measured. Compatibility with existing schemes and runs is a mandatory condition of every stage.
pages.body_html:
Status of the proposal

This is a draft of changes for approval. The engine implementation was not changed during the audit. The basis is the [[run-audit-2026-09-23|architecture analysis]] and the [[run-audit-test-2026-09-23|three completed runs]]. Priority P1 means fixing a contract or correctness; P2 — simplification and later optimization.

Proposed scheme

Editor / CLI / text commands
                 ↓ request adapter
     Command + permissions + commandId + profile
                 ↓
   Run service — one change transaction
                 ↓
   Graph + attempts + marks → next action
                 ↓
   Check / human decision / worker task
                 ↓
   Events + assets + state version
                 ↓
   One consistent snapshot for the interface and agents

External Jev call: reservation → call outside the transaction
                 → freshness check → recording the result

PHP, MariaDB and the current mark model are kept. The proposal is to put the module boundaries in order inside the existing application. Separate microservices, a queue and a new database are not needed for this.

Six boundaries of responsibility

PartWhat it doesWhat the rest of the system gets
AdaptersParse HTTP, CLI and text commands; check the shape of the request and format the reply.One set of domain commands instead of several implementations of start and submission.
Command serviceChecks permissions, the target run/step, commandId, freshness of the version; records the change and events.Common errors and command result; a repeat does not repeat the work.
PlannerFrom a snapshot of the graph, attempts and marks, decides the allowed action.Issue, review, branch, wait, finish with a reason. No HTTP and no network calls.
Execution policiesDefine acceptance and the way a decision is resolved.An explicit basis: formal, human, lead or Jev, kept in the history.
Packages and assetsBuild the TaskPackage, define paths, link inputs/outputs and external requests.One data structure with JSON, text and file views.
Reading and observingBuild consistent state, events and highlighting from the saved data.A passive snapshot with no accidental advancing; a separate command for a move.

Explicit execution profile

Separate the independent settings. Transport is responsible for the form of communication; environment — for starting and connecting the workers; acceptance — for whether a result may be used; decision policy — for the choice of branch. Choosing a terminal must not quietly switch arithmetic to a probabilistic estimate.

Proposed fieldExample valuesCompatibility
transportjson, text, cliChanges the representation and delivery, not the meaning of the command.
environmentorca, sendmessage, subagents, locallocal means agreed execution in the current terminal. The roles are kept as separate actions.
acceptancehuman, formal, lead, semanticA trusted done is kept as acceptance=lead; old runs do not get formal acceptance after the fact.
branch_policyexpression, semantic, human, expression_then_semanticThe existing driver=lead is moved to semantic. For new numeric schemes, expression can be chosen explicitly.
presentationno delay or a set delayKeep the current display pause; changing it must not replace the business pause of the run.

This is a conceptual model, not a demand to add five columns right away. At the first stage it is enough to compute the profile from the existing fields and show it in the task, the state and the log. Changing the stored scheme is a separate migration.

Priority plan

StageChangeDone when
1 · P1Save the chosen start and apply it at the first issue.With two starts, from picks exactly one; the chosen branch and the finishing rules agree. A scheme with a starter keeps working.
1 · P1One outDir through runOutDir; a common task package.JSON and text point to one folder out/rN; earlier assets and links are reachable. The same actual inputs in all views.
1 · P1A common start for begin and run.start: check, allowed start, scheme version, creation.No half-started scheme on a preparation error; two simultaneous starts do not create two active runs of one folder.
2 · P2Separate the profile and the submit/review commands, keeping the trusted leader mode.The same profile gives the same decisions over different transports. The history shows who accepted the work and by which rules.
2 · P2Make the delivery ID mandatory for the new changing interface; wrap the old GETs in an adapter.A repeat is safe, a body conflict is explicit; losing a reply with a secret has a documented recovery path.
2 · P2Merge the task structure and the description of waiting reasons.No contradicting path/input fields; instead of parsing wait_for, a machine client gets reason_code and the linked step/element.
3 · P2Reuse an unchanged graph within a transaction; remove repeated reads of marks.SQL, lock duration and p50/p95 are compared on the same schemes. States, transitions and restrictions match.
3 · P2One consistent observation reply; history pagination and a limit on the growing context.Switching a folder and a late reply do not bring back the old state; events are not lost. Old API consumers keep working.
4 · after a separate decisionKeep cancelled versions of attempts; isolate the legacy adapter.Rollback by dependencies and reading of engine1 are kept; removing the old path is possible only after taking stock of the consumers.

What must not be lost in the simplification

FunctionWhat must be kept
GraphStart, block, yes/no decision, branching, join=all/any, back arrows, attempt limits and dead-end detection.
StepsIssue, session claim, submission, acceptance, return, error, cancel, manual decision, token recovery and dependent rollback.
AcceptanceFormal checks, human, trusted lead, Jev advisor/judge, unsure/unavailable and the impossibility of accepting a stale reply.
DataSpecs, verbatim input replies, variables and their conflicts, files, origin of results, accounting of external jobs and limits.
ObservationVersion, event cursor, waiting reasons, log, report, highlighting, pause settings and reading of finished runs.
CompatibilityCurrent schemes and attempt addresses, simple/API/CLI, environments, the history of engine1; the gateway keeps its current behavior.

A simpler scheme for the task author

For new schemes, offer one order: get input → do the work → check the result → choose the next stage → save the outcome. Set a numeric condition by a formula, a semantic one by a separate Jev criterion, a human decision explicitly. Join parallel tasks with all, alternative branches with any or separate outputs. A loop needs a back arrow and a limit.

A check can stay a block rule; drawing an extra check card for every task is not required. A decision is needed where the route changes. The teaching test scheme contains an extra work block 14 only to show branching clearly; in a real scheme it can be replaced by a suitable structure of transitions after a separate check of how a decision behaves with several outputs. Removing it automatically is not proposed.

How to change the documentation

Fix the actual mismatches in run-start, run-graph, run-task and run-recovery; keep the details in the matching article without repeating them in the parent section. In the protocols, add a table of differences in meaning. For each scenario, give the profile, inputs, outputs, acceptance rules and the sign of a successful end.

All proposals remain plans until approved and implemented. The user's next decision is to choose the stages; the performance check and regression tests of the changes are to be agreed separately. A guarantee that no functionality is lost can be given only from the results of those tests, not from the refactoring scheme.

pages.title: The Goblin utility: analysis and return to service
pages.summary_html:
It makes sense to update the goblin utility and bring it back as a programmatic dispatcher of the run. It already has a suitable base: the engine2 mode calls the server run.advance, gets tasks, keeps the worker context and watches events.

Putting it back into service as it is now would be premature. The old loop must be separated, the packages and rules aligned with the simple path, and task delivery and recovery after failures finished. The main expected gain is fewer mechanical calls to the AI leader; the size of the saving has not been measured yet.
pages.body_html:
Status and basis of the analysis

In readme.md, instructions/old/утилита.md and the section "Goblin utility — rework for high-load runs" of the file md_backend/ru/на_будущее.md, the utility is marked as a postponed path. The historical date of the last use in these documents is 21.09.2026; it is a project record, not a fact that was checked again.

The architecture conclusions below are based on the current code of bin/goblin, bin/goblin.php, lib/cli/*.php and the server handlers. The utility was not run in this work, and no new tests were made. The runs of the previous audit were done with direct HTTP requests and do not confirm that the CLI itself works.

What the utility consists of

ModuleActual responsibilityAssessment
bin/goblin → bin/goblin.phpThe wrapper finds PHP, the single entry point parses the command and picks a handler.Keep the name and the public entry. The server keeps checking permissions.
lib/cli/net.phpHTTP, environment, token choice, worker session, step cache 0600, errors, keys of individual commands.A good base for the client; it needs a stable context of an unfinished command.
lib/cli/engine.phpdrive2 calls run.advance; state/history/report read the result; work2 gets step.take; go takes a decision and continues leading.The base of the updated dispatcher. The transition rules are already on the server.
lib/cli/lead.phpLeader commands plus the old drive: local reading of conditions, opens and acceptance through accept-clean.Separate the API commands from the legacy behavior, without dropping compatibility right away.
lib/cli/worker.phpGetting a task, note, job, submit, fail; exact scope for a long token; submit --next.Keep the working API, align the package and repeats.
lib/cli/launch.phpTask file, starting a CLI from a template, a background process or waiting, printing a message to the worker.Partial delivery. It needs an explicit start contract and confirmation of receipt.
lib/cli/watch.php; bin/watch.phpWatching run.get, timeouts of work and acceptance, log; when the process ends, it notifies the leader.Keep as an observer after states and errors are made clearer.
bin/lead-watch.shPolling where&short for the simple path.This is a separate mechanism; the where it calls can advance the engine.
lib/cli/help.php; instructions/oldHints and old instructions.Update together with the command contract. Part of the text lags behind the implementation.

Two different loops inside one utility

Old drive: reads run.get, looks at submissions, calls acceptance when accept-clean is allowed, reads the conditions of decisions locally and sends open commands. Here part of the execution rules lives in the client.

drive2: calls run.advance, reads events and state, keeps waiting or returns the reason for stopping. Acceptance, branch choice and issuing happen on the server. This is the boundary that suits the new version.

cmdDriveRoute picks the new path for a specific engine2 run, but without an exact run or a leader token it falls back to the old drive. So the old mode's ability to watch the whole project cannot be taken for a ready modern dispatcher of many runs.

What stops the utility from coming back now

Observation from the codeWhat it meansProposal
drive2 does not call launch.Advancing the scheme and starting a real worker are separate actions. One drive command is not enough for full automatic execution.Add an issue dispatcher with the states "task issued", "delivered", "taken by the worker".
launch --mode subagent/terminal prints a message; orca returns "not done yet".The mode names do not prove that an automatic transport exists.Implement adapters only for tools that are really available. Subagents of the built-in agent cannot be started by an arbitrary PHP command without a provided bridge.
Background launch uses nohup; there is no stable record of the process and no confirmation that the task was received on this path.After a crash it is impossible to tell reliably a lost start reply from the absence of a worker.Keep the delivery ID, run/step/session, the confirmation status and the process/session of the environment. Check with the server and the environment before repeating.
commandId is added in start and open; cmdSubmit does not pass it. A random key is kept in the process memory.The server's protection from repeats is not used by all commands. A new process will not restore the earlier key automatically.Save the original body and ID before sending; restoring the same command must use the earlier values.
workTake --raw prints service lines before the JSON.Such output cannot be taken as a single JSON document without extra parsing.Provide a clean --json, diagnostics in stderr and a format version. Keep the text output for people.
watch, in the branch of one run, treats unauthorized/not_found as closing and returns 0.Revoked access to a live run may look like completion. This is a conclusion from a code branch, not a reproduced failure.Confirm closing by the state; report the impossibility of reading it as "outcome unknown".
lead-watch.sh calls where; goWhere calls goMove before handling short.The observer of the simple path is not fully passive, despite the comment about no changes.Do passive observation through run.state; leave the active move as an explicit duty of the dispatcher.
The meaning of exit=0 differs: work — work taken or everything finished; go — a submission shown or the end; watch — also a stopped/failed run.One shell code is not enough for automatic control of the whole set of commands.Add a single structured outcome; write down the compatibility of the existing codes explicitly.
stepPackage and the simple task differ; the simple path explicitly puts the description above the spec and out/rN.Bringing the CLI back must not quietly change the tasks of existing schemes.One server package with a priority rule, assets, an exact address and a results folder.
cmdToken with a numeric --id prints r before this number.The numeric DB ID and the local run label rN are different values; the instruction may name a different run.Take the run label from the server reply, keep the ID and the run label separately.
Background start relies on a shell template, CLI availability and a shared file system.An HTTP connection to a remote Goblin does not by itself make the server's packageFile and workDir local.Describe local placement as the first supported mode; design remote delivery of packages and files separately.
The history hint says that the package holds no history; stepPackage fills earlier.The help may describe the size of the context and the storage/service paths wrongly.Give a versioned help for the current contract; pass the worker the needed dependencies, keeping access to the full history on request.

Proposed reconstruction

Person / editor
        ↓ scheme + execution profile
Goblin server: rules, graph, attempts, marks, acceptance
        ↕ commands and events
Goblin utility: lead → deliver → wait → recover
        ↕ adapter of the available environment
Worker: read the package → do the work → submit the result

Semantic question → Jev by profile
Uncertainty / error / manual acceptance → person

The utility takes over the mechanical coordination: waiting for changes, delivering the exact task, collecting the addressed reply, repeating delivery and reporting. The server stays the source of state and rules. The worker still does the substantive task; the utility code does not replace its reasoning.

For the compatible simple profile these are kept: the task as a file, the address N.K, the priority of the description over the spec, block assets, in/ and out/rN/, the semantic decision of decisions through Jev, turning to a person on failure. The numeric profile from the general proposal stays a separate option; it is not switched on for old schemes automatically.

Trusted acceptance by the leader needs a special decision when the AI leader is removed from the chain. In the lead profile, explicit trust in the worker's addressed submission can be kept, but this is not proof of quality. Where the leader used to judge the result on its merits, a formal check, Jev or a person is needed. An automatic "accept everything" cannot quietly be taken as equal to such a leader.

Minimal new version

  1. Contract. A single server package and profile; exact run/step/session, clean JSON and outcome. Remove the implicit jump to the old drive from the new mode.
  2. One run. The modern drive2 and worker through step.take/submit with stable command IDs. The execution state stays on the server; only the access context, the cursor and an unconfirmed delivery are kept locally.
  3. One real launch adapter. First a supported local CLI or a specific available environment. Start control, confirmation of receipt, stopping and recovery. Printing a message must not be counted as a successful delivery.
  4. Several runs. Limit the number of processes and external calls, give a fair queue between runs. One run waiting for a reply must not block service of the others.
  5. Extra environments and legacy. Connect one adapter at a time, keeping the old commands compatible. Isolate the old engine1; removing it is not part of the proposal.

Expected benefit and limits

The main benefit is removing extra calls to the AI just to forward a task, wait and pass on a reply. This is especially noticeable with a large number of short steps. A long image generation, the work of an external service or the reasoning of a worker will not be sped up by the utility itself.

What should be measured is the number of calls and tokens of the AI leader, the time from issued to receiving the task, the delay between a submission and the next step, the number of duplicate starts, recovery after a break and the SQL load. The current materials give no ground to promise a percentage of saving.

Conclusion

Yes, the utility deserves a second life. The most promising is a reconstruction around engine2: keep the useful client code, separate a delivery dispatcher and use a common server contract. A full rewrite from scratch is not justified by the results of the analysis.

A return in stages makes sense: first one run and one real way to launch, then recovery and several runs. The simple leader path stays as a supported option. The old utility should not be declared a ready solution for high load until the new scheme is implemented and accepted.

The proposal is tied to the [[future-run-simplification|general run optimization]]. To bring it back into service, separately agreed CLI tests will be needed: a full pass, a return, an access denial, an interrupted start, a repeated submit, session expiry and a dispatcher restart. These tests were not done in this analysis.

pages.title: Visualization of work by agents
pages.summary_html:
A separate view of the run is proposed, in which the main displayed objects are the current agents. Each agent is shown as its own block.

Next to the agent, the sequence of scheme blocks that it performs is shown. In how it is displayed, this is an analogue of the timing, which, according to the user, was already implemented in Goblin.
pages.body_html:
What the view should look like

For each current agent a separate block with its name is shown. From it unfolds the sequence of scheme blocks that it performs: the stages already done and the current work. The order reflects the actual sequence of execution.

Such a view lets you see what each agent is busy with and which stages it has done. When several agents work at the same time, their sequences are shown side by side, so that the progress of the work can be compared.

Link with the timing

When working out the idea, study the previously implemented timing and find out which display elements and data can be reused. The content and current state of that implementation were not checked as part of recording the idea.

Related sections

The view belongs to observing the [[run|run]] and to the [[frontend|Goblin interface]]. The exact rules of placement, time scale and jumping to a scheme element are still to be clarified.

pages.body_html:
Purpose of the record

A section of the scheme catalog: sites, photo, video, texts and others — ten in all.

The section passport is the standard frame of the section's schemes, what to ask the person, what can be configured and pitfalls. The builder takes the frame when there is no similar scheme in the catalog. The sections are managed by the admin panel.

Storage

Engine: InnoDB. String collation: utf8mb4_unicode_ci. Snapshot: 2026-09-29. The i18n column was added by migration 024-catalog-i18n.sql.

Full field structure

FieldSQL typeNULLDEFAULTExtraPurpose
keyvarchar(32)NONULL / not set—The key of the section; templates.category refers to it.
titlevarchar(64)NONULL / not set—Name of the section.
iconvarchar(32)NO''—Icon of the section.
aboutvarchar(512)NO''—Short description of the section.
passportlongtextNO'{}'—JSON of the section passport: skeleton, questions, tune, pitfalls.
i18nlongtextNO'{}'—Translations JSON of the section: {"en": {title, about, passport}} — no body. With no translation for the project language, the Russian version is used.
sortint(11)NO0—Order of sections in the catalog.
updated_atdatetime(3)NOcurrent_timestamp(3)on update current_timestamp(3)Time of the last update of the record.

Indexes

IndexFields in orderUniqueMethod
PRIMARYkeyyesBTREE
ix_categories_sortsortnoBTREE

Foreign keys and back references

The table has no foreign keys.

Application rules

The section passport is the standard frame of the section's schemes, what to ask the person, what can be configured and pitfalls. The builder takes the frame when there is no similar scheme in the catalog. The sections are managed by the admin panel.

The section translation lives in i18n under the language key: {"en": {"title": …, "about": …, "passport": {…}}}; a section has no scheme body, so a translation never has body. Section names and passports in the catalog and in the search for similar schemes are returned in the project language (projects.lang); with no translation the Russian text stays. The key, icon and order are shared by all languages. More — [[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]].

SQL describes the allowed form of storage. Permissions and content checks are done in PHP.

CREATE TABLE

CREATE TABLE `template_categories` (
  `key` varchar(32) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(64) NOT NULL,
  `icon` varchar(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `about` varchar(512) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `passport` longtext NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  `i18n` longtext NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  `sort` int(11) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `updated_at` datetime(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT current_timestamp(3) ON UPDATE current_timestamp(3),
  PRIMARY KEY (`key`),
  KEY `ix_categories_sort` (`sort`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci

pages.title: Scheme catalog — lib/templates/catalog.php
pages.summary_html:
A catalog of ready schemes: sections, cards, passports, previews and the "Catalog experience" for the builder.

The article links this file with the PHP modules it calls and the tables. Its functions should be used in the intended context of a request or command, respecting the access checks and transactions of the caller.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

A catalog of ready schemes: sections, cards, previews and the catalog experience for the builder. It provides: catalogGet(), catalogCard(), catalogPreview(), catalogDigest(), catalogPassport(), catalogPick(). It does not: unpack a template (templateApply, templates.php) and does not edit the catalog (admin panel). The catalog holds only templates marked in_catalog: working schemes checked by a run. A passport is knowledge about a scheme: what it is for, what goes in and out, which services, what can be configured, what to ask the person, where runs stumbled. The passports of sections and templates are the only source of the catalog's experience: the builder gets it as the catalogDigest() section.

Location

lib/templates/catalog.php. The description was prepared from the source file on September 29, 2026.

Functions of the file

The signatures are taken from the source. The explanations reproduce the comments next to the declaration; the absence of a comment is marked explicitly. The line number serves as a landmark in this version of the file.

Function and lineParameters and resultComment in the code
catalogPassport:18function catalogPassport(string $json, array $fields): arrayA passport from JSON: only known fields, strings trimmed, lists as strings.
catalogGet:38function catalogGet(): voidGET catalog.get — sections and cards of the catalog; &template=key — one card with the passport and the scheme preview.
catalogCard:62function catalogCard(array $row, bool $full = false): arrayA catalog card: short for the list, with the passport and preview for the scheme window.
catalogPreview:89function catalogPreview(array $body): arrayA scheme preview for the minimap: nodes with frames and the arrows between them — without specs and styling. Default sizes are as on the canvas (defaultSize, public/src/core/kinds.js).
catalogDigest:122function catalogDigest(): stringThe "Catalog experience" for the builder: sections with their passports and templates with passports — as text, by which the model picks the nearest scheme and knows what can be configured in it. Built on every request: a new template immediately becomes the builder's knowledge.
catalogStems:157function catalogStems(string $text): arrayWord stems: lower case, letters and digits, the first five characters — crude, but without dictionaries.
catalogPick:173function catalogPick(string $text, int $limit = 3): arraySimilar catalog schemes by the words of the goal and the person's answers — a hint for the builder, not a decision: the model picks the base by the passports. The name weighs three times, tags and section twice, the description and passport once. Returns up to $limit schemes with scores, best first.

pages.title: New scheme: catalog and builder
pages.summary_html:
The "New scheme" window creates a folder with a run-ready scheme in two ways: take a scheme from the catalog, or put one together in the builder from a short questionnaire.

The window opens with the "▦ new scheme" button above the folders, with the "Scheme catalog" and "Scheme builder" items in settings, and from the assistant's quick menu.
pages.body_html:
Catalog

Schemes are grouped into sections: sites and landing pages, photo, video, texts, social media, documents, data and API, audio, code, and Goblin basics. Every catalog scheme has been checked with a real run — its card has a "checked" mark. Search looks through the name, description and tags.

A scheme card shows a minimap and a passport: what the scheme is for, its input and output, steps, services, and what can be configured in it. "Create folder" unpacks the scheme into a new folder together with the block specs and run settings. "Configure in builder" passes the scheme to the builder as the goal.

Builder

The person writes in their own words what should come out. The AI picks a similar catalog scheme as the base and asks questions one at a time: a card with options, and you can always write your own answer. Three to five questions are usually enough, and there are never more than seven; "Enough, build it" starts the build right away.

The build adjusts the base to the answers — specs, services, number of blocks, checks. If there is no similar scheme, the builder builds from scratch using the section's standard frame. The server tries the draft in the run's pre-check and, if there are problems, asks the AI to fix it. The person sees the minimap and the check result before the folder is created; "Refine" changes the draft according to the person's words.

The service for the kind of work that needs one (images, video, voice-over) is chosen in the questionnaire and written into the block's description. The "Any available" option leaves the choice to the worker.

Phone

In the mobile skin the window takes the whole screen: sections go in a scrolling row above the cards, and the minimap and passport go one under the other.

pages.source_note: checked against public/src/admin/sections/templates.js, lib/admin/actions.php 2026-09-29
pages.title: Scheme catalog
pages.summary_html:
The "Scheme catalog" section of the admin panel manages the catalog's sections and its schemes. There is one catalog per installation.

The passports of sections and schemes are the builder's source of experience: for every request the server assembles the "Catalog experience" section from them.
pages.body_html:
Sections

A table of sections: name, icon, description, order and passport — standard frame, questions, what can be configured, pitfalls. Saving is the category.save action.

Schemes

A scheme card: name, section, description, the "In catalog" mark, the date of the last run check, and the passport (what it is for, input, output, steps, services, what can be configured, questions, pitfalls, tags) — the template.update action. "+ Take from folder" creates a scheme from a project folder, "Update from folder" replaces the body of an existing one (template.fromFolder). Deleting is allowed for built-in schemes too.

A scheme appears in the "New scheme" window only with the "In catalog" mark. Before marking it, it is worth checking the scheme with a run and setting the check date.

pages.title: lib/core/i18n.php
pages.summary_html:
The interface language: the lang/<language>/*.json dictionaries and the choice of language for the person and for agents.

The file provides t() and tn() for the person, ta() and tna() for the project's agents, and langScript() for embedding the dictionary in the page. The person's language comes from the goblin_lang cookie, the agents' language from the project. More in [[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]].
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

The interface language: the dictionaries lang/<language>/<part>.json and the choice of the person's language. Provides: lang(), t(), tn(), langAgents(), ta(), tna(), langFile(), langDict(), langScript() and the LANGS constant. Does not: choose the language itself — the cookie sets it for the person, the project sets it for agents.

Each person chooses the language: the goblin_lang cookie (set by [[backend-resource-public-src-core-i18n-js|public/src/core/i18n.js]]); with no cookie, Russian. A language dictionary lies on top of Russian: if a translation is missing, the Russian text stays and the key never shows. A key is “part.place.meaning”, for example editor.settings.title; parts follow the dictionary files (editor, admin, …).

Two languages in one request: t() is the person's language (the interface, their errors), ta() is the language of the project's agents (projects.lang): run instructions, tasks, the feed, replies to the leader. requireProject() sets it itself; outside a request (background jobs), it is the language of the job's project or Russian.

Location

lib/core/i18n.php. The description was prepared from the source file as of 29 September 2026. There are two languages: const LANGS = ['ru', 'en'] (line 16).

How the file is used

  • The editor page puts the dictionary into the browser through langScript(['common', 'editor']) in [[backend-resource-lib-web-page-php|lib/web/page.php]]; there {{t:key}} in the views is also replaced through t(). The admin page does the same with the parts common and admin.
  • The agents' language is set from the project's language field in [[backend-resource-lib-access-rights-php|lib/access/rights.php]] (line 124) and in [[backend-resource-lib-ai-jobs-php|lib/ai/jobs.php]] (line 29, the background process).
  • langFile() with the agents' language is used by [[backend-resource-lib-ai-settings-php|lib/ai/settings.php]], [[backend-resource-lib-api-service-php|lib/api/service.php]] and lib/api/instructions.php — this is how an md instruction is chosen. langAgents() is also read by [[backend-resource-lib-templates-catalog-php|lib/templates/catalog.php]] and [[backend-resource-lib-engine-events-php|lib/engine/events.php]].

File functions

Signatures are taken from the source. The notes reproduce the comments next to the declaration; a missing comment is marked explicitly. The line number is a guide in this version of the file.

Function and lineParameters and resultComment in code
lang:19function lang(): stringThe person's language: the cookie, otherwise Russian.
langAgents:26function langAgents(?string $set = null): stringThe language of the project's agents; with an argument, sets it.
ta:34function ta(string $key, array $vars = []): stringText for agents, in the project's language.
tna:40function tna(string $key, int $n, array $vars = []): stringA number with a word for agents, in the project's language.
langFill:48function langFill(string $text, array $vars): stringThe declaration has no separate comment; its purpose follows from the module context. By the code: replaces each {name} in the text with the value from $vars.
langFile:55function langFile(string $dir, string $name, ?string $lang = null): stringA file in a language: <folder>/<language>/<name>; no translation means Russian. This is how the md instructions are stored (instructions/ru|en).
langDict:62function langDict(?string $lang = null): arrayThe dictionary of a language on top of Russian.
langFiles:72function langFiles(string $lang): arrayThe declaration has no separate comment; its purpose follows from the module context. By the code: merges all lang/<language>/*.json files into one flat dictionary.
t:82function t(string $key, array $vars = []): stringText by key; {name} in the text is replaced with the value from $vars.
tn:88function tn(string $key, int $n, array $vars = []): stringA number with a word: forms key.one / key.few / key.many (Russian) or key.one / key.other; {n} is the number itself.
langPlural:96function langPlural(string $lang, int $n): stringThe number form, the same as Intl.PluralRules in the browser.
langScript:107function langScript(array $parts): stringThe dictionary for the browser: only the needed parts (editor, common, …), embedded in the page.

Details from the code

  • lang() accepts only values from LANGS; any other cookie value gives Russian.
  • langAgents() keeps the language in a static variable; with no argument it returns the current value (Russian by default), with an argument it sets it first (an unknown language becomes Russian).
  • langDict() caches the dictionary of each language for the length of the request. For Russian these are only the lang/ru files; for another language, the Russian files with the files of that language on top.
  • langFiles() takes all lang/<language>/*.json and merges them into one flat dictionary; for the same key the file read later wins.
  • tn() and tna() look for key.<form>, then key.other, then key.many, then the key itself. {n} is always added to the substitutions.
  • langPlural(): for a language other than Russian, one when n = 1, otherwise other. For Russian: one (ends in 1, except 11), few (2–4, except 12–14), otherwise many.
  • langScript() keeps the keys whose first part (before the first dot) is in the list of parts, and returns a <script>window.GOBLIN_I18N = {"lang": …, "dict": {…}};</script> tag with the person's language. The JSON is written with the flags JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE, JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES and JSON_HEX_TAG, so that dictionary text cannot close the tag.

Related topics

[[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]]; the browser half is [[backend-resource-public-src-core-i18n-js|public/src/core/i18n.js]].

pages.title: Interface language — public/src/core/i18n.js
pages.summary_html:
The interface language in the browser: t(), tn(), lang and setLang().

The module does not load the dictionary: the page puts it into window.GOBLIN_I18N. The language is changed by writing the goblin_lang cookie and reloading. More in [[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]].
pages.body_html:
public/src/core/i18n.js

Purpose and limits

The interface language in the browser: text by key, a number with a word, changing the language. Provides: t(), tn(), lang, setLang(). Does not: load dictionaries — the page puts them into window.GOBLIN_I18N (langScript in [[backend-resource-lib-core-i18n-php|lib/core/i18n.php]]).

A key is “part.place.meaning”: editor.settings.title. If there is no translation, the Russian text is shown; if that is missing too, the key itself.

What the module exports

ExportWhat it does
langA string with the page language: data.lang from GOBLIN_I18N, or ru with no dictionary (line 9).
t(key, vars)Text by key; {name} is replaced with the value from vars. If the key is not in the dictionary, the key itself is returned (line 12).
tn(key, n, vars)A number with a word: forms key.one / key.few / key.many or key.one / key.other; {n} is the number itself (line 19).
setLang(next)Change the language: a cookie for a year and a reload — the page is rebuilt fully in the new language (line 32).

Where the dictionary comes from

On load the module reads globalThis.GOBLIN_I18N; if it is absent, it uses { lang: 'ru', dict: {} }. PHP builds the dictionary in the page: langScript() in [[backend-resource-lib-web-page-php|lib/web/page.php]] (the parts common and editor) puts a script into the head, so t() already works at the top level of any module. The dictionary holds the person's language, with Russian already laid under it on the server side, so there is no merging in the browser.

How substitutions and numbers work

  • The internal fill() replaces each {name} in the text with String(value) from vars (replaceAll).
  • The number form is chosen by Intl.PluralRules(lang), created once on load. tn() looks for key.<form>, then key.other, then key.many, then the key itself; {n} is always added to the substitutions.

Changing the language

setLang(next) does nothing if the language is already the same. Otherwise it writes goblin_lang=<language>; path=/; max-age=31536000; samesite=lax (one year) and reloads the page. The value is not checked in JS: the PHP function lang() accepts only ru or en and turns anything else into Russian. The server reads the cookie, so the language applies to the whole page right after the reload.

The language buttons in the “Settings” window are wired in [[backend-resource-public-src-left-settings-js|public/src/left/settings.js]]: a button with a data-lang attribute gets the class on when its language equals lang, and a click calls setLang().

Related topics

[[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]]; the server half is [[backend-resource-lib-core-i18n-php|lib/core/i18n.php]].

pages.title: instructions/ru/прогон.md
pages.summary_html: The texts of the leader and worker instructions in one file cut into marked parts: the server builds an instruction from them for the team setup and the environment of a folder.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

The file holds the texts agents read during a run: the leader’s instruction and the worker’s instruction. One file is divided into parts: each starts with a line <!-- part:name --> and runs to the next mark. The line break before a mark is a separator, not text.

The server never returns the whole file. The builder lib/api/instructions.php takes only the parts it needs: leaderDoc() builds the leader’s instruction, workerDoc() the worker’s, and instrPart() pulls one part by name. The team setup (solo or team) and the environment (subagents, Orca, SendMessage) decide which parts go in. An agent gets only its own scenario: it would try to carry out anything extra. The leader’s instruction is served by the docs.run link; the worker’s is written by begin to the file service/tasks/rN/worker.md.

The file executes and checks nothing: it is text only. The logic of choosing parts lives in PHP, not here.

Location

instructions/ru/прогон.md. The description is based on the source file as of September 29, 2026. The English version is instructions/en/прогон.md: the same marks and substitutions, and the protocol words (NEXT, SILENCE, “task in file” and others) are given as the server prints them in English output. The line numbers below refer to the Russian file; in the English one they are shifted.

Project language

The language is the agents’ language of the project (langAgents()). langFile() looks for the file: first instructions/<language>/прогон.md, and if there is no such file — the Russian one. In addition, instrPart() looks for each part separately: a part missing from the translation is taken from the Russian file. The files are read once per request and cached.

How the server builds the instruction

First instrScenario() works out the scenario of the folder: the team setup (role_scheme, solo by default), the environment (empty for solo, otherwise run_env, and an unknown or empty one means subagents), the names of the setup and the environment from the agents dictionary, and the soon flag of the setup.

The leader’s instruction is these parts in order; empty ones are dropped, the rest are joined with a line break:

  1. the head (lead_head_solo or lead_head_team);
  2. lead_before;
  3. the rules (lead_rules_solo or lead_rules_team);
  4. lead_order;
  5. lead_begin;
  6. the round (lead_loop_solo or lead_loop_team);
  7. self_work;
  8. lead_diamond;
  9. lead_watch;
  10. the link with the worker for the environment (team only: lead_sub, lead_send, or orca_common with lead_orca);
  11. lead_other;
  12. lead_replies.

The worker’s instruction is three parts: work_head, work_body and a part for the environment (work_env_orca after orca_common, work_env_send or work_env_sub). If the worker file is built before the run starts, rN stands in for the number.

Substitutions

EntryWho substitutesWhat is inserted
{{name}}instrPart(), when reading a partAnother part or a value from the scenario: the setup and environment names, the run number, the folder name, the work folder. The table below shows which slots each part has.
{G}leaderDoc(), at the end of the buildThe API address with the project key: address?project=key.
{KEY}leaderDoc()The project key (url_key).
{FOLDER}leaderDoc()The folder number.
{WATCH}leaderDoc()The full path to bin/lead-watch.sh — the watchdog.
{RUN}workerDoc()The run number like rN.

The {{name}} slots are filled first, while {G}, {KEY}, {FOLDER}, {WATCH} and {RUN} are replaced over the already assembled text. So they may stand inside nested parts too. Samples like r109 in command examples are just text.

Parts of the file

A part goes into another one when its name appears in a slot (for example, lead_who_cards goes into {{who}} of lead_head_team). The order of parts in the file does not affect the build. Some parts deliberately begin with empty lines (lead_soon, lead_model, lead_other_wait, work_env_orca): that way the insert sits in the text with the right spacing. The text before the first mark (the explanation at the top of the file) is not used by the server.

Part (mark) and lineFor whom and whenWhat is in it
lead_head_solo:12leader, team setup “Leader does everything”Title and intro: the leader does every block itself, calls no subagents, needs no worker intro (op=invite), talks to the server with plain curl.
lead_who_subagents:22the {{who}} slot in lead_head_team; environment “Subagents”Performers are the leader’s subagents; the leader decides who does a block; agent cards on blocks do not apply.
lead_who_cards:25the {{who}} slot in lead_head_team; environments “Orca” and “SendMessage”The worker does the block; a block marked “performer — leader: do it yourself” in the NEXT line is done by the leader.
lead_soon:28the {{soon}} slot in lead_head_team; only if the team setup has soon in ROLE_SCHEMESTwo line breaks and a phrase: the consultant and auditor roles do not work yet — run it as “Leader — worker”. {{title}} is the team setup name.
lead_head_team:33leader, any team setup with a workerTitle “leader · setup · environment” and a general intro: takes a task, hands it to the performer, tells the server the result. Slots {{title}}, {{env}}, {{who}}, {{soon}}.
lead_model:44the {{model}} slot in lead_before; team onlyA bullet: if the agent has no model or effort set, that is no obstacle — start with defaults.
lead_before:47leader, alwaysSection “Before you start”: the docs.run link is a task for a run, not for development; scheme not ready — do not start; an unclosed run — ask the human; then begin. Sets the variable G="{G}". Slot {{model}}.
lead_rules_solo:63leader, “Leader does everything”Section “Rules”: does every block itself, calls no subagents, does not open images, submits a finished block at once, nobody checks the content, does not edit the scheme or spec; when to call the human.
lead_self_subagents:80the {{self}} slot in lead_rules_team; environment “Subagents”A bullet: a block the leader chose to do itself follows the section “How to do a block”; the answer goes through done.
lead_self_cards:83the {{self}} slot in lead_rules_team; environments “Orca” and “SendMessage”A bullet: a block marked “do it yourself” follows the section “How to do a block”; the leader does no other block, even tiny ones.
lead_rules_team:86leader, any team setup with a workerSection “Two rules”: 1) the leader is a postman, not an editor (passes the task and answer word for word); 2) the leader is the safety net of the course, a table “what went wrong — what to do”; when to call the human. Slot {{self}}.
lead_order_solo:116the {{mid}} slot in lead_order; soloItem 3: work in the round task → do → done until the server says “RUN PASSED”.
lead_order_team:118the {{mid}} slot in lead_order; teamItem 3: put the worker in its role with the intro from the server (op=invite); item 4: the round task → worker → done.
lead_order:121leader, alwaysSection “Order”: begin at once, set the watchdog, the steps from {{mid}}, then write the human a summary.
lead_begin_self:129the {{self}} slot in lead_begin; soloThe suffix “ · performer — leader: do it yourself” on the NEXT line in the begin answer example.
lead_begin:131leader, alwaysSection “Start the run”: the begin command, an answer example, the run number (&run=), the “RUN DESCRIPTION” and “SCHEME OUTLINE” blocks. Slots {FOLDER}, {{self}}.
lead_loop_solo:154leader, “Leader does everything”Section “Round: task → do → done”: how to take the task file, read it whole, what the task address is, how to submit the answer in one line.
lead_loop_or_subagents:181the {{or}} slot in lead_loop_team; environment “Subagents”Send the task line to the worker whole — or do the block yourself.
lead_loop_or_cards:183the {{or}} slot in lead_loop_team; environments “Orca” and “SendMessage”Send the task line to the worker whole (a block marked “do it yourself” is done by the leader).
lead_loop_team:185leader, any team setup with a workerSection “Round: task → worker → done”: only the line “task in file …” goes to the worker; how to pass the worker’s answer word for word, notes before the address. Slot {{or}}.
self_work_intro:216the {{intro}} slot in self_work; team onlyOne phrase: the section is for blocks the leader does itself.
self_work:220leader, always (in solo — for all blocks, in a team — for its own)Section “How to do a block”: a table of the service lines of the task file (block and address, round, work folder, materials, input, paid-call limit, answer sample) and the rules of a one-line answer by the sample. Slot {{intro}}.
lead_diamond:249leader, alwaysSection “Decisions”: Jev picks the branch; if unsure or unavailable the server writes “DECISION — Jev did not decide, decide yourself” and the leader answers done with branch=yes or branch=no.
lead_watch_why_solo:262the {{why}} slot in lead_watch; soloThe watchdog wakes the leader if the run status has not changed for 5 minutes: the leader got distracted or hung on a block.
lead_watch_why_team:264the {{why}} slot in lead_watch; teamThe watchdog wakes the leader if the status has not changed for 5 minutes: the worker went silent or the matter waits for the leader.
lead_watch_rows_team:267the {{rows}} slot in lead_watch; teamTwo rows of the watchdog table: the first “SILENCE” for a worker’s block — ask the worker; the second in a row — tell the human and wait.
lead_watch:271leader, alwaysSection “Watchdog”: started as a background command {WATCH} {KEY} r109, not through &; one watchdog per run; a table of watchdog lines. Slots {{why}}, {{rows}}.
lead_sub:293leader, team, environment “Subagents”Section “Link with the worker · environment “Subagents””: workers are subagents (in Claude Code the Agent tool); the leader decides how many; the first message to a subagent is the intro (op=invite) and the task line; the answer is the subagent’s final message.
lead_send:320leader, team, environment “SendMessage”Section “Link with the worker · environment “SendMessage””: separate Claude Code sessions; find the worker with ListAgents; the intro and tasks go by SendMessage; the answer arrives as an incoming message.
orca_common:349leader and worker, environment “Orca” (for the leader — before lead_orca, for the worker — before work_env_orca)Common to both roles: a message in one line through orca terminal send; after sending, end the turn and wait; the --wait-submit 4 receipt, requestId, a retry with --retry-request; the agent_prompt_blocked answer.
lead_orca:375leader, team, environment “Orca”The leader’s own address ($ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE), where to find or how to create the worker in Orca, the intro and the task with orca terminal send, the answer “WORKER ANSWER: …”.
lead_other_wait:424the {{wait}} slot in lead_other; team onlyOne line with the op=wait command: nothing to do, several workers are busy, waits up to 25 s.
lead_other:427leader, alwaysSection “Other commands”: where, again, fail, scheme, stop. Slots {FOLDER}, {{wait}}.
lead_replies_team:442the {{team}} slot in lead_replies; team onlyA table row: “Answer to task … not accepted” — an answer to a past round, send nothing.
lead_replies_stuck_solo:445the {{stuck}} slot in lead_replies; soloWhat to do on “STUCK”: a failure — op=again once; otherwise call the human.
lead_replies_stuck_team:447the {{stuck}} slot in lead_replies; teamThe same for “STUCK”, but the cause is a worker failure.
lead_replies_self:449the {{self}} slot in lead_replies; everywhere except environment “Subagents” (in solo too)A table row for the answer “… · performer — leader: do it yourself”: take task, do it, submit done.
lead_replies:452leader, alwaysSection “Server answers — what to do”: a table “answer — what to do” (accepted, “⚠”, gateway, NEXT, “RUN PASSED”, “SCHEME NOT READY” and others). Slots {{team}}, {{stuck}}, {{self}}.
work_dir_default:482the {{dir}} slot in work_head; when the folder has no work folder (work_dir)The text “from the “Work folder” line of the task”.
work_head:484worker, alwaysTitle “worker · run · environment”: the worker does one block and answers the leader; does not go to the server; the work folder and out/{RUN}/. Slots {{no}}, {{name}}, {{env}}, {{dir}}.
work_body:494worker, alwaysSections “How the work goes”, “What comes in the task” (a table of service lines), “How to answer” (address and sample), “Rules”. Substitution {RUN}.
work_env_orca:557worker, environment “Orca” (after orca_common)How to answer the leader with orca terminal send and the text “WORKER ANSWER: …”; end the turn and wait; a retry without --retry-request at most once.
work_env_send:571worker, environment “SendMessage”Section “How to deliver the answer”: messages come from the leader, the answer goes by SendMessage to whoever sent the task; if in doubt — ListAgents; send once.
work_env_sub:581worker, environment “Subagents” (and any other — the default branch)Section “How to deliver the answer”: the worker is the leader’s subagent; the answer is the last line of the final message, with the address; send nothing to anyone.
end:589nobody: an end marker at the end of the fileNo text. The builder does not call this part; the mark gives the last part (work_env_sub) a boundary.

Editing rules

A mark stands on its own line, exactly as <!-- part:name -->: the builder looks for it together with the line break. A new part must not only be written here but also called from instructions.php. The English file is edited together with the Russian one — the marks and substitutions in them must match.

pages.title: tests/v2/check-i18n.php
pages.summary_html: The interface translation check: compares the lang/ru and lang/en dictionaries and the keys in the code, and counts how many Russian strings are still left in the code.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

The script checks the interface translation. It reads the dictionaries lang/ru/*.json and lang/en/*.json and scans the code that calls translation. It fails if a dictionary is not a JSON object; a key does not start with the name of its part (editor.json → editor.*); the ru and en keys differ; the translation has other {name} substitutions; or the code calls a key that is not in the dictionary. Separately it prints how many Russian strings are left in the code, by part. It does not: touch the database or the server, change any files, judge the quality of a translation, or look at the agent instructions in instructions/ (see the article [[backend-resource-instructions-ru-progon-md|instructions/ru/прогон.md]] for those). How translation works is described in [[frontend-languages|Languages: interface and agents]].

Location

tests/v2/check-i18n.php. The description is based on the source file as of September 29, 2026. The file has no named functions: the work goes top to bottom, and repeated pieces are moved into four closures (table below).

How to run

/Applications/XAMPP/xamppfiles/bin/php tests/v2/check-i18n.php [--left] [--part=editor]

Run it from the project root. Only PHP is needed: no server, database or browser.

OptionWhat it does
no optionsChecks the dictionaries and the keys in the code, prints the count of Russian strings by part.
--leftUnder each part prints the files with Russian strings, most strings first.
--part=nameCounts Russian strings in one part only: editor, admin, account, server, docs or agents. The dictionary and key checks do not depend on it.

What is checked in the dictionaries

The script reads all files lang/ru/*.json and lang/en/*.json. The part is the first word of the file name up to - or .: for editor-panel.json the part is editor. At the start it prints “Словари: ru N, en N ключей” (dictionaries: ru N, en N keys).

CheckWhen it fails
File formatThe file is not a JSON object (an empty [] is allowed, a non-empty list is not).
ValueA key’s value is not a string.
Key partA key does not start with the part name of its file: editor*.json may hold only editor.*.
DuplicateOne key is in two files of the same language.
ru and en keysA key is in one dictionary and missing from the other. The first 20 “no en translation” and the first 20 “no Russian text” are printed; for the rest without en translation one summary line with the count is added.
SubstitutionsThe sets of {name} in the Russian and English text of one key differ.
Empty Russian textThe Russian text of a key is empty.
Russian letters in EnglishThe English text contains Cyrillic.

Which keys are looked up in the code

Scanned: public/src/**/*.js, views/**/*.html, lib/**/*.php, the files public/*.php, and md_backend/документация/index.php and graph.php. Paths with /vendor/ and /archive- are skipped. In each file it looks for calls t(, tn(, ta(, tna( with a quoted key (not after a letter or a dot) and {{t:key}} substitutions in views. It prints “Вызовов ключей в коде: N” (key calls in code: N).

CallWhat is checked
t, ta, {{t:…}}The key is in the Russian dictionary.
tn, tnaThe forms exist: in Russian .one, .few, .many, in English .one, .other.
A key ending with a dotThe key is glued together in the code (t('agents.role.' . $roles)), so at least one key of the Russian dictionary must start with it.

How many Russian strings are left in the code

Files are split into parts by the $partOf closure. Comments are not counted: /* … */, <!-- … -->, // to the end of the line (not inside an address), and lines starting with #. In HTML the text between tags and the attributes title, placeholder, aria-label, alt are counted; in other files, quoted and backtick strings with Russian letters. Files outside any part are skipped. This count does not affect the result: it only shows how much work is left.

PartWhich files
adminpublic/src/admin/, lib/admin/, public/admin.php

agentslib/engine/, lib/cli/, lib/ai/, lib/api/simple.php, lib/api/instructions.php — the run, the utility and the AI
serverthe rest of lib/ and public/ — server messages

Output and exit codes

Each error found is printed as a line “ FAIL …”. At the end comes “ok” or “FAIL: N”, where N is the number of errors.

CodeWhen
0No errors. The remaining Russian strings in the code do not affect the exit code.
1At least one error was found.

Closures of the file

The line number is a landmark in this version of the file. Notes come from the comments next to the declaration; a missing comment is stated.

Closure and lineParameters and resultComment in code
$bad:14static function (string $what): voidNo separate comment: raises the error count and prints “ FAIL …”.
$holes:40static function (string $text): arrayNo separate comment: returns a sorted list of the {name} substitutions in the text.
$scan:51static function (string $dir, array $ext): voidNo separate comment: adds the files of a folder with the wanted extensions to the list, skipping /vendor/ and /archive-.

pages.title: Languages: interface and agents
pages.summary_html:
Goblin has two languages: Russian and English. Each person chooses the interface language for themselves, while the agents language is set by the project — these are two independent choices.

The names of projects, folders and blocks that a user typed are not translated in any language.
pages.body_html:
Two choices, not one

What is chosenWho choosesWhere it changes
Interface languageEach person for themselvesThe "Settings" menu, the "Language" switch ([[frontend-settings|"Settings"]])
Agents languageThe project — one for everyone who works in itThe project properties, the "Agents language" field

Interface language

The "Language" switch is at the top of the "Settings" menu in the left panel: the buttons "Русский" and "English", with the current language highlighted. The choice works in this browser and does not affect other people in the same project.

After the click, the browser saves the language in the goblin_lang cookie for a year and reloads the page: it is built again in the chosen language as a whole. If there is no cookie, Russian is on. If a text has no translation, the Russian version is shown — there are no empty places or technical keys on the screen.

How it works in the code: [[backend-resource-public-src-core-i18n-js|public/src/core/i18n.js]] in the browser and [[backend-resource-lib-core-i18n-php|lib/core/i18n.php]] on the server.

Agents language of a project

The agents language is stored in the project — in the lang field of the [[backend-resource-table-projects|projects]] table. You can change it in the project properties: the "Project" section of the right panel (it is visible while no folder is open, and also in the project card from the list of projects), the "Agents language" field with the values "Русский" and "English". The note under the field reminds you: the instructions for the leader and worker, the run tasks and the built-in AI work in this language.

A new project gets the interface language of the person who created it. Later the language can be changed separately from the interface: for example, you work in the Russian interface, while the agents of the project read the instructions in English.

Rules of changing:

  • the language is changed by someone who can edit the project; in view-only mode the field is locked;
  • only ru and en are allowed; the server rejects any other value with the message "Agent language must be one of: ru, en";
  • while a run is going in the project (running or paused), the language does not change: the server refuses, as it does for other meaningful edits of a live run. Stop the run and try again.

For programmatic clients this is the project.update operation with the lang field ([[backend-api|API operations catalog]]).

What is in which language

WhatIn which languageNote
Editor interface, windows, account, errors for a personThe person's languageThe dictionaries lang/ru and lang/en; no translation — Russian text.
DocumentationThe person's languageThe English version is shown if there is one; otherwise the Russian one. On the documentation page itself there are the links "Русский" and "English" under the logo (labeled "Documentation language"): you can change the language without going to the editor. The choice is remembered by the same goblin_lang cookie, and you return to the same page.
Instructions for the leader, worker and drawing, the builder, instructions of the built-in AIThe project languageThe Markdown files are stored by language: instructions/ru and instructions/en. If there is no file in the project language, the Russian one is taken.
Server messages to an agent: run tasks, the feed, replies to the leaderThe project languageThey are printed by the server from the agents dictionary; a person gets their own errors in the interface language.
Scheme catalogThe project languageA template has translations of the title, the description, the scheme body with specs and the passport. No translation — the Russian entry as it is ([[frontend-new-scheme|"New scheme"]]).
Names of projects, folders, blocks, spec texts and assets of the userNot translatedThis is your data: Goblin shows it and passes it to agents exactly as it was typed.

Two languages in one request

The server tells the person's language from the agents language. Replies to a person are built by the cookie of their browser, and everything meant for agents — by the project language, which the server determines when it opens the project. Background jobs (for example, the work of the built-in AI) also take the project language, not anyone's browser, so agents do not switch between languages when different people come into the project.
