pages.title: lib/ai/access.php
pages.summary_html:
Access to models: the shared one of the installation and the personal one of a user (users.access); aiAccess() returns the effective one.

The file does not call models. It says where to go and with which key: personal fields lie over the shared ones from config.php and secrets.php. [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]] and [[backend-resource-lib-ai-deepseek-php|lib/ai/deepseek.php]] take their access from here.
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Access to models: the shared one of the installation and the personal one of a user. Provides: the ACCESS_FIELDS constant and the functions aiAccess(), aiAccessOwn(), aiAccessSave(), aiAccessUse(). Does not: call models. It only says where to go and with which key.

Shared access lives in [[backend-resource-lib-core-config-php|config.php]] and secrets.php: DeepSeek (the ai_* fields) and OpenAI voice (the voice_* fields). A person's own access is stored in the access field of the [[backend-resource-table-users|users]] table and edited in the account, in the "AI" section. An empty field means the shared value.

Location

lib/ai/access.php. Described from the source file as of 29 September 2026. The field list is const ACCESS_FIELDS (line 12): ai_api_url, ai_model, ai_api_key, voice_api_url, voice_model, voice_languages, voice_tts_model, voice_tts_voice, voice_api_key.

How the file is used

  • Assistant model: [[backend-resource-lib-ai-deepseek-php|lib/ai/deepseek.php]] takes the address, model and key from aiAccess().
  • Background job: [[backend-resource-lib-ai-jobs-php|lib/ai/jobs.php]] (line 30) calls aiAccessUse() with the person who asked, so the job runs with that person's key and not with the key of whoever is in the current request.
  • Voice: [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]] takes the key and the recognition and speech settings from aiAccess().
  • Account: [[backend-resource-public-account-php|public/account.php]] reads the personal fields with aiAccessOwn() (the accountAccess form) and saves them with aiAccessSave() (the access-save action).

Functions in the file

Signatures are taken from the source. Descriptions repeat the comment next to the declaration; a missing comment is marked. The line number is a guide for this version of the file.

Function and lineParameters and resultComment in the code
aiAccessUse:18function aiAccessUse(?int $userId): voidBackground job: whose access to take (ai_jobs.user_id); null means the shared one.
aiAccess:24function aiAccess(): arrayThe effective access: personal fields over the shared ones.
aiAccessOwn:41function aiAccessOwn(?int $userId): arrayA person's own fields, only the ones that are set.
aiAccessSave:50function aiAccessSave(int $userId, array $input): voidSave personal access from the account form: an empty field goes back to the shared value.

Details from the code

  • aiAccess() first collects the shared values from config() for every field in ACCESS_FIELDS (each is cast to a string; no value gives an empty string). Then it finds the person and lays the personal values over the shared ones: only non-empty values are taken.
  • Whose access. If a person has already been set with aiAccessUse() (null included), that one is used, which is how the background process works. Otherwise it takes caller()['user_id'] of the signed-in person; if the caller cannot be determined (an exception), the access is the shared one.
  • aiAccessOwn() reads the JSON from users.access; if there is no person, or the field is empty or not an object, it returns an empty array. Extra keys are dropped: only the fields from ACCESS_FIELDS remain, values cast to strings.
  • aiAccessSave() goes through ACCESS_FIELDS, trims spaces and keeps only non-empty values, each at most 500 characters. The whole result is written to users.access as JSON (Unicode and slashes unescaped). The old personal values are replaced, which is why an empty form field brings back the shared value.
  • aiAccessSave() does not check write rights itself: the caller must pass its own identifier (the account passes currentUser()['id']).

Related topics

[[accounts-user-ai|Chats and AI usage]]; [[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]]; the access field is in the [[backend-resource-table-users|users table]].

pages.title: lib/ai/voice.php
pages.summary_html:
Voice: the operations voice.session (a temporary token for live recognition) and voice.speak (reading an answer aloud).

The OpenAI key never goes to the browser: the server issues a token for one session, and orders speech itself and returns mp3. Access comes from [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]].
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

Voice: live speech recognition and reading answers aloud (OpenAI). Provides: two API operations, voice.session and voice.speak, and the helper request voiceHttp(). Does not: listen to the microphone or play sound. That is the browser's job ([[backend-resource-public-src-panel-voice-js|public/src/panel/voice.js]]).

The OpenAI key never goes to the browser. For recognition the server issues a temporary token for one session (the /realtime/client_secrets request), and the browser uses it to connect to OpenAI itself over WebRTC. The server orders speech itself (/audio/speech) and returns the sound. The access is the person's own or the shared one, chosen by [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]].

Location

lib/ai/voice.php. Described from the source file as of 29 September 2026.

How the file is used

  • The operations are wired in the OPS table of [[backend-resource-lib-api-router-php|lib/api/router.php]] (lines 141–142): voice.session and voice.speak, both POST, role human only (human), mode read. A comment there says they are not written to the journal. The catalog is [[backend-api|API operations catalog]].
  • The browser calls them from the assistant panel ([[backend-resource-public-src-panel-voice-js|public/src/panel/voice.js]]); the assistant itself is described in [[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]].

Functions in the file

Signatures are taken from the source. Descriptions repeat the comment next to the declaration; a missing comment is marked. The line number is a guide for this version of the file.

Function and lineParameters and resultComment in the code
voiceHttp:13function voiceHttp(string $path, array $body, array $access): arrayA request to OpenAI on behalf of the access: JSON goes in, [code, body, type] comes back.
voiceSession:38function voiceSession(): voidPOST voice.session: a temporary token for live recognition: {value, expires, url}.
voiceSpeak:66function voiceSpeak(): voidPOST voice.speak {text}: read the answer aloud: mp3 sound right in the response.

Details from the code

  • voiceHttp(). Without a voice_api_key it fails at once with "no key" (code forbidden, text server.voice.no_key: set the key in the account or ask the administrator). Otherwise it sends a POST to voice_api_url plus the path, with JSON and an Authorization: Bearer header, timeout 60 seconds. No answer gives server.voice.silent (code server); an HTTP code of 400 or more gives server.voice.refused with the reason from the answer, or "HTTP code". It returns the code, the body and the content type.
  • voiceSession(). Checks the project with requireProject(false): any project member may speak, write rights are not needed. It takes aiAccess() and builds the recognition settings from voice_model. The languages in voice_languages are a comma-separated list and only a hint for the model; empty means any language. For a model whose name starts with gpt-live the list languages is sent; for other models a single language (the first in the list).
  • The request to /realtime/client_secrets: the token lives 600 seconds from creation, the session type is transcription, noise reduction is near_field, turn_detection is off, so recording goes on until the person presses "stop". If the answer has no value, the error is server.voice.refused with the reason "no client secret". The operation returns value (the token), expires (the end time, or 0) and url, the OpenAI address without a trailing slash, so the browser knows where to connect.
  • voiceSpeak(). Also requireProject(false). It reads the text parameter; empty gives the error server.voice.no_text ("Nothing to read aloud"). It orders speech from /audio/speech with the model voice_tts_model and the voice voice_tts_voice; the text is cut to 4000 characters, the speaking style comes from the dictionary (server.voice.tts_style), the format is mp3.
  • The answer of voiceSpeak() is not JSON: the Content-Type header comes from the OpenAI answer (audio/mpeg if missing), Cache-Control: no-store, the body is the sound itself, then the script ends.

Related topics

Access and keys: [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]]; the field for personal settings: [[backend-resource-table-users|users table]]; error texts: [[backend-resource-lib-core-i18n-php|lib/core/i18n.php]]; shared defaults: [[backend-resource-lib-core-config-php|config.php]]; who the "human" in a request is: [[backend-resource-lib-access-rights-php|lib/access/rights.php]].

pages.title: public/chat.php
pages.summary_html:
The assistant conversation page: messages, train of thought and token usage, read-only.

The conversation is taken from ai_chats, ai_messages and ai_jobs by project key and number; the messages are drawn by [[backend-resource-public-src-shell-chatpage-js|public/src/shell/chatpage.js]].
pages.body_html:
Purpose and limits

The whole conversation with the assistant as a separate page: questions, answers, the train of thought, token usage. Provides: the page chat.php?project=KEY&chat=N. The link comes from the "Link" button in the chat ([[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|public/src/panel/ai.js]], line 114) and from the conversation row in the account, "AI" section ([[backend-resource-public-account-php|public/account.php]], line 226). Does not: change anything, it only reads. The messages are drawn by the module [[backend-resource-public-src-shell-chatpage-js|public/src/shell/chatpage.js]], in the same look as in the chat.

Location

public/chat.php. Described from the source file as of 29 September 2026. The file has no functions: one page scenario runs from top to bottom, and the blocks are listed below with line numbers.

Where the conversation comes from

  • Lines 9–10: loads lib/boot.php and lib/web/page.php ([[backend-resource-lib-web-page-php|lib/web/page.php]]).
  • Lines 12–22: the project is taken with requireProject(false) by the project parameter (the project key), then the conversation row from [[backend-resource-table-ai_chats|ai_chats]] with the folder name from [[backend-resource-table-folders|folders]], by the chat parameter and only inside this project. If there is no such conversation, the error is agents.ai.no_chat ("Chat not found", code not_found).
  • Lines 17–22: any API error becomes a 404 response with plain text (text/plain, UTF-8) and the error message; the page is not drawn.
  • Line 25: the messages come from [[backend-resource-table-ai_messages|ai_messages]] (id, role, text, train of thought, time), in id order.
  • Lines 26–31: the usage of each answer comes from [[backend-resource-table-ai_jobs|ai_jobs]] by message id: model and tokens (in, out, cached). The comment in the code: messages and usage of each answer, as in ai.chat.get.
  • Lines 32–42: builds the $data array: title (the conversation title; without one, the word "chat" from the account.ai.chat_default dictionary key), project (project title or its key), key, folder (the conversation's folder or empty), at (start, 16 characters: date and time) and messages. Each message has role, body, think, at and tokens (usage if known, otherwise null).

What the page returns

  • Lines 44–46: the build version from editorVersion(); the header Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.
  • Lines 48–68: an HTML page with the dark theme (data-theme="dark") and the person's language; in <head> are the styles tokens.css, base.css, panel.css with a version and a small inline style block for an 860-pixel column, the embedded dictionary (langScript with the parts common and editor, see [[backend-resource-lib-core-i18n-php|lib/core/i18n.php]]) and the module map (importMap).
  • Lines 70–77: a heading with the conversation title; under it a line from the dictionary key editor.chatpage.meta (project, folder or "—", start time) and the link "Open the scheme" to index.php#p=KEY; an empty #chat-log block for the messages.
  • Line 78: the conversation data goes into window.GOBLIN_CHAT as JSON protected against closing tags (JSON_HEX_TAG, JSON_HEX_AMP).
  • Line 79: the module goblin/shell/chatpage.js is loaded; it reads this data and draws the messages (the shared look is in [[backend-resource-public-src-ui-rich-js|public/src/ui/rich.js]]).

Rights

The page reads and does not write, so it uses requireProject(false): write rights are not needed. Who is opening the page is decided by [[backend-resource-lib-access-rights-php|lib/access/rights.php]] (a token in the header, the sign-in cookie, or a guest). The only access condition in the file itself is that the project with the key from the link has a conversation with that number; another project or another number gives the same "not found" error. The page does not check separately whether the person is the owner.

Related topics

The assistant itself: [[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]]; conversations and usage in the account: [[accounts-user-ai|Chats and AI usage]]; the same reading through the API is the ai.chat.get operation in [[backend-resource-lib-ai-chat-php|lib/ai/chat.php]].

pages.title: Voice in chat — public/src/panel/voice.js
pages.summary_html:
Microphone and read-aloud in the assistant chat: live dictation into the field, reading the answer aloud.

The browser never knows the keys: the server gives a temporary token (voice.session) and ready sound (voice.speak). The chat screen is [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|panel/ai.js]].
pages.body_html:
public/src/panel/voice.js

Purpose and limits

Voice in the assistant chat: live dictation into the input field and reading the answer aloud. Provides: dictate(), stopDictation(), isDictating(), speak(), stopSpeaking(). Does not: store or know any keys — the server gives a temporary token for recognition (voice.session) and ready sound of the answer (voice.speak), see [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]]. Recognition goes straight between the browser and OpenAI over WebRTC; the microphone button, sending the question and showing errors are done by [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|panel/ai.js]].

What the module exports

Export and lineWhat it does
isDictating() (line 14)Whether dictation is running now: true while an unfinished recording live exists.
dictate(field) (line 17)Start dictation into field. Returns when the connection is ready and you can speak; words appear in the field as you speak, the final text after stopDictation().
stopDictation() (line 86)Finish dictation: the text in the field becomes final. Does nothing if there is no dictation.
speak(text) (line 91)Read the answer aloud. The voice does not read markup (asterisks, hashes, code) — it is cleaned out before sending.
stopSpeaking() (line 106)Stop the sounding answer and free the sound. If nothing is playing, returns at once.

Which API operations it calls

OperationWhere it is calledWhat it returns
voice.sessionline 19, api.post('voice.session', {})A temporary token: value (the secret), expires and url (address of the voice service).
voice.speakline 100, api.postAudio('voice.speak', { text })The sound of the answer (blob), which the module plays through Audio.

Both operations are for a person (role human) and are not written to the change log; they are described in the [[backend-api|API operations catalog]]. The client calls post and postAudio live in [[backend-resource-public-src-api-client-js|public/src/api/client.js]]. If the server returns JSON with an error instead of sound, postAudio throws, and the calling screen catches it.

How dictation goes

  1. Any sounding answer is stopped (stopSpeaking(), line 18): the microphone must not hear the assistant.
  2. The module asks for the token (voice.session, line 19) and for the microphone from the browser (getUserMedia({ audio: true }), line 20).
  3. An RTCPeerConnection is created, the microphone tracks are added to it, and the event channel oai-events is opened (lines 21–23).
  4. The field caret is remembered: the text before and after it stays in place, what you say goes between them; a space is put between old and new text when needed (lines 26–29).
  5. The SDP offer goes to OpenAI: POST <token url>/realtime/calls with the header Authorization: Bearer <value> and type application/sdp; the answer becomes the remote description (lines 53–60). A bad response turns into an error with the first 200 characters of its text or "HTTP code".
  6. It waits for the event channel to open — no longer than 10 seconds (lines 62–66): OpenAI does not hear what was said before that.
  7. If steps 5–6 fail, the microphone and connection are closed and the error goes to the caller (lines 67–71). On success live gets an object with a stop() method (line 73).

Recognition events

Channel event (line)What the module does
conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta (40)Appends a piece of text to the phrase with this item_id and redraws the field.
conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed (43)Replaces the phrase with the final text (transcript), redraws the field and wakes the wait in stop().
error (47)Writes a warning to the console (console.warn); does not interrupt dictation.

Phrases are kept in a Map by item_id; the function paint() (line 31) joins them with spaces, collapses repeated spaces, sets before + space + spoken + after and scrolls the field down. Debugging: if GOBLIN_VOICE_DEBUG is set in the console, every channel event is printed to the console (line 39).

Stopping

The stop() method (line 74) first, if the channel is open, sends input_audio_buffer.commit — it hands over the rest of the sound — then waits for the final completed event, but no longer than 4 seconds (line 77). After that the microphone tracks stop, the connection closes and live is cleared. Dictation does not end by itself: when issuing the token the server turns off splitting into phrases (in [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]]), so recording goes on until the person presses "stop".

How the answer is read aloud

  1. The previous sound is stopped.
  2. Triple-quote code blocks, the characters * _ ` # > | and list markers at line starts are removed from the text, and spaces are collapsed (lines 93–98). If no text is left, it leaves without sound (line 99).
  3. The clean text goes to voice.speak; the received sound is played through new Audio(URL.createObjectURL(...)) (lines 100–103). When it ends, the sound link is freed (revokeObjectURL) and player is cleared.

The server reads at most 4000 characters of text and needs a voice key to be set; without a key the operation returns the error "No voice key…" — where the key is set, see [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]].

Who calls it

The only consumer is [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|public/src/panel/ai.js]] (import on line 14): the microphone button #ai-mic in the assistant window. The first press calls dictate(input): the button is dimmed while connecting and red when you can speak. The second press calls stopDictation(): the text stays in the field, and only "Ask" (or Enter) sends the question. The speaker is a separate button #ai-read (the browser remembers the choice, goblin-ai-read); when the answer is ready (states done, applied, proposal) and the speaker is on, ai.js calls speak() with the text of the last assistant message. A microphone refusal shows a message about the browser permission, other errors show "Voice did not start", a read-aloud error shows "Could not read the answer aloud". The chat as a whole — [[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]].

Related topics

The server half — [[backend-resource-lib-ai-voice-php|lib/ai/voice.php]]; keys and address of the voice service — [[backend-resource-lib-ai-access-php|lib/ai/access.php]]; the chat screen — [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|panel/ai.js]].

pages.title: Conversation page — public/src/shell/chatpage.js
pages.summary_html:
Draws the conversation with the assistant on the chat.php page, in the same look as in the chat.

The module does not call the server: the page gets the conversation at once in window.GOBLIN_CHAT. The page is [[backend-resource-public-chat-php|public/chat.php]].
pages.body_html:
public/src/shell/chatpage.js

Purpose and limits

The conversation page (public/chat.php): messages are drawn in the same look as in the assistant chat. Provides: nothing — the module exports nothing, and on load it draws window.GOBLIN_CHAT into the #chat-log element. Does not: call the server — the page gets the whole conversation at once, ready, from PHP ([[backend-resource-public-chat-php|public/chat.php]]). Changes nothing: display only.

How the file works

The file has no functions, only top-level code (21 lines). It runs once, when the page loads the module with import 'goblin/shell/chatpage.js'.

LinesWhat it does
5–6Imports chatLine from [[backend-resource-public-src-ui-rich-js|public/src/ui/rich.js]] and t from [[backend-resource-public-src-core-i18n-js|public/src/core/i18n.js]].
8Takes globalThis.GOBLIN_CHAT; if it is missing — an empty conversation { messages: [] }.
9Finds the #chat-log container.
11–20For each message builds a chat line and adds it to the container (details below).
21If there are no messages — writes "The conversation has no messages yet." into the container (key editor.chatpage.empty).

How a message is drawn

  • A message is mine when the role is user (line 12): the label is "you" (editor.ai.you); for the rest it is "AI" (editor.ai.ai).
  • The line is built by chatLine(label, text, { mine, tokens, think }) (lines 13–14): assistant answers are shown as markup, own messages as plain text; the reasoning (think) is a collapsed block, the token spending (tokens) is a small line under the message. All this is done by chatLine; this module has no markup of its own.
  • Message time: the at field goes into <small class="chat-at">, and the element is added to the end of the line (lines 15–18); the chat-at style is in chat.php itself.

What arrives in GOBLIN_CHAT

chat.php builds the object and puts it into the page with a separate script. The module reads only messages from it; each message has these fields:

FieldMeaning
roleuser — the person's question; otherwise — the assistant's answer.
bodyMessage text.
thinkThe assistant's reasoning; empty — the block is not drawn.
atMessage time, down to minutes.
tokensSpending on the answer: in, out, cached, model; null — the spending line is not drawn.

The other fields (title, project, key, folder, the conversation at) are used by chat.php itself for the page heading and caption.

Where the page link comes from

The address chat.php?project=KEY&chat=N is given by the link icon in the assistant chat header ("Copy a link to the conversation", [[backend-resource-public-src-panel-ai-js|panel/ai.js]]): the link is copied and opened at once. The same address is in the conversation row of the personal account (section "AI"). More about the chat — [[frontend-right-assistant|AI assistant]].
